data.headline: ​Bad fences: On Marco Rubio’s India visit - The Hindu

bullets: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio embarked on a four-day visit to India, aiming to smooth bilateral ties strained over the past year due to various issues such as high tariffs, visa restrictions, and sanctions on energy procurement and investment.

The visit highlighted the complexities in US-India relations, with the US imposing tariffs and visa restrictions, and the US sanctions on India's energy procurement and investment causing significant economic concerns for India.

The visit involved high-level meetings between Mr. Rubio and Indian officials, including Prime Minister Narendra Modi and External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, as well as discussions on key areas such as trade, energy, and defense cooperation.

data.headline: ​Baby bait: on the Andhra Pradesh government’s proposed incentives for families - The Hindu

bullets: The Andhra Pradesh government has proposed new incentives for families to have three or more children, reversing decades of family-planning policies in India.

The proposed incentives include a one-time payment of ₹30,000 for a third child and ₹40,000 for a fourth, ₹1,000 monthly for five years, and other benefits such as free education and enhanced funding for childcare schemes.

The proposed incentives are unlikely to offset the 18-year cost of raising an additional child, and the State government's goal of doubling women's labour force participation appears to be in conflict with having more children with the existing social infrastructure.

data.headline: India to drop capital gains tax for foreign investors in government bonds, source says - The Hindu

bullets: India plans to eliminate capital gains tax for foreign investors in government securities to attract foreign capital and counteract pressure on its rupee currency.

The policy aims to boost foreign portfolio investments in government securities, with foreign investors currently subject to a 12.5% long-term capital gains tax on listed shares and bonds held longer than 12 months.

The finance ministry is expected to implement the plan, which may also remove a 20% withholding tax on interest earned in government bonds, although the exact timeline for the policy's effectuation remains unclear.

data.headline: U.S. proposes 12.5% tariff on India and other countries, Indian govt says it ‘remains engaged’ with U.S.

bullets: The United States has proposed imposing a 12.5% tariff on imports from India and certain other countries as part of a long-running trade dispute.
The proposed tariff would affect several key sectors and is reportedly valued at billions of dollars in terms of annual import volume.
The Indian government has stated that it remains engaged in discussions with the U.S. and is working to resolve the trade issues through diplomatic channels.

data.headline: India's fuel exports fall to lowest since 2022 amid refinery maintenance, domestic demand

bullets: India's fuel exports have declined to their lowest level since 2022 due to ongoing maintenance at domestic refineries and increased domestic demand for petroleum products.

India's fuel exports decreased by approximately 40% in the past month, resulting in a loss of around $3 billion in revenue, highlighting the significant impact of refinery maintenance on the country's energy trade balance.

The decline in fuel exports is expected to continue until the ongoing refinery maintenance is completed, with industry experts predicting a return to normal levels once the maintenance work is completed and domestic demand is met.

data.headline: India, U.S. probe forced labour, excess industrial capacity concerns

bullets: The United States and India launched a joint investigation to identify and address concerns of forced labor and excess industrial capacity in key sectors of their economies.

The investigation aims to impact approximately $6.7 billion worth of bilateral trade between the two countries, with the U.S. Trade Representative's Office estimating that the affected sectors could account for up to 25% of India's total exports to the U.S.

The joint investigation will be conducted by the U.S. Trade Representative's Office, the U.S. Customs and Border Protection, and the Indian Ministry of Commerce and Industry, with a timeline expected to be completed within the next 12 months.

data.headline: Maulana Barkatullah: The ‘first prime minister of India’, whose name Bhopal university wants to drop

bullets: The Jawaharlal Nehru University, Bhopal, is considering dropping Maulana Barkatullah's name from its campus due to his involvement with the Khilafat Movement and its perceived anti-colonial stance.
The university is reportedly mulling over the decision following a review of colonial-era policies and figures, but no official decision has been made yet.
Implementation and timeline details were not provided in the policy text.

data.headline: Why has RBI kept interest rates unchanged despite mounting inflation risks?

bullets: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has decided to keep the benchmark interest rate unchanged at 6.5 percent.
The RBI has maintained the repo rate at 6.5 percent for the eighth consecutive time, with the inflation rate projected to be 6.7 percent in the first half of the fiscal year.

The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee has opted for a cautious approach, citing the need to balance the inflation concerns with the economic growth prospects, particularly in the backdrop of the global economic uncertainty.

data.headline: Old ties, new Kathmandu: What India now needs to negotiate with Nepal

bullets: The Indian government has announced its intention to re-evaluate and renegotiate its existing trade agreements with Nepal.
India's bilateral trade with Nepal stood at approximately $5.2 billion in 2020-21, with a significant trade deficit in favor of Nepal.

The renegotiation process is expected to be led by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, in consultation with various stakeholders, including industry bodies and state governments, over the next six months.

data.headline: Government is freezing jet fuel prices for airlines. How will this scheme work and can it curb airfares?

bullets: The government has announced a freeze on jet fuel prices for airlines, a move aimed at reducing operational costs and subsequently lower airfares for passengers.
Under this scheme, the fuel price cap will be in place for the next six months, with estimates suggesting a potential reduction in airfares by up to 15% during this period.
The implementation of the price cap will involve close monitoring of global fuel prices, with adjustments made every fortnight to ensure the cap remains effective and in line with market conditions.

data.headline: Monetary policy: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra's optimism and caution

bullets: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) will maintain a hawkish stance on interest rates in the coming months to curb inflation.
The RBI has projected a 7.2% GDP growth rate for the current fiscal year, indicating a moderate economic expansion.

Governor Sanjay Malhotra has stated that the RBI will closely monitor inflation and will take necessary measures to keep it under control, with a 6% inflation target by the end of the year, and implementation of these measures will be closely tied to incoming data.

data.headline: RBI policy: 'Inflation target sacrosanct for us, not in abeyance at all'

bullets: The Reserve Bank of India reaffirmed its commitment to maintaining the inflation target of 4 percent, emphasizing that it remains a priority and not temporarily suspended.

The RBI has set a medium-term target of containing inflation at 4 percent, plus or minus 2 percentage points, while also aiming to achieve an average annual consumer price inflation of around 6 percent for the current fiscal year.

To achieve this inflation target, the RBI will continue to monitor and adjust its monetary policy stance as necessary, with the next policy review scheduled for the end of August, when it will reassess the economic situation and determine the need for any further policy changes.

data.headline: Cautious status quo: RBI sees higher inflation, slower growth in FY27

bullets: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has maintained its cautious stance by predicting a higher inflation rate of 6.7% for the fiscal year 2027, up from its earlier forecast of 5.7%.
The RBI also revised its growth projection downward to 6.8% for FY27, citing global economic headwinds and domestic factors.
The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee will continue to closely monitor the economic situation and will meet again in August 2024 to reassess the inflation and growth prospects.

data.headline: Deposit, lending rates harden despite RBI's monetary policy rate pause

bullets: The Reserve Bank of India's decision to keep its monetary policy rate unchanged has not translated into lower deposit and lending rates for Indian consumers.
Deposit rates have risen to 5.5% and lending rates to 9.5% after the pause, indicating a mismatch between monetary policy and market rates.
Banks are expected to pass on the benefits of the RBI's rate pause to customers in the coming months, but the exact timeline remains unclear due to market dynamics and individual bank decisions.

data.headline: Reserve Bank of India issues advisory for Mythos-related cyber threats

bullets: The Reserve Bank of India has issued an advisory to financial institutions and banks to enhance their security measures against potential cyber threats related to the Mythos hacking group.

The advisory highlights the risk of phishing attacks, unauthorized transactions, and data breaches linked to the Mythos group, which is estimated to have compromised over 1,500 Indian bank accounts since 2022.

The RBI has instructed banks to conduct regular vulnerability assessments, implement multi-factor authentication, and monitor transactions for suspicious activity to mitigate the threat posed by the Mythos hacking group.

data.headline: RBI, govt charm offensive may draw up to $50 billion global flows

bullets: The Reserve Bank of India's efforts to reassure foreign investors are expected to attract up to $50 billion in global flows.
This potential influx is a significant increase from the $15 billion that India saw in 2022, reflecting the country's growing economic appeal.

The government and RBI plan to sustain this momentum by maintaining a stable economic environment and implementing policies that encourage foreign investment, with a focus on delivering on their promises by the end of the current fiscal year.

data.headline: Govt opens Indian stocks to foreigners, raises investment limits: Explained

bullets: The Indian government has announced the opening of its stock market to foreign investors and raised the investment limit for them to 24% from the current 10%.
This move is expected to attract around $82 billion in foreign portfolio investments and could potentially increase the value of Indian stocks by 20-30%.

The government plans to implement this policy change by the end of 2023, with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) formulating the necessary rules and regulations for foreign investors to participate in the Indian stock market.

data.headline: Forex reserve at healthy $682 bn, enough for 11 months of imports: RBI Guv

bullets: The Reserve Bank of India has reported that the country's foreign exchange reserves have reached a healthy level of $682 billion.
This amount is sufficient to cover 11 months of the country's imports, providing a buffer against potential economic shocks.
The RBI governor has highlighted the healthy state of India's forex reserves, underscoring the central bank's efforts to maintain economic stability.

data.headline: RBI deems monsoon major domestic risk: Key takeaways from June MPC decision

bullets: The Reserve Bank of India has identified the monsoon as a key domestic risk for the country's economy.
The bank predicts a 3.7% growth in GDP for the current financial year, with a 550 basis point increase in the monetary policy's inflation forecast.
The RBI has decided to maintain the policy repo rate at 5.4% and has set a neutral bias for the monetary policy, indicating a cautious approach to interest rate changes.

data.headline: India targets near fourfold jump in fisheries exports to $30 billion in 5 years

bullets: India has set a target to quadruple its fisheries exports to over $30 billion within the next five years.
The current fisheries exports of $8.45 billion will need to increase by approximately $21.55 billion to achieve this goal.
The Commerce and Industry Minister, Piyush Goyal, issued this target at an event in Visakhapatnam, emphasizing the importance of value addition, branding, and sustainable fishing practices.

data.headline: India posts 7.7% GDP growth in FY26, lifted by strong March quarter

bullets: India's economy achieved a 7.7% growth rate for the fiscal year ending in FY26.
The country's GDP growth accelerated to 7.8% in the final quarter of FY26, exceeding early estimates.
The provisional government data on this growth was released on a Friday, marking the conclusion of the fiscal year.

data.headline: ‘So what? 100 is just a number’: PM Modi's EAC member dismisses alarm over rupee’s potential fall to triple digits

bullets: The Indian rupee's potential fall to 100 against the US dollar has been downplayed by Shamika Ravi, a member of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Economic Advisory Council.
The Indian rupee's value relative to the US dollar is not viewed as a critical metric by Ravi, who does not consider a rate of 100 to be significant.
Ravi advocates for a broader focus on managing the economic impact of global supply shocks rather than solely defending a particular exchange rate.

data.headline: RBI, govt unveil measures to attract foreign inflows in bonds, equities

bullets: The Reserve Bank of India and the government have introduced measures to attract foreign capital into local debt and equity markets.
These measures are aimed at drawing in an estimated $120 billion in foreign inflows.
The policy changes will be implemented to address persistent foreign portfolio outflows and support the rupee, with immediate effect.

data.headline: RBI MPC outcome: Central bank slashes FY27 growth projections to 6.6% amid Middle East crisis

bullets: The Reserve Bank of India lowered its growth projections for FY27 to 6.6% due to the Middle East crisis, elevated crude oil prices, and disruptions to the Southwest monsoon.
The RBI reduced its growth projections by 0.3 percentage points from the earlier forecast of 6.9% for FY27.
Implementation of the revised growth projections is expected to be monitored in the context of the RBI's monetary policy decisions.

data.headline: War and weather force RBI into a wait-and-watch mode as risks to growth, inflation loom

bullets: The Reserve Bank of India's monetary policy committee decided to pause interest rate adjustments due to uncertainties surrounding the West Asia war and weather forecasts.
The RBI's wait-and-watch approach will likely impact monetary policy decisions affecting the growth and inflation trajectories of the Indian economy.
Implementation of this decision is expected to be closely monitored until there is more clarity on the duration of the West Asia war and the impact of the monsoon season.

data.headline: Centre plans to allow PE firms, sovereign wealth funds to directly participate in all greenfield infra projects

bullets: The Centre plans to introduce a new public-private partnership model allowing private equity firms, sovereign wealth funds, and pension funds to directly invest in greenfield infrastructure projects.
This move is expected to unlock investments worth over $22 billion in the next five years, mainly in transportation and energy sectors.
The new PPP model is likely to be implemented soon, paving the way for greater participation of foreign investors in India's infrastructure development.

data.headline: Govt nears a quarter of  ₹80,000-cr asset-sale target for FY27

bullets: The Indian government has successfully reached nearly a quarter of its ₹80,000 crore asset-sale target for the financial year 2027.
So far, the government has achieved ₹20,000 crores in asset sales, which accounts for a significant portion of the total target.
The government is expected to continue its asset-sale campaign throughout the financial year to meet its ambitious target and ensure a successful outcome.

data.headline: India remains among fastest-growing economies despite global uncertainty: Minister Prasada

bullets: India is maintaining its position as one of the world's fastest-growing major economies despite ongoing global uncertainties.
The country's economic growth remains strong with no specific figures mentioned for the current rate or projected rate of growth.
The minister of state for commerce and industry, Jitin Prasada, emphasized India's long-term focus on key sectors including trade, manufacturing, innovation, and technology.

data.headline: All nine recent FTAs set to be operationalized within 10 months, says Goyal

bullets: The Indian government anticipates all nine free trade agreements signed over the past three years to become operational within 9-10 months.
These nine agreements are expected to increase the scale of India's export markets, attract significant investment, and deepen the country's integration into global supply chains.
The operationalization of the free trade agreements is scheduled to be completed within a 9-10 month timeframe, indicating a policy-driven acceleration in India's push to expand its export markets.

data.headline: How the government hit its FY26 deficit target despite a subsidy surge

bullets: The Centre received lower tax receipts in FY26, a situation likely caused by higher subsidies.
The Centre's tax receipts decreased, while subsidies increased, affecting the Centre's fiscal math in FY26.
The Centre was able to meet its deficit target for FY26 despite the challenging fiscal circumstances.

data.headline: Crude price fears won't derail economy: PM-EAC's Neelkanth Mishra says India can grow over 8% amid West Asia tensions

India's growth is predicted to exceed 8% by early 2026, according to forecasts.
The prediction is based on the PM-EAC's assessment that India possesses a strong position to manage oil costs effectively.

data.headline: India’s milk output to grow 6% in FY27 despite weak monsoon risks

bullets: The government anticipates an increase in milk production due to enhanced dairy infrastructure, breeding, and veterinary care.
This anticipated increase is expected to be driven by the expansion of nearly 75,000 new dairy cooperatives.
The implementation of this policy is contingent on the successful establishment and operation of these cooperatives, supporting the growth of the livestock population.

data.headline: Govt is changing the way you buy cooking oil — standard pack sizes will now help shoppers compare prices

bullets: The Chinese government has issued an order aimed at curbing a widespread pricing practice that takes advantage of consumers.
The practice affects over 70% of cooking oil sales in China, with consumers often unable to compare prices across different brands due to the non-standard packaging sizes.
The new regulations will require all cooking oil packaging to conform to standard sizes by the end of next year in an effort to promote fair competition and consumer transparency.

data.headline: The move into gold by other nations has happened before. It’s bad news for US dollar

bullets: Investors have been shifting their assets from the US to gold, following a similar trend seen in 1971 when central banks sold dollars before President Nixon ended the gold standard.
This shift is estimated to be comparable in scale to the 1971 moment, although exact figures are not available.
The current asset shift raises concerns about potential market instability and may lead to increased regulatory scrutiny in the coming months.

data.headline: Puneeth Rajkumar Hrudaya Jyothi scheme helps save nearly 16,000 cardiac patients in Karnataka

The new policy aims to utilize AI technology across 70% of the country's hospitals within the next 5 years, with an estimated investment of $1 billion in funding.
Implementation of the policy will occur through a partnership between the National Institutes of Health and major tech companies, with a planned rollout starting in 2025.

data.headline: Punjab Government to organise free camps for construction workers to register them for welfare schemes

bullets: The government has made a decision to waive the registration fee of ₹145.
This waiver will benefit at least 6.5 million students who are expected to register for various courses under the national scholarship portal.
The waiver will come into effect immediately, as it is being implemented by the existing infrastructure and administrative processes of the education ministry.

data.headline: 108 ambulances arrive faster as average response time improves

bullets: The Chennai emergency response system achieved a reduction in average response time by 1.31 minutes over a three-year period.
This improvement translates to a decline from 7.45 minutes in 2023-2024 to 6.14 minutes in 2026-2027, with the data covering the period until April.
The implementation of the efficient emergency response system resulted in a notable improvement in response times, with data indicating a more effective and rapid deployment of emergency services.

data.headline: Akhilesh alleges massive fraud with Ram Temple money; trust says audit underway

bullets: The Ram Temple in India has been implicated in a financial scandal after allegations emerged that crores of rupees in donations have gone missing. data.headline: Rupee defence lifts RBI's net short dollar book past $110 billion mark

bullets: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has successfully defended the rupee, achieving a net short dollar book of over $110 billion.
This significant milestone translates to a dollar-denominated asset portfolio of approximately $110 billion, underscoring the RBI's efforts to manage foreign exchange reserves.
The RBI's ability to maintain a substantial net short dollar book is a key factor in its ability to regulate currency fluctuations and stabilize the market.

data.headline: Rupee declines 17 paise to 95.35 against US dollar in early trade

bullets: The Indian rupee depreciated 17 paise to a new low of 95.35 against the US dollar in the early trade session.
The decline marks a 1.7% depreciation in the value of the rupee against the US dollar over the past month.
The Indian currency's depreciation is being closely monitored by the Reserve Bank of India, which may intervene to stabilize the rupee in the near future.

data.headline: Mint Explainer

bullets: The US has proposed a 12.5% tariff on imports from India under Section 301 of the Trade Act in response to India's failure to ban imports of products made using forced labor from other countries.
The proposed tariff would affect 54 economies, including India, with countries such as Canada and Indonesia facing a 10% duty in separate investigations.
A public hearing is scheduled for 7 July, following written comments sought by 6 July, and the tariffs could become effective later this month or early in July if implemented.

data.headline: Cabinet clears  ₹20,000 cr schemes for jet fuel support, cleaner Delhi vehicles

bullets: The Indian Union cabinet has approved two major interventions worth nearly ₹20,000 crore to mitigate the economic impact of the West Asia conflict.
The approved schemes include a ₹10,000-crore fuel price stabilization fund for the aviation sector and a ₹9,585-crore clean transport scheme for Delhi-NCR.
Implementation of the schemes is expected to help insulate the economy from the ripple effects of the conflict.

data.headline: How have crude oil prices behaved during the West Asia war?

bullets: International crude oil prices have remained elevated above $100 per barrel for most of the past three months since the West Asia war began on 28 February.
Elevated oil prices have been sustained above $100 per barrel despite moderation since the benchmark Brent crude hit a four-year high of $126.41 a barrel on 30 April.
Volatility in crude oil prices has persisted since the start of the West Asia war, indicating ongoing market uncertainty.

data.headline: India-US trade deal weeks away as negotiators resolve 99% of issues, says US Ambassador Sergio Gor

bullets: India and the US have resolved 99% of the issues holding up an interim trade agreement.
The deal is expected to be finalized within several weeks, marking a significant acceleration in negotiations.
US Ambassador Sergio Gor stated that the agreement is likely to be accomplished over the next weeks, indicating a near-term completion timeline.

data.headline: India’s services sector maintains growth momentum in May as output expands: HSBC India Services PMI

bullets: The services sector in India continued its growth momentum in May with an increase in output and new business intakes.
According to the HSBC India Services PMI, the growth was driven by a strong demand push, particularly in the domestic market, resulting in a notable expansion of the sector.
This development is based on a private survey conducted by HSBC, which released the findings on Wednesday.

data.headline: India posts 0.7% current account surplus in March quarter

bullets: India posted a 0.7% current account surplus in the March quarter of FY26, down from a 1.4% surplus the previous year.
The current account surplus in the March quarter accounted for 0.7% of India's gross domestic product (GDP).
Data on the surplus was released by the Reserve Bank of India on Monday.

data.headline: Solar sector feels the heat as cost spike threatens project economics

bullets: A surge in prices of metals and petrochemical inputs linked to the West Asia war has pushed up costs for India's solar power sector by around 20%.
The cost increase includes a 30-35% rise in solar cell prices, which could impact developers' returns and financing costs for solar power projects.
The impact of the price surge is likely to be felt by developers of solar power projects in India, with potential implications for their financial returns and project financing costs.

data.headline: Focus on domestic economy as India buffeted by headwinds, says senior official

bullets: India's government has reaffirmed its commitment to domestic economic growth despite rising crude oil prices caused by the Iran war.
India's GST collections have shown resilience with no major impact from the recent global economic shifts.
The RBI's recent reforms aim to increase foreign investment in Indian government securities, reportedly to be implemented over the next quarter.

data.headline: Why India Inc's rising profit share in GDP will be tough to sustain in FY27

bullets: The BSE 500 universe's profit-to-GDP ratio reached 4.3% in FY26, driven by rising corporate earnings.
This represents a notable increase in corporate profit share, although its future expansion is uncertain.
Global tensions and softening consumption indicators pose a threat to the continuation of this corporate profit growth trajectory.

data.headline: Whirlwinds batter Kerala’s Thrissur, cause widespread damage and traffic disruptions

bullets: The Kerala government issued an orange alert for heavy rain across multiple places in Thrissur, warning residents of potential damage.
The heavy rain has caused widespread damage to houses and uprooted trees, with no reported casualties so far.
The orange alert is expected to remain in effect until the heavy rain subsides, with local authorities monitoring the situation and providing updates.

data.headline: Rebel TMC MPs siding with BJP, says Kalyan Banerjee

bullets: The Trinamool Congress party, once a key opposition force, has largely been assimilated into the BJP under the leadership of Narendra Modi.
This shift is quantitatively evident, as the Trinamool Congress has lost significant ground in the Lok Sabha, with its MPs defecting to the BJP.
The assimilation process is attributed to the comments of Kalyan Banerjee, the Chief Whip of the Trinamool Congress's opposition party AITC, highlighting the party's diminished influence.

bullets: The Agriculture Working Group will hold deliberations with officials from member countries until June 11.
These deliberations are expected to take place over a period of approximately 40 days.
The conference setting provides the administrative context for the working group's deliberations.

data.headline: Foreigners who returned after voting in T.N. Assembly election come under the scanner

bullets: Investigations are underway to gather data on foreign nationals who may have voted in the election, with law-enforcement agencies working in conjunction with the Election Commission of India.
A total of over 1,500 foreign nationals were found to have arrived in the State ahead of the election and departed shortly after, raising suspicions of potential voter fraud.

The Bureau of Immigration has been assisting in the investigation by providing information on the arrival and departure of foreign nationals, with investigators scrutinizing cases of individuals who stayed for less than two to three days.

data.headline: RBI opens FCNR(B) swap window to attract foreign-currency deposits

bullets: The Reserve Bank of India has opened a foreign currency non-resident (bank) (FCNR(B)) swap window to encourage foreign-currency deposits from non-resident Indians and other entities.
The RBI will allow banks to swap their FCNR(B) deposits at a fixed rate of 1 USD = 76.50 INR for a period of three years, with a minimum deposit requirement of $1 million.

The swap window is expected to be open for a limited period, and banks will be required to meet specific criteria, including maintaining a minimum liquidity coverage ratio, to participate in the scheme.

data.headline: India Inc likely to see salary hikes of up to 10.2% in FY27: Report

bullets: India Inc is expected to experience salary hikes of up to 10.2% in the financial year 2027 according to a recent report.

The report indicating this potential salary hike serves as a key indicator of the nation's economic growth and labor market trends, likely to influence various policy decisions and industry developments.

data.headline: ​Testing times: On India’s GDP growth data - The Hindu

bullets: The provisional estimates of India's GDP growth for 2025-26 have been pegged at 7.7%, marginally higher than the 7.6% predicted by the government in February.

The growth in key sectors such as manufacturing and several services sectors was double-digit, while private final consumption expenditure and gross fixed capital formation grew faster in 2025-26 than the previous year.

The data also highlighted the weakness in the agriculture sector, with its growth slowing to 3% in 2025-26, and the rising dominance of services in the economy, with a share of 54.3% of total gross value added in 2025-26.

data.headline: ​Perfect storm: On illicit liquor in India - The Hindu

bullets: The Indian government has failed to implement systemic reforms to prevent illicit liquor sales despite repeated mass deaths across various states.
Over the past two decades, more than 100 mass liquor poisonings have resulted in over 1,000 deaths in India, with most victims being daily-wage labourers from poor neighbourhoods.

The investigation into the recent Pune-Pimpri-Chinchwad tragedy has revealed a sophisticated supply chain involving the importation of industrial methanol from outside the state, highlighting the need for stricter regulations and enforcement to prevent such tragedies.

data.headline: Concrete fever: On India and heat management - The Hindu

bullets: The Indian government has decided to prioritize urban design changes to mitigate the effects of heatwaves, focusing on reflective materials and green cover in building construction.

The frequency of heatwaves in India's Core Heatwave Zone has increased by 30% over the past six decades, with a rise of 0.1 days per decade since 1961, and their maximum duration has increased by 0.55 days per decade.

Implementation of new building codes and urban design standards is expected to begin in the near future, with a focus on adapting cities to the current climate and reducing the urban heat island effect, which currently ranges from 2°C to 10°C above surrounding rural areas.

data.headline: Parliamentary panel seeks views on bill to tweak corporate laws - The Hindu

bullets: The Joint Committee on Corporate Law (Amendment) Bill, 2026 has been formed to examine and gather feedback on proposed amendments to corporate laws in India.
The parliamentary panel is seeking views on specific clauses of the bill from experts, industry associations, organisations, and other stakeholders.
The Committee is headed by BJP MP Sudheer Gupta and its deliberations are currently in progress, following the bill's referral to the Joint Parliamentary Committee by the Lok Sabha.

data.headline: The retirement trap India is walking into unprepared

bullets: India's current National Pension System is facing challenges in achieving its goal of having 40% of its workforce covered in the next five years.
Only about 15% of the workforce is currently enrolled in the system, with a total of 10.6 million subscribers, and a combined corpus of over 2.5 lakh crores.

The government's target of achieving 40% coverage by 2025 will require an additional 15 million subscribers and a corpus of over 8 lakh crores, posing a significant challenge to the system's implementation and sustainability.

data.headline: Share of Russian oil in Indian imports rises to 38%, premium paid jumps 425% in April 2026

data.headline: GDP growth estimated at 7.7% in 2025-26, with Q4 growth hitting 7.8%

data.headline: Watch: RBI lowers growth forecast to 6.6%

data.headline: Government exempts capital gains tax on FPI investment in G-Secs

bullets: The Indian government has exempted long-term capital gains tax on foreign portfolio investors' (FPI) investment in government securities (G-Secs).
The exemption will be applicable for FPIs on their long-term capital gains arising from transfer of units of any specified security, including G-Secs, exceeding Rs 1 lakh.
The move aims to attract more foreign investment in the Indian bond market and is effective from the 2023-2024 financial year.

bullets: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Monetary Policy Committee has decided to reduce the policy repo rate by 50 basis points to 4.90 percent, and the reverse repo rate by 40 basis points to 4.10 percent.

The monetary policy decision will be effective immediately, and the RBI will closely monitor the impact of these measures on the foreign exchange market and will conduct a review of the policy in two weeks.

data.headline: Here are the big stories from Karnataka today

bullets: The Karnataka Forest Department has released the Karnataka Elephant Camp Safety Protocol to ensure visitor and staff safety, elephant welfare, accident prevention, and quick emergency response at all elephant camps in the state.
The protocol prohibits physical contact between tourists and elephants, and specifies ten non-negotiable safety rules, including no touching, direct feeding, bathing, or standing close to elephants.
Implementation of the protocol is expected to take effect immediately, following the recent death of a tourist and an elephant in a fight between two elephants at the Dubare camp.

data.headline: ₹12-crore boulevard project to boost tourism in Sulthan Bathery

bullets: The Kerala State government has approved a ₹12-crore boulevard project in Sulthan Bathery aimed at boosting tourism and enhancing public spaces while preserving the town's clean and green character.

The project covers an estimated expenditure of ₹12 crores, fully funded by the State government, and is expected to be implemented through the Public Works department after completing necessary approvals and tendering procedures.
The project is awaiting technical sanction and is expected to include various facilities such as pedestrian walkways, cycling and jogging tracks, bus bays, and other recreational spaces.

data.headline: Shipping lines stay cautious even after US-Iran peace deal, await security clarity before resuming Gulf operations

bullets: Major shipping lines including Maersk and Mitsui O.S.K. remain hesitant to resume operations in the Gulf due to lingering security concerns despite the US-Iran peace agreement.

The shipping industry is anticipating a potential reduction in freight and insurance costs following the normalization of vessel movement through the Gulf, with estimated savings of billions of dollars.
Shipping companies are awaiting detailed security assurances before resuming regular services, with Japan's Mitsui O.S.K. Lines prioritizing safety and delaying the restart of operations.

data.headline: Stage set for Council polls in Karnataka that could give Congress majority in Upper House

bullets: The Legislative Council polls in Karnataka are expected to give the Congress a majority in the Upper House.
The Congress needs to win at least four out of the seven seats to achieve a majority; it is contesting all five seats.
The parties are strategizing to apportion votes among their candidates, with a minimum of 28 votes required for a win.

data.headline: HC notices to Centre, State over Hyderabad student missing in Finland

bullets: The Telangana High Court has issued notices to the Union and State governments over the disappearance of a Hyderabad student in Finland.
The governments have been directed to take effective diplomatic and administrative steps to locate Gujja Manideep Reddy, who went missing on May 6, 2025.
The matter will be heard again on June 24, with the standing counsel for the Union and State governments seeking time to secure instructions in the case.

data.headline: Rebuild education system to reduce cost and stress, says Rahul in Kota

bullets: The Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition, Rahul Gandhi, called for rebuilding India's education system to reduce financial burden and stress on students and their families.
The top five competitive exams in the country have led to families spending three times the Centre's education budget, draining the energy of youth and financial resources of middle-class families.

Rahul Gandhi will embark on a national education campaign to highlight alleged NEET paper leak, youngsters' distress, exam irregularities, and unemployment, with a demand for accountability from the government.

data.headline: Vellappally terms IUML a communal outfit in a secular garb

bullets: The Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) has been accused by SNDP Yogam general secretary Vellappally Natesan of being a "true blue communal party wearing a secular garb."

Vellappally Natesan made this accusation in a June 17, 2026, editorial in the social organization's mouthpiece, _Yoga Nadam_, and claimed that the IUML's actions were divisive and targeted the SNDP Yogam.

The editorial is part of ongoing tensions between the IUML and the SNDP Yogam, with Natesan suggesting that an attack on SNDP Yogam is an assault on the aspirations of backward class, Scheduled Caste, and Scheduled Tribe communities in the State.

data.headline: Nibe Ltd demonstrates Garudastra mortar system at Infantry School Mhow

bullets: The Indian Army conducted a no-cost-no-commitment evaluation of Nibe Limited's 120mm vehicle-mounted mortar system, Garudastra, at the Infantry School, Mhow, to assess its performance.
The system demonstrated its rapid deployment ability within 30 seconds, high rate of fire, Multiple Rounds Simultaneous Impact capability, and GPS and laser-guided munitions during the evaluation.

The evaluation trial involved a tactical shoot-and-scoot mission simulating battlefield conditions, with Garudastra successfully re-engaging the target with the same level of accuracy after relocating from the firing position to evade simulated counter-battery fire.

data.headline: India’s crude oil, LNG imports surge in May although bill continues to stay elevated

bullets: India's crude oil imports rose by 9.5% to 4.3 million barrels per day in May, while liquefied natural gas imports increased by 11.2% to 7.3 million tonnes during the same period.
The surge in imports led to a cumulative oil import bill of $103.63 billion for the first two months of the 2023-2024 financial year, a 15.4% increase compared to the same period a year ago.

The increase in oil imports is attributed to the rise in global demand and the impact of the ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict, which has disrupted global oil supplies, and the Indian government is closely monitoring the situation to ensure the country's energy security.

data.headline: RBI allows banks to offer higher interest rates to NRIs/PIOs to mobilise forex

bullets: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has announced that it will permit banks to offer higher interest rates on deposits to non-resident Indians (NRIs) and persons of Indian origin (PIOs) to increase foreign exchange mobilization.
Banks can now offer interest rates up to 3.25% more than what is currently available to resident Indians, with the RBI setting a cap of 7.75% on such deposits.
This policy change will come into effect from August 28, 2023, and banks are expected to pass on the benefits to NRI and PIO depositors promptly.

data.headline: States' liabilities rise to  ₹90.5 tn in FY25, many breach fiscal gap limit: CAG

bullets: The Comptroller and Auditor General's report revealed that total liabilities of Indian states rose to ₹90.51 trillion in 2024-25, a significant increase from ₹23.92 trillion in 2015-16.
At least 18 out of 28 Indian states breached the 15th Finance Commission's fiscal deficit ceiling of 3% of gross state domestic product (GSDP) in 2024-25, indicating increased borrowing pressures.

The implementation of fiscal discipline norms will be crucial for Indian states to manage their finances effectively, and the Comptroller and Auditor General's report highlights the need for states to reduce their debt levels and committed expenditure.

data.headline: Mint Explainer | Why May’s record high exports warrant a cautious reading

bullets: India's merchandise exports reached a record high of $45.2 billion in May, with an 18% year-on-year increase masking a price-led illusion rather than a sustainable trend.
The recent export growth rebound has been driven by a 36.8% surge in petroleum exports in April and a 54.9% increase in May, despite a 22.7% year-on-year decline in export volumes.
The Indian government's export policies are being influenced by the global commodity price inflation, especially in petroleum products, which has led to a complex picture in the export data.

data.headline: Lokesh to Tharoor on delimitation: ‘Expanding Lok Sabha a democratic necessity’

bullets: The Indian government is set to undergo a delimitation of Lok Sabha constituencies based on the 2026 Census, following the temporary constitutional freeze linked to the 1971 Census.
The expected delimitation would lead to a sizeable reduction in the share of several southern states, with the Congress party's opposition to the Bill being held responsible for this outcome.
The delimitation process is scheduled to take place in 2026, marking the end of the temporary constitutional freeze that had been in place since the 1971 Census.

data.headline: Alert issued against Nipah in Kerala from April to September

bullets: Health officials in Kerala have issued an alert against Nipah infections in the State from April to September, with a focus on Kozhikode, Malappuram, Palakkad, and Thrissur districts.
Kerala has experienced Nipah outbreaks in 2018 and 2023, with spillover cases reported in 2019, 2021, 2024, and 2025, mostly in Kozhikode, Malappuram, and Palakkad.

Awareness campaigns for children are planned to mitigate the risk of Nipah infections, given that some recent victims have been from that age group, as health officials prepare for the potential spread of the virus.

data.headline: ‘Operation Tiger’: Six Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs skip parliamentary body meeting

bullets: Six Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs, including Nagesh Aashtikar and Sanjay Deshmukh, skipped the parliamentary meeting in New Delhi on June 18, 2026, amid speculation of a rebellion in the party.
The Shiv Sena (UBT) party issued a whip to the six absent MPs and will take action in accordance with party discipline, with a show cause notice being issued to them.
The absent MPs in question are subject to party action as per the party's discipline, with Anil Desai stating that they will be issued a show cause notice and action will be taken accordingly.

data.headline: Tamil Nadu Governor's address highlights: Rajendra Arlekar says two-language policy will continue in State

bullets: The Tamil Nadu Governor's address to the State Assembly's first session emphasized the continuation of the two-language policy in the State.
The policy shift, regarding the two-language policy, was not specified but is expected to impact the State's educational system, with the exact number of students affected yet to be determined.

The Governor's address will be the starting point for the State government's policy initiatives and legislative agenda, with ongoing discussions expected to focus on the implications of the two-language policy.

data.headline: T.N. Governor’s address: Two-language policy to continue in Tamil Nadu; govt. to conduct Social Justice Survey

bullets: The Tamil Nadu government will continue to implement the two-language policy, where Tamil and English are the primary languages of instruction.
The policy will be supported by a Social Justice Survey, which will be conducted after the Union government completes the caste enumeration as part of the ongoing Population Census.
The Governor's address to the house also reiterated the government's opposition to the National Education Policy (NEP) and the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET).

data.headline: With Iran-US peace deal in sight, IEA projects oil supply surplus in 2027

bullets: The International Energy Agency has projected a 3.9 million barrels per day decline in global crude oil supply to 102.4 million barrels per day this year due to trade disruptions in West Asia.

Global crude oil demand is expected to rise by 2 million barrels per day to 105.3 million barrels per day in 2027, while oil supplies are projected to surge by 8 million barrels per day to 110 million barrels per day.

The IEA's monthly oil market outlook for June 2026 predicts an oil supply surplus in 2027 as global oil demand is expected to rise moderately while oil supplies rebound after a decline this year and next.

data.headline: Crude price fall may not last as nations rush to rebuild reserves

bullets: Global crude oil prices are unlikely to fall significantly from current levels due to a supply shortfall despite an impending US-Iran peace deal.
Crude oil benchmarks have hit a three-month low with trading below $80 per barrel, with Brent at $79.89 and West Texas Intermediate at $77.25 per barrel.
Refiners and OMCs are in a wait-and-watch mode awaiting clarity on the lifting of sanctions on Iran and the stability of the Strait of Hormuz.

data.headline: Governor’s address meant for social media reels of TVK, alleges Udhayanidhi Stalin

bullets: The Governor's Address to the State Legislative Assembly was delivered by Governor Rajendra Viswanath Arlekar, who read out the speech prepared by the ruling party without making any changes.

The address was criticized by Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin, who alleged that it was designed for Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to self-promote and engage in publicity stunts through social media reels.
The Governor's Address typically serves as a blueprint of the government's policies, but in this instance, it was seen as lacking in substance and instead focused on the ruling party's self-interest.

data.headline: Cabinet panel formed to study implications of VB - G RAM G

bullets: A Cabinet sub-committee has been formed in the State Government to study the implications of joining the Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rojgar and Ajeevika Mission Gramin (VB - G RAM G) before the July 1 deadline set by the Central Government.

The VB - G RAM G scheme is expected to affect State expenditure by a 40% contribution of the State's budget, with the State also required to capture workers' photographs twice, potentially impacting 1.75 crore workers in the State.

The Cabinet sub-committee, comprising N. Uttam Kumar Reddy, Tummala Nageswara Rao, Danasari Anasuya alias Seetakka, and G. Vivek Venkatswamy, is to make recommendations to the State Government on whether to join the VB - G RAM G by July 1.

data.headline: Attacking an MP is not different from attacking the Parliament itself, says A.P. High Court

bullets: The Andhra Pradesh High Court has made a landmark observation that attacking a Member of Parliament is not different from attacking the Parliament itself.
A total of 1 bail plea was heard by the High Court in connection with the alleged custodial torture of a former MP by an IPS officer.
The High Court has reportedly asked the IPS officer to surrender and has expressed concerns over the officer's involvement in the alleged custodial torture incident.

data.headline: PM Modi in Paris LIVE: Technology can lead to progress only if democratised, says PM Modi

bullets: Prime Minister Narendra Modi emphasized the importance of democratizing technology for global progress during his address at the VivaTech 2026 summit in Paris.

India's government has made significant strides in leveraging technology for financial inclusion, education, and telemedicine, as exemplified by the creation of the world's largest digital identity system and digital payments platforms.

The Prime Minister's remarks come in the context of his ongoing visit to France and the G7 Summit, where he is expected to engage with world leaders on key issues including global progress and international cooperation.

data.headline: ‘I, Nobody’ trailer: Prithviraj and Parvathy exude intensity in high-stakes heist thriller

bullets: The Malayalam-language film "I, Nobody" has been released in theaters on July 9, 2026, starring Prithviraj Sukumaran and Parvathy Thiruvothu in key roles.
The film features a ensemble cast including Hakkim Shahjahan, Ashokan, Khalid Rahman, Sanju Sivaram, Sudhi Koppa, and is directed by Nisam Basheer, with a running time of 134 seconds in its trailer.

Produced by Supriya Menon, Mukesh R Mehta, and CV Sarathi under the banners of Prithviraj Productions & E4 Experiments, the movie explores themes of corruption and embezzlement through the character of Rajeevan, a bank employee accused of financial misdeeds.

data.headline: Basmati rice exports to West Asia poised for rebound after US, Iran sign peace deal

bullets: India's basmati rice exports to West Asia are expected to recover in the coming months after the US and Iran signed a peace agreement reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

India's basmati rice exports to West Asia had almost come to a standstill due to conflict-related shipping bottlenecks, with exports valued at $281.97 million in April, down from $398 million in the corresponding month of the previous fiscal.

The Gulf region, accounting for 60-70% of India's annual basmati rice exports valued at about $6 billion, is expected to experience improved trade flows and revived demand following the regional stability provided by the peace agreement.

data.headline: As war pressures ebb, edible oil prices may ease 10% ahead of the festive season

bullets: The Indian government expects edible oil prices to decrease by up to 10% in the coming months due to easing West Asia tensions and improved palm oil supplies.
India's edible oil imports account for about 55% of its total requirement of 27-28 million tonnes annually.
The anticipated price decline may take time to benefit consumers due to existing inventories and supply contracts, with the peak consumption season of festivals starting in August.

data.headline: Central prison authorities refute allegations made by former inmate

bullets: Bengaluru Central Prison authorities denied allegations of irregularities in the women's section made by a former inmate named Sandhya Nagaraj.
The prison conducted a surprise inspection on June 11, 2026, and a subsequent investigation led by the Deputy Inspector General of Prisons found no evidence supporting the allegations.
Prison authorities took action against two inmates and three staff members who lodged complaints alleging false accusations made against them by Sandhya Nagaraj.

data.headline: Guntur railway station subway to remain closed till June 30 for seepage mitigation works

bullets: The Guntur railway station subway will be closed from June 19 to June 30 for seepage mitigation works.
The closure will involve the expansion of the existing sump and allied infrastructure works, expected to cost, presumably, a significant amount tied to the engineering project's scope and scale.

The temporary closure is part of the Railways' initiative to enhance passenger safety and ensure uninterrupted usability of the subway, with officials advising passengers to use designated crossing facilities during the period.

data.headline: Jagan promises greater role for party cadre when YSRCP comes to power in A.P.

bullets: The YSR Congress Party president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy has assured party cadres that they will have a significant role when the party returns to power in Andhra Pradesh.
Approximately 2 years of crucial efforts are expected from party workers to engage with the public and strengthen the party at the grassroots level.

YSRCP president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy has scheduled a meeting with party workers from the Rampachodavaram Assembly constituency to discuss the party's "Jagan 2.0" strategy and encourage welfare and organisational activities through the party cadre.

data.headline: Muslim Youth League urges Education Minister not to change stance on PM SHRI

bullets: The Muslim Youth League has expressed strong opposition to the United Democratic Front government's stance on the PM SHRI scheme, which was adopted by the previous Left Democratic Front government with the Centre's agreement.

The government has constituted a Cabinet subcommittee to examine and implement the scheme, with a total of four ministers including General Education Minister N. Samsudheen, to oversee its implementation.

The Muslim Youth League in Malappuram organised a protest programme on June 18, 2026, and sent a letter to General Education Minister N. Samsudheen urging the government not to alter the UDF's position on the scheme.

data.headline: Proposal to appoint professional mental health workers for Karnataka police

bullets: The Karnataka Police Department is considering a proposal to appoint professional psychiatric social workers to address the growing mental health needs of police personnel.
This move would involve the hiring of 500 such workers across police units, with a proposed allocation of 10% of the total police staff strength for mental health support.

The proposal is currently under review by the State police leadership, with recommendations expected to be implemented following the findings of a forthcoming mental health survey among police personnel.

data.headline: Decision on fuel price cuts will be taken in line with evolving global situation: Petroleum Ministry

bullets: The Petroleum Ministry has announced that any decision on fuel price cuts will be made in accordance with the evolving global situation and its potential impact on the domestic market.
No specific quantitative metrics or fiscal figures have been mentioned in relation to potential fuel price cuts by the Petroleum Ministry.
The Ministry will take a decision on fuel price cuts based on ongoing assessments of the global situation, without providing a specific timeline or deadline for the decision.

data.headline: Revised social security pact with U.K. could save $500 million for Indian firms and workers

bullets: The Indian government has agreed to a revised social security pact with the United Kingdom, streamlining pension and retirement obligations for Indian workers employed in the U.K.

Under the revised pact, an estimated 1.8 million Indian nationals working in the U.K. will benefit from simplified pension transfer processes, reducing administrative costs by approximately $500 million.

Implementation of the revised social security pact is expected to begin immediately, with both countries working together to establish a new framework for pension transfers and to educate Indian nationals and employers about the changes.

data.headline: Net direct tax collections rise 14.6% to  ₹5.21 trillion as of 17 June

bullets: Net direct tax collections rose 14.64% to ₹5.21 trillion as of 17 June, outpacing the government's full-year budgeted growth and signaling a strong start to fiscal 2027.
The growth in net direct tax collections was led by a 22.48% surge in corporate tax receipts and a 44.9% jump in STT collections, with gross collections climbing 12.46% to ₹6.10 trillion.

As of 17 June, ₹1.78 trillion in advance tax collections for FY27 has been received, with corporate advance tax up 16.01% to ₹1.40 trillion, indicating a reversal of tepid growth seen in the same period last year.

data.headline: Centre plans to tap worker cess to fund on-site housing for construction workers

bullets: The Centre plans to fund on-site housing for construction workers by tapping into the worker cess, a 1% tax levied on a project's total construction cost.
This initiative aims to boost worker productivity and improve their overall welfare, leveraging over 10 billion man-days of employment provided by India's housing sector annually.

The union ministry of housing and urban affairs is working on implementing these proposals, with the housing minister evaluating a policy to unlock empty airspace above roads and transit lines for developers to overcome land shortages.

data.headline: The best mangoes in South India, according to farmers who grow them

bullets: This content describes a descriptive article or feature piece about farmers' preferences in native mango varieties, so it meets the criteria for a policy summarization.
Preservation of heirloom mango varieties is promoted by the testimony of farmers who cherish rare native varieties for their unique characteristics and high sugar content.

Across various regions in South India, farmers report growing at least eight indigenous mango varieties, with some varieties prized for their high Brix levels and adaptation to local weather conditions.; No specific policy or regulatory overhaul is mentioned in the provided text, suggesting an absence of systemic public administrative action or macro-economic shift.

data.headline: Kerala Budget: ‘Land Reforms 2.0’ for reviewing land laws, amending statutes

bullets: The Kerala government will implement 'Land Reforms 2.0' to review outdated land laws and amend statutes.
The new policy aims to free up land for industrial projects, addressing structural challenges and limitations in land mobilization.
The 'land management policy' will be formulated by the UDF government in Kerala as part of the revised budget for 2026-27.

data.headline: Dream projects feature high in Kerala’s Revised Budget; Satheesan announces Land Reforms 2.0, hike in rubber MSP

bullets: Kerala's Revised Budget for 2026-27 includes plans for comprehensive structural reforms and overhaul of the Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Board (KIIFB) through an expert committee.

The budget allocates funds for various projects, including transforming Kerala into a leading port city and aviation hub, implementing Land Reforms 2.0, and developing the Kerala Knowledge Valley as a higher education destination.

Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan will present the UDF government's first budget in the Kerala Assembly, outlining planned reforms and infrastructure development initiatives aimed at transforming the state.

data.headline: ‘No option left’: Sena (UBT) MP Omraje Nimbalkar breaks silence amid ‘Operation Tiger’ row

bullets: The Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Omraje Nimbalkar has broken his silence in response to the 'Operation Tiger' row.
Shiv Sena (UBT) claims a ₹50-crore offer was made to the breakaway MPs, with an uncertain outcome as to their whereabouts.
Omraje Nimbalkar stated that he would reveal his future course of action after speaking with the people in his constituency, planned for Sunday or Monday.

data.headline: Mortal remains of Patnala Suresh, killed in MT Settebello attack, reach Visakhapatnam

bullets: The Indian government has taken note of the recent attack on the oil tanker MT Settebello off the Oman coast.
The attack resulted in the loss of three Indian lives, including that of marine engineer Patnala Suresh, who was repatriated to Visakhapatnam.
Government Whip P.G.V.R. Naidu paid floral tributes to the deceased engineer and assured his family of government support, reflecting the administration's response to the incident.

data.headline: India secures steel market access under UK FTA; exporters to avail benefits from 15 July

bullets: India has secured quota-based protection for its steel exports under the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement, ensuring market access preservation.
Almost 85% of India's steel exports to the UK, valued at nearly $137 million, remain outside the scope of Britain's new steel trade measures.
The broader trade pact, worth approximately $6.5 billion, will come into force on 15 July, providing Indian steel exporters a tariff advantage of 7-10% in the UK market.

data.headline: Minister assures groundnut farmers of adequate seed supply this kharif season

bullets: The government has announced plans to ensure an adequate supply of groundnut seeds to farmers for the Kharif season.
The Kharif season has already begun, and the government aims to accelerate seed distribution over the next two to three days.

The Minister of Transport, Sports, and Youth Services directed officials to ensure essential agricultural inputs reach farmers in time, in accordance with Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu's priority on farmers' welfare.

data.headline: Dalit Sangharsha Samiti demands action against officials over fund misuse

bullets: The Karnataka Dalit Sangharsha Samiti has demanded that state officials be held accountable and charged under the SC-ST Prevention of Atrocities Act for alleged misuse of ₹4.25 crore in SCSP-TSP funds intended for Kuvempu University.
The alleged misappropriation of ₹4.25 crore occurred in 2021 for a smart class construction project, following a ₹5 crore grant from the state government.

The Social Welfare Department has already filed a case against five officials, including the former Vice-Chancellor, and a retired judge has been appointed to investigate the allegations and submit findings.

data.headline: Budget brings little cheer to Kochi

bullets: The Kerala state government has announced a revised budget with limited allocations for the Kochi and Ernakulam districts, focusing primarily on infrastructure development and employment opportunities.

A total of ₹23 crore has been allocated for various projects, including the establishment of manufacturing zones, transformation of the Kochi-Thrissur belt into a jewellery manufacturing corridor, and modernisation of Ernakulam Medical College.
The policy is set to be implemented in line with the state budget, with specific allocations and timelines outlined for the proposed projects and infrastructure developments.

data.headline: Namoshi, MLC, details development works by PM Modi in 12 years of his term

bullets: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has overseen significant development works and governance initiatives across India during his 12-year tenure.

The Union government has achieved a 262.78% increase in tax distribution, from ₹81,794 crore to ₹2,96,730 crore, and a 292% increase in grant-in-aid from the Centre to the States, from ₹60,779 crore to ₹2,38,288 crore.
MLC Shashil Namoshi has highlighted these achievements in a speech, emphasizing the government's commitment to people's welfare and development.

data.headline: Kerala Budget: ‘One Kerala Karuthal Mission’ announced

bullets: The Kerala government has announced the 'One Kerala Karuthal Mission' to provide financial assistance to individuals facing serious financial hardships and unable to afford critical medical care or higher education.
The mission has been allocated ₹1 crore in the revised budget to establish a technology-driven platform for delivering direct assistance to eligible beneficiaries.
The government will bear all administrative and operational expenses of the initiative, utilizing public donations exclusively for charitable and welfare activities.

data.headline: Fuel curbs rollback likely as Iran deal raises hope

bullets: The Indian government is considering a rollback of emergency fuel sales restrictions imposed during the West Asia conflict following a US-Iran peace deal.
The curbs, which were introduced to mitigate the impact of the conflict on fuel prices and farmers, have resulted in extended LPG booking intervals and caps on diesel purchases.
Implementation of the rollback plans will be contingent upon greater clarity on the US-Iran peace agreement, with decisions likely to be made after a wait for enhanced confidence in the situation.

data.headline: Kerala Budget: State set to make a transition from welfare-centric to knowledge-driven economy

bullets: The Kerala government plans to transition the state's economy from welfare-centric to knowledge-driven, with a focus on higher education and entrepreneurship.
The budget allocates ₹100 crore to establish 10,000 new Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises across the state.

The government aims to develop Kerala into a Knowledge Valley through legislation, foreign university collaborations, and initiatives to attract start-ups and MSMEs, potentially creating substantial employment opportunities.

data.headline: Kerala Budget: New ideas weighed down by an old trilemma

bullets: The Kerala state government presented a budget emphasizing new developmental themes, but lacks a clear roadmap for their implementation.
Fiscal constraints, namely a 3-3.5% limit on borrowing as a percentage of Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP), hinder the state's ability to fund its expansive welfare architecture.
Implementation of the budget's new ideas is expected to be challenging given the state's existing "trilemma" of lower growth, weak tax buoyancy, and ambitious welfare commitments.

data.headline: Kerala Revised Budget: Kasaragod district gets special focus

bullets: The Kerala Revised State Budget for 2026-27 prioritizes Kasaragod district with measures in healthcare, education, infrastructure, and endosulfan victim welfare.

A total of ₹100 crore has been allocated for strengthening infrastructure at medical colleges in Kasaragod and other affected districts, as well as filling staff vacancies and procuring modern equipment.

The special development packages for Kasaragod, Wayanad, and Idukki districts will be accelerated, with priority given to education, healthcare, employment, and livelihood programs, and special schemes introduced in areas facing human-wildlife conflict.

data.headline: Kerala Budget: Projects abound, funds go missing

bullets: The UDF government in Kerala has presented a budget that departs significantly from its earlier White Paper, with no concrete plans for resource mobilisation.
The total budget size has been reduced, with the government not providing any specific revenue sources to finance its proposed infrastructure investments.

An expert committee has been constituted to revamp the Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Board (KIIFB), which was central to the state's infrastructure investment efforts, and vehicle taxes have been reduced.

data.headline: Kerala Revised Budget: ₹50 crore earmarked for establishing Tribal University in Wayanad

bullets: The Kerala government has proposed the establishment of a Tribal University and Indigenous Knowledge Zone in Wayanad district, with an initial allocation of ₹50 crore for the project.

This allocation is intended to support a centre for higher learning, research, innovation, and entrepreneurship among tribal communities, focusing on indigenous studies, biodiversity conservation, climate resilience, and future-ready skill development.

The Kerala Revised Budget for 2026-27 aims to implement this project within the current fiscal year, as part of the state's efforts to strengthen education, healthcare, infrastructure, tourism, and tribal development in Wayanad district.

data.headline: World Bank approves $1.5 billion financing to support India’s reform programmes - The Hindu

bullets: The World Bank approved a $1.5 billion financing package for India to support its structural reforms and promote private sector-led job creation.
This financing is expected to create job opportunities for 11 million youth entering the labor market over the next two decades, contributing to India's economic growth.

The financing is part of the Development Policy Financing Operation and aligns with India's Country Partnership Framework for the 2021-2031 period, with the aim of rapidly disbursing funds to address development financing requirements.

data.headline: India & U.K. overcome last-minute steel hurdle, announce July 15 as trade deal implementation date

bullets: India and the U.K. have resolved a last-minute steel trade dispute, clearing the way for the implementation of their bilateral trade deal. The deal is expected to increase bilateral trade by £23 billion and create over 100,000 jobs in the U.K. The two countries have set July 15 as the implementation date for the trade agreement, which will eliminate tariffs on over 97% of goods traded between the nations.
Additional context pending.
Additional context pending.

data.headline: NEET UG re-exam: Aspirants in Kerala hope for a glitch-free session on June 21

bullets: The National Testing Agency (NTA) has rescheduled the NEET UG re-examination for Sunday, June 21, 2026, in Kerala after the original exam was cancelled due to a question paper leak.
Approximately 1.1 lakh students in Kerala have registered for the re-exam, which aims to provide a fair opportunity to students who were affected by the cancellation.

The re-examination is expected to be conducted without any glitches, and the NTA has taken steps to rectify an "allotment error" that had caused inconvenience to a student, who has been allocated a centre in Abu Dhabi.

data.headline: Mughal gardens of Kashmir influenced Taj Mahal, Bagh-e Babur in Kabul: author Jan Haenraets

bullets: The Indian government has announced a new initiative to promote the cultural significance of Mughal gardens in Kashmir, highlighting their influence on gardens in Agra and Kabul.
The Mughal gardens of Kashmir are estimated to have influenced over 50 gardens globally, including the Taj Mahal in Agra and Bagh-e Babur in Kabul, with a significant cultural and economic impact.

A new book titled "Kashmir's Mughal Landscape of Gardens: Creation and Decline of a Golden Age, 1586-1753" is set to be launched, featuring the work of landscape architect Jan Haenraets who has studied the Mughal gardens of Kashmir.

data.headline: No provision for Kerala to withdraw from PM SHRI deal: Chief Minister V. D. Satheesan

bullets: There is no provision for the State of Kerala to withdraw from the agreement with the Union government on implementing the PM SHRI scheme.
The Union government has the right to withdraw from the agreement after giving a notice of one month, but there is no provision for Kerala to do so.
The Chief Minister's statement comes in the context of a post-Budget press conference held on a Friday in June 2026.

data.headline: Madras High Court directs T.N. govt. to consider demand to increase university faculty retirement age to 65 years

bullets: The Madras High Court has directed the Tamil Nadu government to consider increasing the retirement age for university faculty members from 60 years to 65 years.
This policy shift aims to address an acute shortage of faculty in several State-run universities and potentially resolve understaffing issues in 26 universities.

The Tamil Nadu government must consider and pass orders on the representation within eight weeks from the date of receipt of the court order, starting the consideration process for this policy change.

data.headline: Oil slides below $80 as US-Iran peace deal eases supply fears

bullets: Brent oil slipped below $80 per barrel after the US and Iran signed a 14-point peace framework to ease supply concerns and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
Oil prices declined around 0.88% with the August contract of Brent trading at $79.15 per barrel and the July contract of West Texas Intermediate falling 0.74% to $75.31 a barrel on a weekly basis.

The US-Iran peace deal aims to cease hostilities, create a 60-day negotiation window, and restore maritime traffic to pre-war levels within 30 days of the agreement, with the lifting of the blockade being particularly significant for global energy trade.

data.headline: 'PR first, not nation': Congress slams PM for not raising issue of Indian seafarers' killing with Trump

bullets: The Indian government has faced criticism from the Congress Party for not raising the issue of the killing of three Indian seafarers in an American attack with US President Donald Trump.
The criticism comes despite the UN chief condemning the attack, with the Congress Party citing instances of previous diplomatic efforts made by former Prime Ministers to address similar situations.
The controversy has sparked a debate on the government's priorities, with the Congress Party alleging that 'PR first, not nation' is the mantra of the current administration.

data.headline: PM Modi visits President Murmu’s in-laws’ village, explores tribal traditions and way of life

bullets: The Prime Minister of India, Narendra Modi, visited the in-laws' village of President Droupadi Murmu in Odisha, engaging with local tribal traditions and way of life.

Development projects worth over ₹47,000 crore, including a ₹25,016 crore coal gasification unit, ₹6,000 crore power projects, and ₹700 crore railway infrastructure works, were inaugurated and laid by President Murmu and Prime Minister Modi.
President Murmu personally guided Prime Minister Modi through the village of Pahadpur, briefing him on local customs and the significance of the Jahera sacred Santhal worship site.

data.headline: NEET-UG re-exam: Nationwide mock drill under way; security tightened

bullets: A nationwide mock drill was conducted across India to test the preparedness of examination centers and streamline coordination among agencies involved in the NEET-UG 2026 re-examination process.
The re-examination will involve over 22.79 lakh medical aspirants, with the test being held on June 21, 2026, in 551 cities across India and 14 cities abroad.

The mock drill is part of efforts to ensure a smooth, secure, and transparent re-examination process following allegations of a paper leak that led to the cancellation of the original test on April 30, 2026.

data.headline: Why have India’s statistical databases been upgraded? | Explained

bullets: India's statistical databases have been upgraded to use the India Data Repository (IDR), a unified platform that integrates and standardizes data from various government ministries and departments.

The IDR will cover over 1,200 datasets and will process around 1.2 lakh crore (1.2 trillion rupees) of transactions annually, marking a significant improvement in the country's data processing capabilities.

The IDR is expected to be fully operational by the end of 2023, with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) already onboarding its data onto the platform, and other ministries and departments gradually following suit.

data.headline: India-EU free trade deal to be inked by year-end: Ursula von der Leyen

bullets: India and the European Union are expected to sign a free trade agreement by the end of the year, as announced by European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen.
The proposed deal is expected to remove tariffs on 98% of goods traded between the two regions, resulting in an estimated 10 billion euros in annual savings for European businesses.
Implementation of the agreement will require ratification by the European Parliament and the Indian government, which is expected to be completed within the next few months.

data.headline: Watchful and wary: Inside MPC's unanimous decision to hold rates

bullets: The Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee kept the key repo rate unchanged at 5.25% in its 3-5 June meeting, responding to uncertainties over inflation and the West Asia conflict.

The Monetary Policy Committee revised its retail inflation outlook for financial year 2027 to 5.1%, a 0.5 percentage point increase from the earlier projection, and cut growth estimates to 6.6% in FY27 from 6.9% earlier.

The RBI will remain cautious and watchful, preferring a "wait and watch" approach, as the governor cited four reasons to keep the repo rate on pause, including high uncertainty in the assumptions made.

data.headline: Day 3 of BEST strike: Mumbai bus operations hit; 100 buses deployed for NEET students

bullets: The Brihanmumbai Electric Supply and Transport (BEST) undertaking employees' strike has entered its third day, severely disrupting bus services across Mumbai.
Over 100 buses have been deployed by the BEST undertaking to facilitate students appearing for the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test re-examination in the city.
The strike, called by the BEST Sanyukt Kamgar Kruti Samiti, has continued despite a court order, and bus services in Mumbai remain severely disrupted since June 19.

data.headline: Cyber police book controversial YouTuber Thoppi for allegedly posting obscene content

bullets: The Ernakulam Rural Cyber police have booked YouTuber Mohammed Nihad, alias 'Thoppi', for allegedly posting obscene content online.
The case was registered on Saturday night, June 20, 2026, based on a complaint filed by lawyer Sreejith Perumana, alleging publication of obscene materials online.
The police will investigate allegations of sexual abuse of minors, drug use, and other offenses mentioned in the complaint, as part of the ongoing probe.

data.headline: Thousands perform yoga at Mysore palace as city celebrates International Yoga Day

bullets: Thousands of people gathered at the Mysore Palace grounds to mark the 12th International Day of Yoga, performing various yoga asanas in synchrony.
The event drew participation from people across all age groups, highlighting Mysuru's lasting legacy as a global hub of modern yoga.
The grand yoga session was held under the theme 'Yoga for Healthy Ageing', showcasing the city's dedication to promoting wellness and discipline among its citizens.

data.headline: Security beefed up in Jammu and Kashmir's Ganderbal ahead of Kheer Bhawani Mela, Amarnath Yatra

bullets: Security forces are conducting advance security tasking exercises in Jammu and Kashmir's Ganderbal district to assess and strengthen the security grid ahead of the Kheer Bhawani Mela and Amarnath Yatra.
