These security measures include area domination exercises, highway checking, and surveillance, with security personnel conducting thorough checks of vehicles and maintaining strict vigil at important points.
The enhanced security is scheduled to be in place by July 3, when the Amarnath Yatra begins, with a comprehensive security preparedness also being implemented for the Kheer Bhawani Mela on June 22.

data.headline: CM Vijay forms three-member committee to probe ammonia gas leak near Periyapalayam

bullets: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay has ordered the formation of a three-member committee to investigate the ammonia gas leak near Periyapalayam.

The committee, comprising the Director of Industrial Safety and Health, Member Secretary of the Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board, and Additional Director of Public Health, will submit an interim report within 24 hours and a final report in three days.

The committee's formation comes in the wake of a deadly ammonia gas leak at a seafood processing unit in Tiruvallur district, which resulted in the deaths of seven workers and the hospitalization of several others.

data.headline: Human milk bank inaugurated in Cuddalore

bullets: A human milk bank has been inaugurated in Cuddalore's Government Medical College and Hospital, aiming to provide breast milk access to newborns who are unable to suckle-feed due to various reasons.

The milk bank is expected to ensure safe and nutritious breast milk for over 1,000 newborns annually, reducing neonatal morbidity and mortality, while promoting optimal nutrition during the crucial early days of life.

The facility will function as a dedicated centre for collection, screening, processing, pasteurization, storage, and distribution of donor human milk in accordance with national guidelines, expected to strengthen neonatal services in the district and support the care of high-risk newborns.

data.headline: AICC in-charge’s endorsement of party rebel candidates contradicts Puducherry unit chief’s stand

bullets: The All India Congress Committee (AICC) in-charge for Puducherry, Girish Chodankar, has endorsed six party rebel candidates who filed nominations before the allocation of constituencies.
These six candidates have been allocated 60% of the total tickets by the Congress party for the recent Assembly election.

The endorsement of these candidates by Mr Chodankar directly contradicts the stand of the Puducherry Pradesh Congress Committee (PPCC) chief V. Vaithilingam, who had declared them as "rebels" and threatened to take action against them.

data.headline: Development finance should be used strategically to improve governance, service delivery in Northeast: FM Sitharaman

bullets: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman urged the northeastern states to strategically utilize externally aided project funding to improve governance and service delivery.
The funding to India's Northeast has risen nearly eightfold to ₹76,000 crore since 2014.
The finance minister called for greater investments in human capital, describing the region's youth, entrepreneurial energy, and women leaders as key drivers of growth.

data.headline: AI boom shields Asia from West Asia shock, but risks mount for India and region: Moody’s Analytics

bullets: Asia-Pacific economies have weathered the fallout from the West Asia conflict due to AI-led exports and investment, but regional growth is expected to slow as these benefits dissipate.
Moody's Analytics forecasts Asia-Pacific growth to ease to 4.1% in 2026 from 4.3% in 2025 and further decline to 3.6% in 2027 as the AI-driven demand boost fades.

The ratings firm expects higher oil prices, inflation, trade tensions, and weather-related disruptions to weigh on growth in the second half of 2026 and beyond, potentially exacerbating existing vulnerabilities for India and the region.

data.headline: CISF to be deployed at five more prisons in Jammu and Kashmir

bullets: The Union Ministry of Home Affairs plans to deploy the Central Industrial Security Force at five more prisons in Jammu and Kashmir, including a high-security prison in Kathua.
The CISF will secure the perimeters of these facilities using a combination of trained manpower, modern surveillance systems, and strict access control measures.

The new deployments are set to extend the CISF's security cover to five additional prisons, including the high-security prison at Mahanpur (Kathua), with the first deployments expected to take place following the operationalisation of the new facilities.

data.headline: Engineer’s body recovered from Varthur STP; search continues for another missing worker

bullets: The Varthur Police have registered a FIR against a private firm contracted for sewage treatment plant maintenance following a complaint from BWSSB.
Five days of rescue operations have been hindered by heavy rain, poor visibility, and toxic gases, with one worker's body recovered and another still missing.
The deceased worker, identified as 30-year-old Agilan Mohan, has been shifted for post-mortem examination, while efforts to locate 27-year-old Brijesh Kumar continue with slim chances of survival.

data.headline: Gunfire at Congress MLA’s office shows law and order collapse in Haryana, says Hooda

bullets: The Haryana government has faced criticism from Leader of Opposition Bhupinder Singh Hooda regarding its handling of law and order in the state.

At least 50 to 60 gangs are now active across Haryana, according to Mr. Hooda, who previously led the state government and implemented a policy to either deter crime or have individuals leave the state.

The state police have arrested one suspect in connection with the gunfire at Congress MLA Balram Dangi's office in Rohtak, an incident that Mr. Hooda described as evidence of the state's crumbling law and order situation.

data.headline: CBSE announces Class 12 re-valuation results

bullets: The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) announced the revaluation results for Class 12 board exam answer sheets of students who applied for verification and re-evaluation.
Over 87% of the total applications received have been declared, with the remaining outcomes to be released in phases and the entire process expected to be completed soon.
Students can check their updated marks on the CBSE's official website using their login credentials, with the results being released in phases over the coming days.

data.headline: Right to vote should be a Fundamental Right: Jairam Ramesh

bullets: The Indian Congress leader Jairam Ramesh advocates for the right to vote to be recognized as a fundamental right to safeguard citizens against arbitrary disenfranchisement and voter suppression.

This policy shift would potentially impact millions of voters in India, as Jairam Ramesh alleges that under the Special Intensive Revision process, astronomical numbers of individuals faced disqualifications in various states.

The proposal to recognize the right to vote as a fundamental right is expected to be discussed following a recent Supreme Court judgment that declared the right to walk on a footpath a fundamental right, setting a precedent for future constitutional amendments.

data.headline: India-U.S. interim deal requires only ‘final touches’; Greer to visit New Delhi on June 23-24

bullets: The India-U.S. interim trade deal is nearing completion, requiring only minor adjustments before its formal announcement.
The deal is estimated to have the potential to increase U.S. agricultural exports to India by up to $10 billion annually.
U.S. Trade Representative Katherine Tai's deputy, Sarah Bianchi, will accompany Trade Representative Brendan Carr to New Delhi on June 23-24 to finalize the agreement.

data.headline: India boosts Russian, UAE oil purchases in June ahead of full Hormuz recovery

bullets: India's oil imports from Russia and the UAE significantly increased in June, with purchases from Russia rising by 44.3% and from the UAE by 32.9% compared to the previous month. In June, India imported 1.16 million barrels per day from Russia and 1.53 million barrels per day from the UAE, with total oil purchases reaching 4.79 million barrels per day. The increased imports from Russia and the UAE are part of India's strategy to diversify its oil supplies and reduce reliance on Middle Eastern countries in the wake of the full recovery of the Hormuz Strait.
Additional context pending.
Additional context pending.

data.headline: India, Iran look to soon resume talks to get Chabahar Port plan back on track

bullets: India and Iran are set to resume talks on restoring operations and expanding the Chabahar Port, a strategic facility seen as a counterweight to China's influence in the region.
The 10-year agreement signed in May 2024 for running the Shahid Beheshti terminal by India Ports Global Ltd IPGL is expected to be a key focus point in the upcoming talks.

The discussions are expected to take place as geopolitical conditions in the region begin to stabilize after months of uncertainty surrounding the project due to US sanctions-related concerns and disruptions caused by conflict in West Asia.

data.headline: Young Punjab kids ‘rich for 4 yrs after selling their lands… then broke’: World Bank's Ajay Banga on urban agri economy

bullets: The World Bank has identified financial instability among young people in Punjab who quickly spend earnings from selling their farmland on consumer goods and lifestyle expenses.
According to World Bank President Ajay Banga, a significant portion of young people in Punjab who sell their farmland receive substantial sums, but remain financially unstable within four years.

The World Bank has suggested that providing cooperatives and access to better agricultural technology, such as seeds and fertilizers, could help young farmers in Punjab increase productivity and achieve more stable financial outcomes.

data.headline: The week in charts: State debt concerns, WPI inflation, NSE’s IPO debut

bullets: India's state finances are coming under pressure as debt levels and fiscal deficits remain high, with the combined liabilities of 28 states rising 10.5% year-on-year to Rs 90.5 trillion in FY25.
The states' debt accounted for 28.5% of India's GDP in FY25, with 18 states breaching the 15th Finance Commission's fiscal deficit limit of 3% of gross state domestic product.

The Comptroller and Auditor General's report highlights the need for states to manage their debt levels, with consistent annual growth of 10-13% over the past few years and a deteriorating debt-to-GDP ratio.

data.headline: West Bengal Budget: State Finance Minister pledges to fill up 1 lakh government vacancies, 33% for women

bullets: The West Bengal state government has pledged to fill up 1 lakh government vacancies, with 33% of the positions reserved for women.
The proposed budget allocates a ₹36,000-crore outlay for the Annapurna Yojana financial assistance scheme for women, offering them ₹3,000 per month.
Finance Minister Swapan Dasgupta has announced a 20% hike in dearness allowance (DA) for government employees and aimed to present the BJP government's first full budget in the Assembly.

data.headline: Industries Secretary submits unconditional apology in Kerala High Court

bullets: The Principal Secretary of Industries, A.P.M. Mohammad Hanish, submitted an unconditional apology to the Kerala High Court in a contempt of court petition related to alleged irregularities in the import of raw cashew by Kerala State Cashew Development Corporation.
The Kerala High Court had previously warned Mohammad Hanish that he would have to appear in person, or else ‘coercive steps’ would be initiated to secure his presence.

The current Secretary in charge of the Cashew Development Department, K. Biju, has sought time to reconsider the denial of sanction for a CBI probe into the alleged misappropriation of ₹600 crore in the import of raw cashew between 2006 and 2015.

data.headline: AIADMK legislators walk out of Tamil Nadu Assembly over Mekedatu issue

bullets: The Tamil Nadu Assembly was disrupted when AIADMK legislators, led by Edappadi K. Palaniswami, staged a walkout in protest of the Speaker's denial of permission to discuss the Mekedatu issue.
The walkout occurred despite a resolution on the issue being unanimously accepted by all parties in the Business Advisory Committee.
The disruption took place during a sitting of the Assembly on June 22, 2026, where the Speaker cited the absence of Question Hour and Zero Hour as the reason for not permitting the discussion.

data.headline: Telangana CM seeks passenger terminal, MRO and other amenities at proposed airport in Adilabad

bullets: The Telangana government has assured full cooperation to the Central government for the establishment of an airport in Adilabad district.
The proposed airport is expected to have a passenger terminal, MRO, and other amenities developed alongside the existing IAF terminal.
The Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy has conveyed the government's readiness to support the Union government in land acquisition, transfer of utilities, and other requirements for the project.

data.headline: VHP alleges 'communal discrimination' at NEET centres, seeks probe

bullets: The Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) has accused the National Testing Agency (NTA) of communal discrimination against Hindu NEET-UG aspirants who were allegedly prohibited from wearing certain religious symbols at exam centres.
According to the NTA, over 20 lakh candidates took the NEET re-exam at 5,440 centres across India and 14 centres abroad.

The VHP has demanded a probe into the alleged discrimination and sought a detailed explanation from the NTA on its dress code norms, with National Spokesperson Vinod Bansal calling for an investigation into the matter.

data.headline: The benefits and risks of RBI’s policy on foreign currency NRI deposits

bullets: The Reserve Bank of India is reviving an old strategy by allowing non-resident Indians to make foreign currency deposits in Indian banks to stabilize the rupee.
As of March, the total NRI deposits in Indian banks stood at around $165 billion, with foreign currency non-resident (B) deposits accounting for $33 billion or 20% of the total.

The Reserve Bank of India plans to implement recent policy changes on foreign currency non-resident (B) deposits, with Indian banks now offering these deposits in several foreign currencies, subject to a minimum maturity of one year.

data.headline: Telangana’s legitimate rights over Tungabhadra waters will not be compromised: Uttam

bullets: The Telangana government, led by Irrigation Minister N. Uttam Kumar Reddy, has reaffirmed its commitment to protecting the state's legitimate rights over Tungabhadra waters.

Telangana's rights over Tungabhadra waters amount to ensuring equitable distribution of water among basin states, and the government aims to expedite modernisation of the Rajolibanda Diversion Scheme by 2024.

The Telangana government will pursue technical, legal, and administrative measures to safeguard its interests in Tungabhadra waters, including a stronger role by state officials in the Tungabhadra Board and implementation of Phase-II of the Tummilla Lift Irrigation Scheme.

data.headline: SBI team calls on Telangana Chief Secretary amid Raidurgam Knowledge City land controversy

bullets: The State Bank of India has sent a delegation to meet with the Telangana Chief Secretary in response to the controversy over a disputed 5.09-acre land parcel in Raidurgam Knowledge City.

The SBI's actions in challenging the Telangana government's decision to auction the land in the High Court have led to a controversy and raised concerns about potential repercussions, including the withdrawal of government transactions from the bank.

The Chief Secretary is understood to have conveyed the government's concerns and positions to the SBI delegation during their 30-minute meeting, although the details of the discussions remain unclear.

data.headline: Indians among 13 dead in Qatar explosion, says Qatar's Minister

bullets: At least 13 people, including Indians, were killed in an explosion at the Ras Laffan Industrial City in Qatar on June 21, 2026.
The incident resulted in 66 injuries and involved fatalities of both Indian and Pakistani origins, with the exact number of Indian victims unknown.

The Embassy of India in Doha is in constant touch with Qatari authorities and will provide assistance to the families of those affected by the explosion and fire at the Barzan local gas supply facility.

data.headline: BJP leader slams govt. over police job issues, GO 46

bullets: The Telangana state government's Government Order 46 has been criticized by BJP leader A. Maheshwar Reddy for causing difficulties for unemployed youth applying for police jobs.
A total of 5,000 constable posts are currently advertised, which the BJP leader claims is insufficient and should be increased to 20,000 to meet the demands of job seekers.

Implementation of Government Order 46 has resulted in unequal treatment of candidates from rural districts, who are losing out on jobs despite scoring high marks, prompting the BJP leader to demand a review of the policy.

data.headline: India's core sector growth hits seven-month low as Iran war bites

bullets: India's eight core sector growth rate slowed to a seven-month low of 0.5% in May 2026 due to disruptions caused by the crisis in West Asia, primarily affecting coal and petroleum sectors.

The contraction in coal and petroleum sectors led to a decline in crude oil production by 4.6%, natural gas production by 4.9%, and fertilizer production by 0.9% in May 2026, while the steel, cement, and power sectors showed growth.

The provisional data from the union ministry of commerce and industry suggested that the IIP growth is likely to weaken to 2-3% in May 2026 from 4.9% in April 2026, attributing the decline in production to higher import of crude and softening of international prices.

data.headline: Gen Z is out-earning millennials, shows data; but has inflation already closed the gap?

bullets: The UK's Resolution Foundation reported a 12% difference in real weekly pay between Generation Z and millennials at age 24, with Generation Z workers outearning their millennial counterparts.
This pay disparity translates to higher nominal wages, but economists caution that real financial freedom is not automatically ensured due to rising costs and inflation.

The Resolution Foundation's findings are based on analysis of economic data from the UK, with the report's senior economist stating that the stagnation of living standards for millennials has indeed been followed by similar trends for Generation Z.

data.headline: Reclaiming Tamil Nadu’s fiscal autonomy and sustaining its growth model

bullets: The Government of Tamil Nadu has released a 120-page white paper analyzing the State's financial status and economic conditions, presenting a genuine and honest account of tax collection issues.
The white paper attributes the State's fiscal challenges to a shrinking tax base and leakages in revenue collection and expenditure patterns, rather than blaming corruption or fiscal profligacy.
Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Joseph Vijay aims to reclaim the State's fiscal autonomy from the Union, generate decent jobs, and improve wages by actively renegotiating fiscal space with the Union.

data.headline: Kodagu villagers’ opposition forces spiritual guru Sri M to withdraw proposed meditation retreat

bullets: Sri M, a spiritual guru, has withdrawn his proposed meditation retreat project near the Malma Hills in Karnataka's Kodagu district following opposition from local residents and organisations.
The project would have had a significant impact, with 522 hectares of land being affected by the construction of roads, ponds, and alleged commercial activity.
The villagers' sustained protests led to the project's cancellation, with Sri M citing ecological, cultural, and religious concerns as the reason for withdrawing the development.

data.headline: Freshworks founder pays ₹211 crores to own a 7.65-ground house on Boat Club Road in Chennai

bullets: Girish Mathrubootham, founder of Freshworks, purchased a 7.65-ground residential property in Chennai's Boat Club Road for ₹211 crore.
This real estate transaction marks a rare and exclusive deal in Chennai's ultra-exclusive Boat Club area, where land is highly sought after and scarce.
The property sale was facilitated by Global Adjustments, a luxury real estate advisory firm, which represented both the buyer and seller in the deal.

data.headline: Cross-voting intensifies mistrust in faction-ridden BJP State unit

bullets: The BJP State unit in Karnataka is experiencing intensified mistrust due to cross-voting by its MLAs during the recent Legislative Council elections.

The party has 7 members in the Legislative Council who crossed the floor to vote in favor of the Congress-JD(S) candidate, accounting for nearly 50% of the total cross-voting incidents in the elections.
The party high command is set to discuss the issue in Delhi on Tuesday, with senior leaders concerned that the air of mistrust may affect the morale of its cadre ahead of the next Assembly elections.

data.headline: Governor is like a manager, doesn’t understand the needs of students, says Tamil Nadu Law Minister

bullets: The Tamil Nadu state government has taken a stance against the Governor's role in appointing Vice-Chancellors to state-run universities, citing a lack of understanding of students' and people's needs.
This decision is based on a proposal to have the government directly appoint Vice-Chancellors, although the exact number of universities affected by this shift is not specified.
Implementation of this proposal may depend on ongoing negotiations between the state government and the Governor, with no concrete timeline announced for the change.

data.headline: Global economic landscape remains fragile: RBI Bulletin

bullets: The Reserve Bank of India has announced a cautious stance on interest rates to mitigate potential economic shocks in the global market.

The RBI has estimated that a 50 basis point increase in interest rates could lead to a 30-40 basis point increase in the benchmark lending rate, affecting around 70% of outstanding non-performing assets.

Implementation of the RBI's monetary policy decision will be closely monitored and assessed over the next six months, with a review of the economic situation scheduled for the next Central Board meeting in September.

data.headline: Demand driving growth, but economic outlook ‘somewhat clouded’ by supply issues: RBI

bullets: The Reserve Bank of India has announced that the country's economic growth is being driven by demand but faces some uncertainty due to ongoing supply chain disruptions.
The RBI has forecast a GDP growth rate of around 6.7% for the fiscal year 2023-24, with a projected inflation rate of 5.3% and a fiscal deficit of 4.5% of the GDP.

The central bank has attributed the supply-side challenges to factors such as global events, logistics issues, and a shortage of raw materials, and has stated its intention to monitor the situation closely and take necessary policy interventions to mitigate the impact.

data.headline: RBI governor asks banks to treat MSMEs as long-term partners

bullets: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) governor has asked financial institutions to treat micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) as long-term business partners rather than just a regulatory obligation.

The RBI plans to utilize India's digital public infrastructure, including the account aggregator framework and Unified Lending Interface, to build an inclusive credit ecosystem for MSMEs, aiming to strengthen credit access and support their growth.

Financial institutions, including banks and non-banking financial companies, have been asked to accelerate the implementation of government-backed programmes such as priority sector lending, Mudra, and the credit guarantee scheme for micro and small enterprises by the end of 2026.

data.headline: RBI flags risks if West Asia peace deal fails, says India remains strong

bullets: The Reserve Bank of India has warned that a breakdown of the West Asia peace agreement could lead to significant economic risks, including higher inflation and disruptions to energy supplies.

India's economy remains resilient, with a 7.8% GDP growth in the fourth quarter of 2025-26 and sustained economic momentum, as indicated by high-frequency indicators for the first two months of 2026-27.
The RBI will closely monitor global and domestic economic developments, amid easing tensions in the region, to assess and mitigate potential risks to financial stability and economic growth.

data.headline: Cockroaches in kitchen, mould growth on vegetables found during Cyberabad food safety inspections

bullets: The Cyberabad Municipal Corporation conducted food safety inspections at restaurants and a packaged drinking water unit in Hyderabad, uncovering multiple violations. A total of 14 out of 33 food establishments inspected were found to be violating food safety norms, with most of the incidents occurring due to lack of proper records and inadequate hygiene practices. The inspections, carried out on June 22, 2026, resulted in the detection of cockroaches in kitchens, mould growth on vegetables, and other health hazards, prompting calls for immediate corrective actions.
Additional context pending.
Additional context pending.

data.headline: Two dead in explosion at Dakshin Energy unit in Parawada industrial park, Anakapalli

bullets: The explosion at the Dakshin Energy unit in the Parawada Industrial Park resulted in the deaths of two workers and injuries to two others.
The cause of the fire that killed B. Trinadh and V. Venkatesh remains unknown.
An investigation into the incident is pending as the police are still gathering information and assessing the damage to the rotary pyrolysis plant.

data.headline: Karnataka CM tells officials to provide land and building to house 20 lakh books of Anke Gowda

bullets: Karnataka's Chief Minister D. K. Shivakumar has directed officials to provide an alternative place and building to house over 20 lakh books collected by M. Anke Gowda's library.
The library, set up by Anke Gowda in Pandavapura, has entered the Limca Book of Records for being the largest private library in India.

Karnataka's Chief Minister D. K. Shivakumar issued the direction on June 22, 2026, after meeting with Anke Gowda at Vidhana Soudha in Bengaluru to discuss suitable arrangements for the library's massive book collection.

data.headline: Leopard that strayed into Kelakam in Kerala’s Kannur trapped and released into deep forest

bullets: The Kerala Forest Department successfully trapped and released a five-year-old male leopard that had strayed into Kelakam in Kannur, bringing relief to local residents.
The operation involved a large-scale search with local residents participating, and the leopard was found to be in good health after a detailed examination by a veterinary doctor.

The Forest Department intensified surveillance and search operations in the area, with the leopard being trapped and released into the deep forest on the same night by the Rapid Response Team veterinary unit.

data.headline: Lucknow building fire: Mother's plea, colleague’s distress call capture horror

bullets: Uttar Pradesh authorities have launched a high-level investigation into a devastating fire at a three-storey commercial building in Lucknow on June 22, 2026.
The fire resulted in 15 fatalities and 7 injuries, with the cause yet to be determined.
Additional context pending.

data.headline: Govt plans subsidized tomato sales to cool price surge

bullets: The Indian government plans to intervene in the tomato market by selling tomatoes at subsidized rates through cooperative outlets to cool a price surge caused by supply disruptions.

The proposed market intervention aims to bring down the retail price of tomatoes, which has risen to ₹44.36 per kg on average, up from ₹34.43 per kg a year ago, and is currently being sold at ₹60-70 per kg in several local retail markets.

The government is likely to sell tomatoes at ₹35-45 per kg through outlets operated by the National Cooperative Consumers' Federation of India and other cooperative networks, with the department of consumer affairs discussing the issue last week.

data.headline: US trade chief to visit India for interim deal discussions

bullets: US trade representative Jamieson Greer will visit India to discuss an interim trade agreement as part of the broader US-India bilateral trade agreement framework.
The negotiations will focus on implementing the US-India joint statement and are nearing completion, with a first tranche of the trade deal potentially signed before 24 July.

The visit comes amid efforts by India and the US to deepen economic ties and address market access issues through a comprehensive trade pact, following talks between US President Donald Trump and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 13 February 2025.

data.headline: Symposium explores humour’s role in challenging social and political realities

bullets: The University College Union and Film Club organized a symposium on 'Humour in Malayalam cinema' at Ayyankali Hall, exploring its role in challenging social and political realities.

The event featured a special session titled "Priyadarshan at 100" paying tribute to filmmaker Priyadarshan, and speakers highlighted the evolution of humour in Malayalam cinema, tracing its roots in literature, theatre, and traditional performance forms.

The symposium included discussions on the portrayal of women in comedy, the relevance of political satires such as _Sandesham_, and the role of humour in exposing social issues, with speakers noting its importance as a tool of criticism and reflection in Malayalam cinema.

data.headline: Srisailam temple staff told to maintain cleanliness, hygiene at Kalyanakatta

bullets: The Sri Bhramaramba Mallikarjuna Swamy temple trust board chairman directed staff to prioritize cleanliness and hygiene at the Kalyanakatta tonsuring centre.
A surprise inspection by the chairman emphasized the need for continuous sanitation measures, with staff instructed to maintain punctuality and ensure devotees do not experience long waiting periods.
The chairman asked officials to regularly monitor working conditions of lights and fans at the Kalyanakatta and interacted with devotees to gather feedback on facilities provided.

data.headline: India needs to move from ease and cost to speed of doing business, CII president Mukundan says

bullets: The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) president R. Mukundan has emphasized the need for India's reforms process to prioritize the speed of doing business alongside ease and cost considerations.
According to CII president R. Mukundan, the private sector has been investing in India, contradicting government officials' claims, with such investments expected to become more apparent soon.

The CII president's recommendations aim to streamline bureaucratic processes and logistics to enhance the overall business environment in India, a goal expected to be pursued by the government in its ongoing reforms.

data.headline: CCMB scientist K. Thangaraj gets Padma Shri

bullets: The Government of India has conferred the Padma Shri award on K. Thangaraj, a Geneticist at the Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology (CCMB) in Hyderabad, in recognition of his significant contributions to understanding Indian population ancestry and migration patterns.

Over three decades of research, Mr. Thangaraj's work has involved extensive genetic analyses of unique markers among various communities, tracing their links across regions, and decoding historical mysteries linked to ancient sites and populations.

The award ceremony took place at the Rashtrapati Bhavan in New Delhi, where President Droupadi Murmu presented the Padma Shri to Mr. Thangaraj, a CSIR Bhatnagar Fellow, amidst other distinguished scientists and researchers.

data.headline: 76% health insurance reimbursement claimants face immediate financial burden: report

bullets: The Indian government has not announced any policy directly related to the provided content, however, a recent report by Policybazaar suggests that approximately 76% of health insurance reimbursement claimants in the country face immediate financial burden.
This financial burden is reflected in the decreasing ability to manage costs with liquid savings, which dropped from 32% to 24% between 2024-25 according to the Policybazaar report.

The report also highlights the increasing financial stress faced by insurance holders at the time of raising claims, with metros recording a 14% increase and Tier-2 cities having the highest incidence overall at 78%.

data.headline: India's private sector output moderates further in June

bullets: The Indian private sector output moderated further in June, with slower growth in new orders, international sales, employment, and business activity.
The HSBC Flash India Manufacturing PMI Output Index fell to 57.4 in June from 58.0 in May, and the HSBC Flash India Composite PMI Output Index fell to 57.4 from the revised May figure of 59.3.

The West Asia war-induced global slowdown dampened Indian manufacturing and services, leading to a weaker expansion in both sectors in June, and the full Purchasing Managers' Index readings are expected to be released shortly.

data.headline: Will Singapore remain India's export star even after Iran war ends?

bullets: India's merchandise exports to Singapore rose 124% year-on-year to $5.07 billion in April-May, the sharpest rise among all major destinations driven by higher petroleum exports.

Despite being less geographically advantageous than the UAE, Singapore's robust transshipment infrastructure and structural advantages have driven a surge in India's exports to the country, utilizing it as a key hub for East and Southeast Asia.
The continued viability of Singapore's export market for India will depend on the extent to which its structural advantages endure once the current West Asian war disruptions subside.

data.headline: IMD forecasts a wet weekend for Andhra Pradesh

bullets: The India Meteorological Department has forecast a wet weekend for Andhra Pradesh from June 26 to 28, 2026, with a possibility of isolated heavy rain in coastal areas.
According to the forecast, the State's rainfall deficit has decreased from 32.8% on June 18 to 27.3% on June 23, with 11 out of 28 districts still reporting deficient rainfall.
The IMD is predicting light to moderate showers in all three regions of Andhra Pradesh, including South and North Coastal A.P. and Rayalaseema, till the end of the month.

data.headline: One-gram gold ring for babies born in T.N. government hospitals

bullets: The Tamil Nadu government has launched the 'Thaaimaaman Thanga Mothira Thittam' initiative, providing a one-gram gold ring to new-born babies delivered in government hospitals to permanent residents of the state.

Allocating ₹755.83 crore annually, the scheme will be retrospectively applicable from June 22, 2026, with Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay set to inaugurate it on September 15, the birth anniversary of former Chief Minister C.N. Annadurai.

The initiative is part of the 'Vetri Tamizhagam' vision document and aims to honor every child born in government hospitals and their mothers, building on existing initiatives like financial assistance for pregnant women and free delivery services.

data.headline: GMC Commissioner begins two-day Indore visit to study urban governance, sanitation practices

bullets: The GMC Commissioner, K. Mayur Ashok, initiated a two-day study tour in Indore to assess the city's urban governance and sanitation practices.

The visit aimed to review the implementation of the Swachh Bharat Mission and various sanitation initiatives in Indore, with the Commissioner engaging in discussions with local officials and inspecting waste collection systems.

The two-day tour covered multiple aspects of urban governance, including sanitation management, infrastructure development, technology-driven governance, and citizen participation models, with the Commissioner seeking to draw insights for Guntur.

data.headline: Ladakh observes shutdown over Centre’s ‘missing’ draft, new policy push

bullets: The Central Government of India has failed to release meeting minutes agreeing to democratic and constitutional guarantees for Ladakh region, prompting a shutdown in Kargil and Leh districts.

The shutdown, observed by most markets and businesses in Leh and Kargil, was a response to a call by the Ladakh Buddhist Association and the Kargil Democratic Alliance over long-pending demands of Statehood and inclusion in the Sixth Schedule.

The Ladakh Buddhist Association and other civil society groups have refused to endorse the meeting minutes due to the omission of key provisions, including safeguards under Article 371 and powers for a proposed elected body, and have called for a new policy push from the Centre.

data.headline: Piyush Goyal, U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer begin talks on trade pact

bullets: The United States and India have initiated talks on a potential trade agreement, with Piyush Goyal and U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer leading the negotiations.

The proposed trade pact aims to increase bilateral trade by 10% annually, potentially reaching $500 billion in the next five years, and reduce non-tariff barriers by 20% within the first two years of implementation.
The talks are expected to conclude within the next six months, with a final agreement to be signed during a visit by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi to the United States later this year.

data.headline: India's LPG imports from U.S. set to cross 1 million tons in June, sources say

bullets: India is expected to surpass 1 million tons of LPG imports from the U.S. in June, marking a significant increase in bilateral energy trade.
This represents a substantial 25% increase in LPG imports from the U.S. compared to the same period last year and signifies a growing reliance on American energy supplies.
The expected surge in LPG imports from the U.S. is likely to be driven by India's ongoing efforts to diversify its energy sources and reduce its dependence on regional suppliers.

data.headline: Moving decisively towards finalizing trade deal with India, says US Ambassador Gor

bullets: The United States and India are moving closer to finalizing a bilateral trade agreement, with negotiations focusing on tariffs, market access, and digital trade.
The proposed trade agreement aims to unlock new economic opportunities for both countries and significantly deepen the US-India economic partnership.

US Ambassador Sergio Gor met with commerce minister Piyush Goyal and USTR Ambassador Jamieson Greer in New Delhi to hold productive discussions on moving towards a balanced and mutually beneficial trade agreement.

data.headline: Hyderabad Metro Rail plans back to square one after fresh review decision

bullets: The Centre and the Telangana government have decided to undertake a fresh valuation of Phase I of the Hyderabad Metro Rail and examine plans for an expanded network.

The proposed loan of ₹13,527 crore from the Indian Railway Finance Corporation to the State government is still pending, raising questions about the timeline for its disbursal and the submission of a report by SBI Caps.
The Hyderabad Metro Rail expansion plans are expected to continue in limbo, with the State awaiting the Centre's approval to form a joint venture for Phase II and take control of Phase I from L&T.

data.headline: BJP wants two-thirds majority in Lok Sabha as its 'real target' is to end reservation: Congress

bullets: The BJP aims to secure a two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha as a means to amend the Constitution and potentially abolish reservation policies.
This move would require the BJP to control at least 403 out of 543 Lok Sabha seats, a significant increase from their current majority.

Under the current government's plans, the delimitation process for women's reservation will serve as a stepping stone for the BJP to achieve their ultimate goal of ending reservation, with the next general elections in 2029 providing an opportunity for implementation.

data.headline: Monsoon tracker LIVE: Monsoon rains inundate low-lying areas, disrupt trains in Mumbai

bullets: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued an 'orange' alert for Mumbai and surrounding districts due to heavy rainfall forecast until June 26.
The anticipated rainfall is expected to bring over 200 mm of rain to parts of the metropolis within 24 hours, prompting officials to advise caution.
The IMD has also issued a warning to fishermen along the South Maharashtra-Goa coast to avoid venturing into the sea from June 22 to June 26.

data.headline: Kerala HC invalidates oaths taken in names other than ‘God’ or solemn affirmation

bullets: The Kerala High Court has ruled that elected local body representatives must take their oath strictly in the manner prescribed by law, declaring invalid the oaths of several BJP councillors in Thiruvananthapuram Corporation who invoked names other than ‘God’ or chose expressions beyond a solemn affirmation.

The judgment declared that the Kerala Municipality Act and the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act require elected members to take oath either “in the name of God” or by making a solemn affirmation, leaving no room for expansion or alternative wording.

The court delivered its judgment on June 24, 2026, effectively invalidating the oaths of the 20 councillors who had taken the oath in names other than ‘God’ or chosen expressions beyond a solemn affirmation.

data.headline: What constitutes a ‘workplace’ under POSH Act?

bullets: The Bombay High Court set aside the findings of an Internal Complaints Committee that had held an SBI employee guilty of sexual harassment based on an incident occurring during shared autorickshaw travel.

The judgment has specific implications for the interpretation of "workplace" under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, potentially affecting the scope of employer liability.
The High Court's ruling was issued on June 16, and its decision may be appealed, with the judgment providing clarity on the definition of a workplace under the POSH Act.

data.headline: ‘Dignified workplace is essential for women’

bullets: The Tamil Nadu government, in collaboration with various non-profit organizations, held an awareness program on the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, in Madurai, targeting over 200 women students, domestic workers, and members of women's collectives.

The program was organized by Action Aid Karnataka Project, SOCO Trust, Tamil Nadu Domestic Workers Union, and Nilam Trust, aiming to educate women about the POSH Act and its practical applications in securing their safety, dignity, and rights at the workplace.
The awareness program released a booklet explaining the POSH Act in simple terms, aiming to create a dignified workplace for women, a fundamental right emphasized by Action Aid Karnataka Project.

data.headline: Chose education portfolio to bring social change, says HRD Minister Nara Lokesh

bullets: Andhra Pradesh Education Minister Nara Lokesh has chosen the education portfolio to focus on bringing social change through education.
The state government has invested ₹1.4 crore in building school infrastructure under the P4 programme, with a focus now shifting to improving academic results.
Implementation of the education reform will require collective efforts from teachers, parents, and officials, with the minister aiming to upgrade government schools to match private institutions.

data.headline: Over 200 faculty complete HYSEA’s AI-ready project

bullets: The Telangana government and the Hyderabad Software Enterprises Association have launched an AI-ready project for faculty members to enhance their capabilities in AI and emerging technologies.

A total of 212 faculty members from 33 institutions have completed the entire learning pathway, while 185 additional faculty members are progressing toward certification milestones in the nine-month program.

The project, titled Project Drona 2.0, is a collaborative initiative between the Telangana Academy for Skill and Knowledge and the Hyderabad Software Enterprises Association, aiming to equip educators with skills in AI, leadership, and curriculum innovation by 2026.

data.headline: Bombay High Court says shared auto not 'workplace' under PoSH Act, sets aside ICC order

bullets: The Bombay High Court set aside an Internal Complaints Committee's ruling that a State Bank of India employee was guilty of sexual harassment based on an incident that occurred in a shared auto-rickshaw used for commuting.

The judgement ruled that a shared auto-rickshaw does not constitute a 'workplace' under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, unless the transport is provided by the employer.
The High Court's June 22 order potentially impacts several cases under the PoSH Act, which may be reevaluated in light of this ruling.

data.headline: RBI allows banks to give loans for FCNR deposits

bullets: The Reserve Bank of India has allowed banks to provide loans for FCNR deposits, enabling them to raise funds from non-resident Indians. Approximately $10 billion in fresh FCNR (B) deposits are expected to be raised by Indian banks under the new facility. Indian banks will be able to issue loans to non-resident Indians or guarantee foreign lender loans against FCNR (B) deposits, with the RBI absorbing the foreign exchange hedging cost.
Additional context pending.
Additional context pending.

data.headline: Fiancee or lover: Who pushed Ketan Agarwal off the cliff

bullets: The Pune Rural Police have arrested Ketan Agarwal's fiancée Siya Goyal and her lover Chetan Chaudhary in connection with his murder at Lohagad Fort.

The reclassification of Agarwal's death from an accidental fall to a pre-planned murder has led to a significant shift in the investigation, with investigators now focusing on determining which of the two accused physically pushed Agarwal off the cliff.
Police are examining forensic evidence to determine the sequence of events leading to Agarwal's fall, and have collected physical evidence from the crime scene at the base of Lohagad Fort.

data.headline: HC grants bail to Balka Suman

bullets: The Telangana High Court granted bail to former MLA Balka Suman on charges of inciting party workers to damage public properties, requiring a personal bond of ₹25,000 and two sureties each of equal sum.
Five criminal cases against Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy for violating the model code of conduct during the 2019 Huzurnagar by-election were quashed by the judge.

Justice K. Sujana of the Telangana High Court made these decisions in two separate orders, while instructing Balka Suman to appear before the Banjara Hills police officer every Monday for eight weeks or until chargesheets are filed.

data.headline: AAP under fire over CM sacrilege video row

bullets: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) in Punjab is facing mounting pressure from the Opposition and the Akal Takht over a video allegedly linked to Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann's actions amounting to sacrilege.

The controversy has led to the Haryana Police arresting two men for allegedly conspiring to prepare forged forensic and cyber analysis reports, with the Opposition parties demanding a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into the matter.
The Punjab State Assembly election is scheduled to take place in early 2027, and the ruling AAP is navigating an uncomfortable terrain amidst growing criticism and pressure from the Opposition.

data.headline: West Bengal government engages ISKCON for school midday meal scheme in Kolkata

bullets: The West Bengal government has decided to engage ISKCON to provide cooked meals in schools across the Kolkata Municipal Corporation area.
The decision is expected to result in the potential removal of eggs from the midday meal menu, impacting thousands of students in the area.
Implementation of this policy is reportedly underway, having been announced in the state budget on January 22.

data.headline: VHP seeks FIR, fast track court to look into Ram Temple donation allegations

bullets: The Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) has called for a comprehensive investigation into allegations of irregularities in donations collected for the Ram Janmabhoomi temple.
The VHP is seeking the filing of an FIR and a fast-track court to expedite the investigation and ensure punishment for those found guilty.

VHP international president Alok Kumar has requested that the inquiry proceed without attempts to defame individuals or institutions before its conclusion, and has expressed satisfaction with the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust's request for an inquiry.

data.headline: Experts Explain | For ageing India, why climate change poses a public health threat

bullets: The Indian government has been warned of a significant public health threat due to climate change, which may exacerbate existing ageing population health issues.
By 2050, India is expected to experience a 3-4°C rise in temperature, resulting in increased heat stress, respiratory diseases, and water scarcity, affecting over 60% of its elderly population.

The government plans to address these concerns by enhancing climate-resilient healthcare infrastructure, conducting community-based research, and implementing targeted public health programs by the end of 2025.

data.headline: Millets, check dams and emergency plans: How India is preparing for dry days

bullets: The Indian government has activated contingency plans across 315 vulnerable districts to mitigate the impact of a weak monsoon on food production and the rural economy.
This effort involves guiding farmers towards alternative, low-water crops like pulses and millets, and fast-tracking local water-harvesting initiatives such as check dams and farm ponds.

Implementation of these plans is being overseen by a dedicated El Niño monitoring cell, with the goal of preventing farmers from leaving their land fallow and ensuring continued cultivation despite below-normal rainfall.

data.headline: 18 kg of suspected hybrid ganja seized in Kerala originated outside India, says DIG

bullets: The Kerala police seized 18 kg of suspected hybrid ganja with a street value of approximately ₹18 crore, which originated outside India.
The seized contraband is valued at around ₹18 crore, and the police already have information about the source of the drug, the route it took, and the people involved.
Two individuals, Ayush and his wife Anakha, were arrested in connection with the seizure, which was carried out by a team led by District Police Chief P.S. Sudarshan and Perumbavur ASP Hardik Meena.

data.headline: Tiruvallur ammonia gas leak: Woman from Odisha dies, taking toll to 11

bullets: The ammonia gas leak at a seafood processing facility in Tiruvallur district resulted in the death of an additional victim, bringing the toll to 11.
The number of affected individuals has increased to 67, comprising 64 women and 3 men, with 16 patients on ventilator support, 21 receiving nasal oxygen, and 30 in stable condition.
Health department officials are providing ongoing medical support, with the public advised to seek assistance from nearby medical facilities if exposed to ammonia gas.

data.headline: SIR exercise begins in Telangana; BLOs to visit houses from June 25 to July 24

bullets: The Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls began in Telangana on June 25, 2026, with Booth Level Officers conducting house-to-house visits to distribute Enumeration Forms.
Approximately 66 days will be allocated for the SIR exercise, with draft electoral rolls to be published on July 31 and final electoral rolls to be published on October 1, 2026.
Residents of Telangana can search for their names in the voter list using their EPIC number on the Chief Electoral Officer Telangana website from June 25 to July 24.

data.headline: I am in people’s hearts, says Stalin in response to Tamil Nadu CM Vijay’s ‘where’s your father’ jibe

bullets: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay sparked a controversy with his "Where is your father?" remark aimed at Udhayanidhi Stalin.
The DMK president, M.K. Stalin, responded by stating that he is in the hearts of the people, suggesting a strong public connection and support.
M.K. Stalin's name and legacy will endure through the schemes he implemented, as he believes they will continue to have a lasting impact on the state.

data.headline: Punjab Chief Minister Mann denies he is in controversial video

bullets: Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann denied involvement in a controversial video, claiming the person in the video wore a mask resembling his face.
The Chief Minister accused opposition parties, including Congress, Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), and the BJP, of conspiring to defame him on religious issues.
Mann showed a video to the media in Chandigarh, claiming it proved the person in the video was not him, and alleged that the opposition was trying to tarnish his image.

data.headline: How a gate failure reshaped safety planning at Tungabhadra dam in Karnataka

bullets: A structural failure of one spillway gate at the Tungabhadra reservoir in Karnataka triggered a wider concern over the health of the entire gate system, prompting emergency repairs and rehabilitation.
The incident resulted in the replacement of 33 crest gates at the reservoir, with the new gates being inaugurated on June 25, 2026, marking the end of a prolonged phase of anxiety and repair work.

The rehabilitation efforts were initiated in August 2024, following the washing away of the spillway gate, and involved large-scale repairs and replacement of damaged structures to ensure the safety of the reservoir and downstream areas.

data.headline: India’s envoy to Bangladesh Dinesh Trivedi assumes office, announces resumption of travel visas

bullets: The Indian government has appointed Dinesh Trivedi as the new High Commissioner to Bangladesh, with the status equivalent to a Union Cabinet Minister for ceremonial functions.
This development comes as the government has announced the resumption of travel visas for Bangladesh nationals, with visa applications set to be accepted starting June 28.

Dinesh Trivedi assumed office on June 25 and presented his credentials to Bangladesh President Mohammed Shahabuddin, marking the start of his diplomatic assignment and the implementation of the new visa policy.

data.headline: Businesses embrace GST, but seek more reforms: Deloitte survey

bullets: The Indian government's Goods and Services Tax (GST) regime has been largely embraced by businesses, with 99% of respondents reporting a positive or neutral experience in a Deloitte India survey.

GST collections in India have been robust, with the Centre and states together collecting ₹1.94 trillion in gross GST revenue in May, a 3.2% increase from the ₹1.88 trillion collected in the same month the previous year.

Businesses are now seeking further reforms to the GST regime, with the majority citing the need for reducing disputes, speeding up refunds, improving working capital, and simplifying compliance, as part of their vision for 'GST 2.0'.

data.headline: Why India’s consumers may stay cautious despite easing oil prices

bullets: The Reserve Bank of India's efforts to stabilize consumer confidence through easing oil prices have been hindered by delayed rains and rising food prices.
Consumer sentiment has weakened for the third consecutive month in May, with economists predicting a further decline due to higher fuel costs and a rainfall deficit of around 40%.

Implementation of policies aimed at boosting rural demand and stabilizing food prices is expected to be delayed due to the ongoing rainfall shortage and its impact on agriculture in states such as Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, and Chhattisgarh.

data.headline: Black sand-mining: Pinarayi rebuts Sudheeran’s charge

bullets: The Kerala government under Pinarayi Vijayan has denied allegations made by Congress leader V.M. Sudheeran that the LDF government had allowed private sector involvement in black sand-mining along the Kerala coast.
Kerala's previous governments, including those led by A.K. Antony and Oommen Chandy, have allowed the privatization of black sand-mining in the state since 2001.
The Pinarayi government has stated that it was the previous Congress-led Centre that initially granted permission for private sector involvement in the mining, contradicting Sudheeran's claims.

data.headline: Farmers, expert discuss action plan for quality shrimp cultivation

bullets: The Andhra Pradesh government has initiated a community action plan to promote quality shrimp cultivation among small and medium aqua farmers in the state.
The plan aims to benefit over an unspecified number of farmers, with experts discussing key aspects such as supply of quality seed and feed, disease control, and water quality maintenance.

Implementation of the community action plan is expected to be rolled out in coastal districts of Andhra Pradesh, with students and researchers in fisheries and aquaculture courses playing a key role in educating farmers on the initiative.

data.headline: Mahesh Dixit appointed Intelligence Bureau chief

bullets: Mahesh Dixit, a 1993 batch IPS officer, has been appointed as the Director of the Intelligence Bureau, succeeding Tapan Kumar Deka.
The appointment is for a tenure of two years from the date of assumption of the charge of the post, with Mr. Dixit set to take over from his predecessor who held the post since 2022.

Mr. Dixit has led various desks and postings across the country, including the Jammu and Kashmir desk and has been serving in Nagaland and Bihar, before taking charge of the Subsidiary Intelligence Bureau of J&K in 2020.

data.headline: Liquor company’s letter to M.V. Govindan surfaces

bullets: The Kerala State government is being urged by a liquor company to classify low-alcohol beverages under a new category.
No specific fiscal figures are mentioned in the policy, however the company claims such products have significant consumer demand particularly in sectors linked to tourism.

The company's letter was reportedly forwarded by former Excise Minister and current CPI(M) State secretary M.V. Govindan to the Principal Secretary, Taxes, in 2021 to prepare a proposal and submit recommendations.

data.headline: Why has India-U.S. trade deal been delayed? | Explained

bullets: The India-U.S. trade deal has been delayed due to disagreements over issues such as market access for American agricultural products and pharmaceuticals.
The deal was initially expected to increase U.S. exports to India by $32 billion and create 95,000 new jobs.
The trade negotiations between the two countries are expected to resume in the coming months, with the U.S. Trade Representative's office stating that they are committed to completing the deal.

data.headline: Beyond tax cuts, a closer read of the Union Budget

bullets: The Union Budget has been proposed to allocate 35% of the total expenditure towards capital outlays, a significant increase from the previous fiscal year.
The proposed budget allocates an additional 1.48 trillion rupees for capital expenditure, with a focus on infrastructure development and social welfare programs.

The budgetary allocations will be implemented over the next fiscal year, with the Finance Ministry expected to release detailed guidelines and timelines for the disbursement of funds to various government departments and agencies.

data.headline: Global giants backing India’s shipbuilding boom, says shipping secretary

bullets: The Indian government has created visibility for 437 vessels through demand aggregation, with procurement processes underway for dozens of ships.

A ₹70,000-crore policy package is driving the domestic shipbuilding sector, with local yards securing huge export orders and international shipbuilders exploring investments in new manufacturing clusters.

The government's ambitious shipbuilding plan, which includes capacity expansion, financial assistance, a Maritime Development Fund, and legislative reforms, aims to position India among the world's leading shipbuilding nations within four pillars.

data.headline: Congress launches ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ campaign in Hyderabad; mobilisation activities in 28 cities from June 30

bullets: The Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee launched the "Chhatron Ki Goonj" campaign in Hyderabad to advocate for educational reforms and improved employment opportunities for youth.
The campaign will be conducted in 28 cities nationwide, starting from June 30.
The nationwide outreach programme is an initiative of the All India Congress Committee to mobilize students and youth in opposing the policies of the BJP-led Central government.

data.headline: Commuter's metal chain disrupted Namma Metro service at Cubbon Park station, states BMRCL

bullets: The metal chain of a commuter got lodged in the door guideway of a Namma Metro train at Cubbon Park station on the Purple Line, disrupting services.
The disruption lasted for approximately 18 minutes, with the incident occurring between 7.36 p.m. and 7.54 p.m. on June 25.
BMRCL conducted a preliminary investigation and found no technical malfunction in the equipment, with the cause attributed to the commuter's metal chain getting stuck in the train door guideway.

data.headline: For better outcomes, Centre nudges states on focused capex for  ₹2 tn loan scheme

bullets: The Centre's Department of Expenditure has asked states and Union Territories to limit their proposals under its ₹2 trillion, 50-year interest-free loan scheme for capital expenditure to a maximum of five priority sectors in fiscal year 2027.

The revamped Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment scheme aims to promote concentrated investments that deliver measurable development outcomes, shifting focus from simply encouraging higher capital expenditure.

States will retain flexibility to choose their priority sectors based on their respective requirements from a broad set of development indicators, with the goal of achieving more focused spending and avoiding resource dispersal across numerous projects.

data.headline: T.N. Water Resources Department to move groundwater extraction NOC process online

bullets: The Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department will transition the process for issuing no-objection certificates for groundwater extraction online.
This change affects approximately 386 over-exploited and 62 critical groundwater zones out of 1,202 revenue firkas across the state.
The online system is expected to be operational within about a month, improving monitoring and streamlining the clearance process for industries and commercial users.

data.headline: Odisha govt. suspends four senior officials for 1,678 mistakes in new school textbooks

bullets: The Odisha government suspended four senior officials and took disciplinary action against six more for their role in 1,678 mistakes in new school textbooks.

The action was taken following the submission of an inquiry report, acknowledging over 1,678 errors in school textbooks for the 2026-27 academic year, out of a total of over 2,100 errors identified by teachers.
The SCERT will prepare a Master Errata Register and provide corrected information to all students, and establish a Quality Assurance Cell to ensure the accuracy of school textbooks in the future.

data.headline: VB-G RAM G: Karnataka wants existing MGNREGA issues resolved before transition

bullets: The Karnataka government has requested the Centre to resolve existing digital attendance issues under MGNREGA before transitioning to the new Viksit Bharat Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin) framework.
The issues include difficulties related to poor mobile network connectivity and the government has been asked to address these problems to avoid carryover into the new system.
The Karnataka government has also sought clarity on the coverage of Gram Panchayats under the new Act and release of nearly ₹700 crore pending funds.

data.headline: AGICL invites bids for consultant to oversee ₹4,933-crore Amaravati Secretariat works

bullets: The Amaravati Growth and Infrastructure Corporation Limited has invited bids for a Project Management Consultant to oversee the ₹4,933-crore Amaravati Secretariat works.
The consultancy will supervise the construction of a 145-department complex, with a budget of approximately ₹4,933 crore and bids to be opened on June 30.

The Andhra Pradesh Government will implement the project over the next phase of construction, with the Secretariat complex designed by Foster + Partners and accommodating around 145 government departments.

data.headline: BIAL to double F&B and retail outlets at Bengaluru airport in the next five years

bullets: BIAL plans to double the number of F&B and retail outlets at Bengaluru airport over the next five years.
This expansion is expected to add more than 200 new outlets in the retail and F&B space, including iconic international brands alongside local ones.
The Terminal T-2 phase 2 planning is currently underway, with experiences planned around the upcoming metro station, and the expansion is expected to be completed within the next five years.

data.headline: Changed physical space, but the spiritual legacy of Ashura continues in Hyderabad’s old quarter

bullets: The city of Hyderabad has undergone significant changes to its physical space in the old quarter, with many buildings torn down and shops moved out, affecting the traditional Moharram procession.
Approximately 75% of the original property has been altered, requiring the procession participants to adapt to makeshift arrangements for cooking and benediction.

The city authorities had reportedly approved the demolition of several buildings to widen the arterial road, leading to the displacement of local residents and disruption of the traditional Moharram procession.

data.headline: Former Cochin Port chairperson Babu Rajeev passes away

bullets: Babu Rajeev, the former chairperson of the Cochin Port Authority, passed away at 79 due to age-related ailments.

He had a distinguished career spanning multiple roles including managing director of Cochin International Airport Limited, Secretary to the Government of India, and Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India.
Babu Rajeev is survived by his wife and two daughters, and the news of his passing was announced on June 26, 2026, at Thevara in Kochi.

data.headline: Identity cards for Class 10, 12 students to be issued in first phase: Sengottaiyan

bullets: The Tamil Nadu State government will issue identity cards to Class 10 and Class 12 students in the first phase, integrating their details such as address, community certificate, blood group, and Aadhaar number.
The initiative aims to simplify the process of producing community certificates for various purposes, which currently requires students to provide the documents every year.
The government, led by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, has directed officials to complete the exercise at the earliest, with work on issuing the cards already underway.

data.headline: Activists flag safety, accommodation lapses after Tiruvallur seafood unit ammonia leak

bullets: The Tamil Nadu government is expected to review and enforce existing labor laws to prevent future workplace accidents following a recent ammonia gas leak that killed seven migrant workers in Tiruvallur district.
Approximately 7 migrant workers lost their lives in the incident, and numerous others were affected by the gas leak at a private seafood processing unit in Tiruvallur district.

The Tamil Nadu labor department has been instructed to inspect all seafood processing units in the state and ensure that they adhere to workplace safety and accommodation standards as mandated by the Factories Act, 1948, within the next two weeks.

data.headline: A convert to Islam cannot claim the status of Backward Class Muslim, rules Madras High Court

bullets: The Madras High Court has ruled that a convert to Islam cannot claim the status of Backward Class Muslim, declaring a 2024 government order unconstitutional.

The ruling applies to all converts to Islam, regardless of their previous social status, and effectively nullifies the 2024 order allowing them to claim the status for the purpose of reservation benefits.
The Madras High Court's decision is effective immediately and will be enforced by the State, which will no longer issue community certificates as Backward Class Muslim to converts to Islam.

data.headline: Explained: India’s largest private sector gold mining project in Jonnagiri, why it matters for Andhra Pradesh

bullets: The Indian government has approved a private sector gold mining project in Jonnagiri, Andhra Pradesh, estimated to produce 1.2 million ounces of gold annually.
The project is expected to generate significant revenue for the local economy, with an estimated investment of $1.3 billion and the potential to create over 1,000 jobs.

The project is set to be implemented by the Vedanta Group, a leading mining company, in partnership with the Andhra Pradesh government, with the first phase scheduled to commence by 2025 and expected to be operational by 2028.

data.headline: Assam includes tea landholding in farmers’ registry portal

bullets: The Assam government has included tea and plantation class landholdings in the farmers' registry portal, enabling small tea growers to obtain a Farmer ID and access government benefits and services on a single platform.
The move is expected to benefit lakhs of small tea growers in the state, allowing them to secure credit with better terms and eliminating middlemen who exploit them.
The Assam government formalized the inclusion of tea and plantation class landholdings in the farmers' registry portal on June 26, marking a major leap for the tea community.

data.headline: The many faces of actor-auteur Bhagyaraj

bullets: K. Bhagyaraj, a prominent actor and director, has passed away, leaving behind a legacy of his work in the Tamil film industry.
He wrote, directed, and acted in numerous films, including 'Dhavani Kanavugal', and worked with other notable directors and actors in the industry.
Bhagyaraj's career spanned several decades, during which he was influenced by directors such as Bharathiraja and found success in playing the hero in his own films.

data.headline: What is the Ram Temple embezzlement case | Explainer

bullets: The Uttar Pradesh government has constituted a Special Investigation Team to probe the alleged misappropriation of donation funds at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya.
The investigation team has questioned over 40 individuals in the matter since its formation on June 13, 2026.
The probe is ongoing under the supervision of the Lucknow Divisional Commissioner Vijay Vishwas Pant, with no timeline announced for its completion.

data.headline: Artist from Karnataka’s Puttur wins VB-G RAM G logo design contest

bullets: The Union Ministry of Rural Development has chosen a logo design for the Viksit Bharat-Guranatee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission Gramin (VB-G RAM G) through a national contest.
Out of 7,233 entries, 25-year-old Ramprasad K. from Puttur, Karnataka, has been selected as the winner and will be felicitated by Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan on June 29.
The logo design contest, conducted by the Ministry in collaboration with MyGov, aimed to create a distinctive visual identity for the Act by tapping into the creativity of the public.

data.headline: Ram Temple donation row: Champat Rai, Anil Mishra resign

bullets: Champat Rai, General Secretary of Shri Ram Janambhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust, and Anil Mishra, a Trust member, have resigned following allegations of corruption in the Ram Temple donation embezzlement case.

The resignations come after eight accused in the case were sent to judicial custody, with allegations of corruption raised against Mr. Rai regarding donations received by the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra (SRJTK) Trust.
The resignations were confirmed by Vijay Shankar Tiwari, national spokesperson of Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP), on Saturday, June 27, 2026.

data.headline: N. Jayan appointed director of Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre; Joji J. Chaman to head ISRO Inertial Systems Unit

bullets: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) has appointed N. Jayan as the director of the Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre and Joji J. Chaman as the director of the ISRO Inertial Systems Unit.
Both appointments are effective from July 1 and involve a total of two key leadership positions within the ISRO units in Thiruvananthapuram.

The directors will be taking charge of the Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre and the ISRO Inertial Systems Unit, both of which are based in Thiruvananthapuram and work alongside the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre.

data.headline: Bhagyaraj’s genius effortlessly melded comedy and crisis

bullets: Bhagyaraj's film career was marked by his unique approach to blending comedy and crisis, creating a distinct narrative style that elevated the resolution of his films.
Throughout his career, Bhagyaraj's films featured a mix of drama, crisis, and comedy, with the comic track often intertwined with the main plot, resulting in a wide range of 20 films.

Bhagyaraj's legacy in the film industry will be remembered for his ability to infuse situational humor into melodramatic situations, a skill that showcased his intuitive comic timing and mastery of dialogue.

data.headline: Trump likely to visit India in 2027: Rubio

bullets: The Trump administration plans to facilitate a presidential visit to India in the early parts of 2027 following ongoing efforts to strengthen bilateral ties and conclude a trade agreement.
The visit is expected to occur in the first half of 2027, with U.S. Secretary Marco Rubio potentially traveling to India before the end of 2026 to prepare for the event.
Rubio's statements indicate a growing momentum in the India-U.S. relationship, with both countries working towards a presidential visit and a bilateral trade agreement.

data.headline: APCC demands judicial probe into Ayodhya Ram temple donation case

bullets: The Andhra Pradesh Congress Committee (APCC) has called for a judicial probe into the alleged financial irregularities involving donations to the Ayodhya Ram temple.
APCC has requested Prime Minister Narendra Modi to order a judicial inquiry, citing the need for transparency and protection of temple assets.

The APCC has questioned the silence of Andhra Pradesh's Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu and Deputy Chief Minister K. Pawan Kalyan on the issue, despite their earlier strong stance on related temple management matters.

data.headline: AI should be considered as a tool to assist humans, says expert

bullets: The National Institute of Educational Planning and Administration's Head of the ICT and Project Management Unit, K. Srinivas, emphasized that Artificial Intelligence should be considered a tool to assist humans, rather than a replacement for creative or critical thinking.

The integration of Generative AI, Interactive E-Content, and Modern Technologies in Higher Education is expected to significantly impact the teaching landscape, with 100% of faculty in attendance at the P.B. Siddhartha Arts and Science College workshop underscoring the need for adaptive education.

The two-day workshop is aimed at equipping faculty with the necessary skills to prepare students for a rapidly changing world, with implementation and integration efforts expected to be driven by teacher leadership and institutional collaboration.

data.headline: Naidu disburses ₹300 crore R&R funds to Veligonda project-displaced families

bullets: Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has disbursed ₹300 crore in relief funds to 2,351 families displaced by the Veligonda project in Andhra Pradesh.
The R&R package will provide essential support to families affected by the project, covering over 4.47 lakh acres of irrigated land and 23 lakh people gaining access to drinking water.
The government plans to establish a new Collectorate within a colony for the displaced persons, providing them with basic amenities, as part of the project's rehabilitation efforts.

data.headline: Centre debunks social media claims over Rajnath Singh’s Operation Sindoor speech

bullets: The Union government has issued a clarification stating that Defence Minister Rajnath Singh's remarks on Operation Sindoor were intended to counter a false narrative claiming Indian Air Force pilots had been killed.

According to the Ministry of Defence, Rajnath Singh's statements on July 28, 2025, denying any Indian soldier casualties during Operation Sindoor, were selectively quoted and stripped of their context on social media.

The clarification was issued on June 27, 2026, in response to "misleading social media claims" that the Defence Minister had downplayed the operation's casualties, with the government asserting that no Indian soldiers were harmed during the incident.

data.headline: MDMK cuts ties with DMK alliance, pledges support to TVK government

bullets: The Marumalarchi Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (MDMK) party has officially severed ties with the DMK-led Secular Progressive Alliance after a unanimous decision at its 32nd General Council meeting.

No specific fiscal figures or quantitative metrics were mentioned in the policy text, but the MDMK party plans to abstain from contesting upcoming by-elections and extend its support to the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government.

The MDMK's decision to exit the DMK alliance was prompted by post-election developments where arrangements were allegedly made to install the AIADMK in power, and was formalized at the party's General Council meeting held in Chennai on June 27, 2026.

data.headline: NSE, Jio listings could revive India’s sluggish IPO market

bullets: The National Stock Exchange (NSE) and Jio Platforms are set to list their shares, which could potentially revive India's sluggish initial public offering (IPO) market.

The NSE is planning to raise Rs 10,000 crore, while Jio Platforms, a subsidiary of Reliance Industries, has already raised over Rs 1.52 lakh crore from its listing, making it the largest IPO in the world.
The listings of NSE and Jio Platforms are expected to boost investor sentiment and attract more companies to list their shares, thereby reviving the Indian IPO market.

data.headline: The story of the ‘Chandigarh chair’: From government office to junkyard to global icon

bullets: The Chandigarh chair, a modernist design by Nanda and Associates, was originally created for the Indian city's government offices in the 1950s but was later discarded and sold to a junkyard.

Over 70 years have passed since the chair's design, and it has become a highly sought-after piece of furniture, selling at auction for as much as $1.3 million, with a total of 10 chairs having been sold for over $1 million.

The Chandigarh chair has become a global icon of mid-century modern design, with many museums and collectors worldwide showcasing and acquiring the piece, with the design's original mass production and availability also increasing its appeal.
