data.headline: The week in charts: Weak core output, Russian crude imports, AI edge

bullets: India's core sector output growth slowed down to 0.5% in May, marking its weakest pace in seven months and contrasting with the 1.8% growth in April.
Five of the eight core industries contracted in May, with coal recording the steepest decline of 9.3% and extending its negative trend to a fourth consecutive month.
The core sector growth remains subdued, with only electricity, cement, and steel industries showing positive growth, led by electricity with an 8.7% increase in May.

data.headline: YSRCP’s fight is for power and ours is for public service, says A.P. Minister Kandula Durgesh

bullets: The Minister of Tourism in Andhra Pradesh, Kandula Durgesh, has publicly criticized the YSR Congress Party for its perceived divisive agenda and irresponsible statements.

The YSR Congress Party's criticisms of the Jana Sena Party and its leaders are seen as attempts to provoke the public, with Minister Durgesh asserting that the party's leaders are driven by a desire for power rather than public service.
Minister Durgesh's statement comes in response to recent remarks by YSR Congress Party leaders, including criticism of Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu and Deputy Chief Minister K. Pawan Kalyan.

data.headline: Inside Tiruvallur’s ammonia gas leak nightmare

bullets: A government committee has recommended the permanent closure of the company where an ammonia gas leak has claimed 16 lives so far.
The incident highlights serious concerns about industrial safety, emergency preparedness, and the conditions of migrants employed far away from home.
The committee's recommendation for permanent closure is likely to be implemented under existing regulations governing workplace safety and environmental protection in India.

data.headline: Bhagyaraj’s last rites conducted with full State honours | LIVE

bullets: The Indian government has not announced any new policy in relation to the content, but rather a news report about the death of Tamil actor and director K. Bhagyaraj.
The news report does not provide any specific quantitative metrics or fiscal figures.
The implementation details of the report, if any, are not present in the provided information.

data.headline: ‘Blatant loot’: Congress on MoS Agriculture getting subsidy from own ministry

bullets: The Union Minister of State for Agriculture, Bhagirath Choudhary, has been accused by the Congress party of approving a ₹99.03 lakh subsidy for his own commercial farm, which they have termed as a case of "blatant loot" and conflict of interest.

This alleged incident is the latest in a series of corruption charges leveled against the BJP-led government, with the Congress party questioning the government's claims of zero tolerance for corruption.

The Congress party has also criticized the Prime Minister for his silence on the issue, with party leader Pawan Khera accusing the government of being corrupt and only providing subsidies to its own members, as exemplified by the "subsidy beginning at home" in this case.

data.headline: Mint Explainer | Will water shortages derail India’s AI Data Centre boom?

bullets: India is racing to establish itself as a leading AI data centre hub, offering tax breaks and attracting billions in foreign investment.

The construction of data centres in India, particularly in water-stressed states like Maharashtra, poses significant water consumption concerns, with cooling technologies potentially unable to alleviate these issues.

Implementation of sustainable practices and water-saving technologies is crucial to ensure the growth of India's AI data centre industry does not come at the cost of exacerbating water scarcity in the country.

data.headline: Attempts to weaken Congress through controversies will not succeed, says Thrissur DCC chief Joseph Tajet

bullets: The Thrissur District Congress Committee (DCC) president Joseph Tajet has dismissed allegations against the party over the Mattathur grama panchayat issue, stating attempts to weaken the organisation through controversies will not succeed.

The expelled leaders who have made the allegations have been removed from the party for alleged betrayal and have lost credibility within the Congress and among the public, with 100% of their party membership withdrawn.

Joseph Tajet's statement was released on June 27, 2026, in response to the allegations made by the expelled leaders, who he said had entered into a secret understanding with the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in Mattathur.

data.headline: Health Ministry to launch revised Anaemia Mukt Bharat guidelines

bullets: The Union Health Ministry is set to launch revised operational guidelines for the Anaemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan on June 29, 2026, which will expand the national programme's strategy to include a new beneficiary group and digital tracking of beneficiaries. The revised guidelines are expected to strengthen anaemia control through improved testing, treatment, monitoring, and community participation, and will introduce a 7x7x7 framework, expanding the existing 6x6x6 strategy. The new guidelines will be released by Union Health Minister J.P. Nadda during the 16th meeting of the Central Council of Health and Family Welfare at Vigyan Bhawan.
Additional context pending.

data.headline: Gold worth ₹10 lakh missing from Karipur police station in Malappuram; former SHO under scanner

bullets: The Karipur police station in Malappuram reported a missing gold valued at approximately ₹10 lakh after an internal inquiry implicated a suspended former Station House Officer.
The gold ornaments, which were kept in custody for safekeeping, were discovered missing after a Special Branch report flagged the issue in February.
An investigation led by DySP, Kondotty, is ongoing, with the suspended officer allegedly admitting to possessing the missing gold during questioning.

data.headline: Activists’ body urges NCPCR to take action against T.N. Minister Viswanathan for touching girl athletes’ legs

bullets: The Tamil Nadu Child Rights Watch has filed a complaint against Higher Education Minister P. Viswanathan for allegedly touching the legs of girl athletes at a school programme in Madurai.
The TNCRW has requested the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights to take suo moto cognisance of the case and demanded a report from the State government regarding the incident.

The TNCRW has expressed concerns that the matter requires prompt and transparent scrutiny to maintain public confidence in child protection mechanisms, highlighting the State's fundamental obligation to protect children.

data.headline: Seven accused nabbed by Bengaluru CCB planned revenge killing of history-sheeter

bullets: The Central Crime Branch in Bengaluru City arrested seven individuals for conspiring to murder a history-sheeter in a revenge plot.

The arrests followed intelligence collection regarding criminal activities within the Ashok Nagar police station limits, where the accused allegedly procured illegal weapons and formed a gang to carry out the attack.
The operation, led by Inspector S. Mahadevaiah, was conducted by the Organised Crime Wing (West Division) as part of ongoing efforts to combat organized crime in the region.

data.headline: Iranian oil may return, but Indian refiners eye concessions

bullets: The US Treasury Department's Office of Foreign Assets Control has issued a 60-day sanctions waiver allowing the production, sale, and transport of Iranian crude and petroleum products until 21 August 2026.

Indian refiners imported approximately 133,000 barrels per day of Iranian crude in April and are awaiting sweeter terms from Tehran, including deferred payments and longer credit periods, to regain market share in India.

Indian refiners are taking a long-term approach to procure Iranian crude and are waiting for clarity on payment mechanisms and the durability of US-Iran peace talks before making any immediate purchases.

data.headline: PGRS cancelled on Monday owing to President’s visit

bullets: The Public Grievance Redressal System (PGRS) program scheduled for Visakhapatnam on Monday was cancelled due to preparations for the President's visit on June 30.
No specific quantitative metrics or fiscal figures were mentioned in the policy text regarding the cancellation of PGRS.

The cancellation of PGRS was announced by District Collector M. Abhishikth Kishore, who appealed to the public and complainants to cooperate with the district administration amidst preparations for the President's visit on June 30.

data.headline: State to promote e-cooking in hotels and cloud kitchens

bullets: The Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation Limited will prioritize applications seeking new service connection or loan enhancement for electric cooking in hotels, cloud kitchens, and other commercial establishments.

The TNPDCL aims to accelerate the adoption of e-cooking in the state, with plans to fast-track new electricity connection/load enhancement requests from commercial and institutional establishments, and upgrade capacity on priority.

Applications for new service or load enhancement for e-cooking will undergo a simplified online application process on the Distribution Company portal, with Chief Engineers instructed to provide priority processing.

data.headline: Stalin accuses TVK-led government of not addressing power cuts, farmers’ problems

bullets: The TVK-led government in Tamil Nadu is facing criticism from DMK president M.K. Stalin for failing to address pressing issues such as power outages and farmers' protests.

The DMK claims that during their previous governance, Tamil Nadu achieved new heights in several sectors, becoming the second-largest economy in India, with investors from across the country and around the world investing in the State.

The DMK president has also accused the ruling party of deteriorating law and order in the State, citing a rise in sexual abuse cases, narcotic drug menace, and robberies, with some members of the ruling party being accused in these crimes.

data.headline: Telangana CM presents Rugby Premier League trophy as Hyderabad Heroes win Season 2 title

bullets: Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy presented the HSBC Rugby Premier League Season 2 trophy to Hyderabad Heroes after they defeated Mumbai Dreamers 41-17 in the final at Gachibowli Stadium in Hyderabad on Sunday.

A total of ₹75 lakh in prize money was distributed among the teams, with Chennai Bulls finishing third after being defeated in the play-off, and receiving ₹15 lakh, Mumbai Dreamers receiving ₹25 lakh, and Hyderabad Heroes receiving ₹45 lakh.

The HSBC Rugby Premier League Season 2 featured six men's franchises competing in 34 matches over 13 days in Hyderabad, with a total of 84 players participating, including 54 international players from 19 countries and 30 Indian players.

data.headline: Commerce Ministry convenes stakeholders' meet on June 30 on SEZ issues

bullets: The Commerce Ministry will hold a stakeholders' meeting on June 30 to discuss ongoing issues and concerns related to Special Economic Zones (SEZs) nationwide.
Over 50 representatives from various industries and sectors have been invited to attend the meeting, including officials from the Commerce Ministry, SEZ developers, and industry associations.
The meeting aims to address key issues such as simplification of SEZ procedures, clarifying tax exemptions, and facilitating greater foreign investment in these zones.

data.headline: AI job apocalypse ‘unlikely,' could create new opportunities over time: Goldman Sachs report

bullets: A new Goldman Sachs report suggests that the feared AI-driven job apocalypse is unlikely to occur, predicting instead that labor market disruption will lead to new employment opportunities over time.
The report estimates that approximately 9% of the labor force, or around 15 million workers, could be displaced during a 10-year AI transition period.

Implementation of AI technologies and creation of new job opportunities are expected to advance over the coming decade, according to a Goldman Sachs report predicting a moderate impact on labor markets.

data.headline: Ram Temple embezzlement row: Supreme Court urged to secure digital evidence before it is ‘quietly lost’

bullets: The Supreme Court has been urged to secure digital evidence in the Ram Temple embezzlement case before it can be lost or tampered with.
The court has been informed that the petition will not be taken up until the summer vacation ends on July 12.
Advocate N.K. Goswami has expressed concern that electronic evidence like CCTV footage can be erased or modified during the delay, potentially denying justice.

data.headline: Four held in Ujjain for blowing up car in Muharram stunt; police rule out communal angle

bullets: Four individuals, including an Akhara organiser, have been arrested in Ujjain for performing a car explosion stunt during Muharram processions.
No quantitative metrics or fiscal figures are provided in the policy.
The National Security Act may be invoked against those arrested, with the incident occurring on June 24, 2026, in Madhya Pradesh's Ujjain.

data.headline: Bidadi project provides ground for Vokkaliga leaders’ one-upmanship

bullets: The Karnataka government's Bidadi Township Project has become a contentious issue, pitting Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar against Union Minister H.D. Kumaraswamy in a battle for Vokkaliga support.

The dispute over the project has led to a widening of the wealth gap between the two leaders, with allegations of Mr. Shivakumar accumulating wealth over the last two decades and a poster campaign targeting Mr. Kumaraswamy's family.

The project's opposition has shifted from farmers' interests to a ground for one-upmanship among Vokkaliga leaders, with both leaders seeking to outdo each other in the Old Mysore region of south Karnataka.

data.headline: A.G. Srinivas takes charge at South Western Railway

bullets: A.G. Srinivas, an officer of the Indian Railway Service of Engineers of 1989 batch, has assumed charge as Additional General Manager of South Western Railway.
He has over three decades of experience in key assignments across various railways, including commissioning of approximately 500 km of railway lines and redevelopment of multiple stations.

The appointment is effective, with no specific end date mentioned, and Mr. Srinivas is expected to leverage his experience to drive operational efficiency and infrastructure development at South Western Railway.

data.headline: Residents seek greener Yadavagiri with community-led initiatives

bullets: The Yadavagiri Residents' Association has launched a community-led initiative to transform the locality into a cleaner and greener neighbourhood by distributing free snake plants and promoting large-scale tree plantation on vacant railway land.
The initiative aims to discourage littering and improve the local environment, with the distribution of 32 snake plants to residents at the association's weekly Sunday meeting.

The association plans to seek an appointment with the Divisional Railway Manager to propose plantation drives on vacant railway land in and around Yadavagiri, with the ultimate goal of transforming the area into a cleaner and more sustainable community.

data.headline: Sports quota candidates unable to make optional entry in mock CET rounds with final list yet to be submitted

bullets: The Karnataka Examinations Authority has written multiple letters to the Department of Youth Empowerment and Sports to submit the final list of eligible sports quota candidates.

A total of 2,273 candidates in the State have applied to the KEA for a seat under the sports quota, but they cannot make optional entries in the mock seat allotment process due to the lack of the final list.

The KEA is set to announce the mock seat allotment results on July 6, and its latest communication to the Commissioner of the department set Tuesday, June 30, 2026, as the deadline for submission of the final list.

data.headline: Stalin, Kanimozhi condemn arrest of DMK cadre for protest against T.N. Minister Sarathkumar

bullets: The Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay's government has denied permission and arrested DMK student wing cadres for protesting against Human Resources Management Minister D. Sarathkumar.
The denial of permission to protest and subsequent arrest of DMK cadres has been condemned by the DMK president M.K. Stalin and deputy general secretary Kanimozhi, with 1 or more arrests reported.

The protests against Minister D. Sarathkumar were triggered by a viral video showing him performing actions that looked like preparations for snorting drugs during an IPL match, with no specific timeline given for the DMK's planned response or further actions.

data.headline: Telangana seeks stronger tourism ties with France

bullets: The Government of Telangana has formally proposed to strengthen tourism ties with France, pitching the state as a major tourist destination and promoting its diverse attractions in France.
The proposed tourism and cultural cooperation is expected to create new opportunities for tourism, investment, and economic growth, with the state government estimating significant economic benefits.

Telangana's Tourism Minister Jupally Krishna Rao suggested constituting a joint working group to institutionalise cooperation and expand cultural exchange programmes through reciprocal visits by artists, scholars, and tourism professionals between the two regions.

data.headline: North-East floods raise power, logistics and inflation risks

bullets: Heavy south-west monsoon rainfall has caused rivers across North-East India to swell, threatening to disrupt hydropower generation, coal transportation, and the movement of agricultural produce.

The disruptions could have wider consequences for the rest of the country, where power demand remains high amid persistent heat, with power generation capacity affected by hydropower contribution of around 6GW out of 48GW.

The Indian government and regional authorities are likely to closely monitor the situation and implement relief measures to mitigate the impact on the energy sector, logistics, and inflation, although specific actions and timeline have not been announced.

data.headline: Modi spotlights shift to public transport, natural fertilizers amid Gulf crisis

bullets: Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced a shift in national behavior in response to the West Asia conflict, urging citizens to reduce foreign travel and gold purchases.
The policy change resulted in a reported increase in carpooling and the use of public transport, as well as a shift towards natural fertilizers in agriculture.
Implementation of the policy is ongoing, with Modi encouraging citizens to recycle old gold for new jewellery and adopt chemical-free farming methods.

data.headline: Govt eases Quality Control Order rules: Which industry segments are likely to get relief?

bullets: The Indian government has introduced a new transition framework to ease compliance with quality control orders for industries such as toys, personal protective equipment, and air conditioners.
The alternative risk-based compliance mechanism is expected to benefit around 15 key sectors, as notified by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade.

The Transition Facilitation (Quality Control) Order, 2026, was notified by the Ministry of Commerce & Industry on June 25 and will be implemented to facilitate a smooth transition for industry while maintaining quality assurance and consumer protection.

data.headline: Panel will be set up to bring land laws up to date: Kerala Revenue Minister

bullets: A panel will be established to review and update Kerala's land laws to ensure they remain relevant and effective.
The digitisation of Kerala's Revenue department is expected to cover 72.73 lakh land parcels, with 10.42 lakh hectares already completed as part of the Rebuild Kerala scheme.

The Kerala government plans to frame a new legislation to benefit marginalised sections that were not adequately included in the initial land reforms, with a focus on implementation of Land Reforms 2.0 as proposed in the Revised Budget.

data.headline: KTU signs MoU with National Insurance Company for ‘Suraksha’ student insurance scheme

bullets: APJ Abdul Kalam Technological University (KTU) has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with National Insurance Company Ltd for implementing the 'Suraksha' group personal accident insurance scheme for students in affiliated colleges.

Under the Suraksha Scheme, a total of ₹12 lakh will be provided as accident insurance coverage for each student, along with additional financial assistance in cases of accidental death, treatment, or permanent disability.

The scheme will be implemented during the academic year 2026-27, with KTU providing ongoing financial assistance for various illnesses and the insurance company offering medical coverage for up to 30 days after hospitalisation.

data.headline: Making Rahul Gandhi PM in 2029 should be our objective, says B. Manickam Tagore

bullets: The Tamil Nadu Congress Committee (TNCC) has appointed B. Manickam Tagore as its new president, succeeding K. Selvaperunthagai.
This appointment comes with the goal of the party securing 40 out of 40 Lok Sabha seats in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry, with the ultimate objective of making Rahul Gandhi the Prime Minister in 2029.

B. Manickam Tagore is expected to run the TNCC with a vision of achieving these electoral goals, leveraging the party's benefits and products, and focusing on issues like NEET abolition, Cauvery rights, and fishermen security.

data.headline: O.V. Vijayan’s birthday to be celebrated on July 2

bullets: The Malayalam writer O.V. Vijayan's birthday will be celebrated on July 2 by the OV Vijayan Memorial Committee at Thasrak.
The event, titled 'Khasak, a pictorial epic', is expected to feature several writers and critics paying tribute to Vijayan's life and literary legacy.
District Collector Sudhir K. will inaugurate the event, which will be presided over by Committee president T.K. Narayanadas.

data.headline: Caught in the middle: On India and curbing drug abuse - The Hindu

bullets: India is strategically positioned between major global sources of illicit drugs, including Afghanistan, Pakistan, and Myanmar, which has led to a significant increase in drug smuggling via maritime routes and the use of drones.

India faces a substantial challenge in addressing its drug abuse problem, with an estimated dramatic surge in the use of methamphetamine and heroin, particularly in the states of Gujarat, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu.

The Indian government's response to the growing drug abuse issue involves adopting a 'whole of society' approach that incorporates public health and social dimensions, while also improving regulatory certainty and enhancing enforcement capabilities to combat emerging smuggling trends.

data.headline: Union Cabinet approves ₹30,000 crore additional investment in NIIF for new fund creation - The Hindu

bullets: The Union Cabinet has approved an additional investment of ₹30,000 crore in the National Investment and Infrastructure Fund (NIIF) to support its new fund creation.
This investment brings the government's total commitment to NIIF to ₹60,000 crore, with the fund currently managing ₹40,000 crore in capital commitments across its various funds and strategies.
The additional funding is expected to support NIIF's investment plans, including a recent $200 million investment in iBUS for the expansion of digital infrastructure in India.

data.headline: Industrial output grows 5.1% in May under new IIP series with 2022-23 base

bullets: India's industrial output, as measured by the Index of Industrial Production (IIP), grew 5.1% year-on-year in May 2026, led by a robust expansion in manufacturing and supported by strong growth in electricity and gas supply sector.
The IIP stood at 122.7 in May 2026, compared with 116.7 a year ago, reflecting an overall improvement in output levels with manufacturing, which carries over 76% weight in the IIP, expanding 5.5%.

The new IIP series with 2022-23 as the base year has recorded a 5.1% growth for the second month this fiscal year, indicating a gradual strengthening in industrial activity and providing an early signal on manufacturing momentum and overall growth trends in the economy.

data.headline: India regains top spot in EM tracker, but higher cost pressures continue to linger

bullets: India reclaimed the top spot in Mint's Emerging Markets Tracker in May after a six-month gap due to stronger manufacturing activity and faster export growth.
The country's composite score rose to 68.05 in May, with China climbing two places to second and Vietnam registering the biggest monthly jump to third.

India's economy is expected to face higher input costs and wholesale inflation, though oil prices have eased following the Israel-Iran ceasefire, with the impact of the earlier surge still spreading to factory input costs.

data.headline: Andhra Pradesh’s Sanjeevani health screening drew interest at national conference, says Minister

bullets: The Andhra Pradesh government has introduced the Sanjeevani health screening initiative, which uses mobile medical units to conduct diagnostic tests for disease detection and prevention.
A total of 904 mobile medical units will be used to conduct 41 diagnostic tests for every individual as part of the Sanjeevani initiative.

The initiative is set to be implemented across the state from August 15, with Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu announcing that free health tests will be provided to over 72 lakh people under the Sanjeevani digital drive.

data.headline: INDIA bloc writes to CJI, flags EC’s ‘biased conduct’

bullets: Twenty-three Opposition parties, including the AAP and DMK, have sent a joint memorandum to the Chief Justice of India alleging biased conduct by the Election Commission.

The memorandum highlights the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls in several States, including West Bengal and Bihar, and ongoing revisions in other States, but does not specify the exact number of affected voters or electoral areas.

The parties took the decision to send the joint letter during a June 8 meeting in Delhi, with the DMK and AAP, which did not attend the meeting, also signing the letter reportedly due to their opposition to the Congress's post-election alliance switch.

data.headline: ‘It’s about time’: How a Chennai journalist’s book inspired ‘Made in India: A Titan Story’

bullets: The Indian streaming platform Amazon MX Player has reported that the web series "Made in India: A Titan Story" has become the most-viewed Indian web series of 2026, according to an Ormax report that tracks viewership.

The series, chronicling the journey of Titan founder Xerxes Desai and his mentor, JRD Tata, has garnered significant attention, with a notable 3 weeks of streaming resulting in substantial viewership.

The web series "Made in India: A Titan Story" is directed by Robbie Grewal and stars Jim Sarbh and Naseeruddin Shah, and its success is attributed to its unique storytelling and engaging narrative that transports viewers to the early 70s and 80s Bombay.

data.headline: Switzerland’s MSC to acquire 49% stake in Adani’s Vizhinjam port in Kerala for ₹13,220 crore

bullets: The Mediterranean Shipping Company (MSC) Group will acquire a 49% stake in Adani's Vizhinjam port in Kerala for ₹13,220 crore, marking the largest foreign private investment in India's domestic port infrastructure.
The investment value is approximately $1.397 billion, with MSC's acquisition of a 49% interest in Adani Vizhinjam Port Private Limited (AVPPL) subject to customary regulatory approvals.
The partnership is expected to be finalized after regulatory approvals, with the MSC Group's container terminal operating and investing arm, TiL, making the investment in Adani's Vizhinjam port.

data.headline: Rythu Bharosa for Kharif to be released today; Telangana PCC chief reaffirms govt commitment to farmers

bullets: The Telangana State government has reaffirmed its commitment to farmers by releasing financial assistance under the Rythu Bharosa scheme for the Kharif season, providing annual investment support of ₹12,000 per acre.

This initiative will benefit eligible farmer families and fulfils promises made in the Warangal Farmers' Declaration, a key policy framework of the Congress, with over 25 lakh farmer families already benefiting from the government's up to ₹2 lakh farm loan waiver.

The Rythu Bharosa scheme is set to be released today, as announced by Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee president Mahesh Kumar Goud, who also highlighted Telangana's emergence as a national model in agricultural welfare and farm support.

data.headline: Freight rates to stay elevated amid high demand for tankers, vessels

bullets: Global shipping freight rates are expected to remain elevated for the next few months due to increased demand from recovering trade flows and the peak shipping season.
The freight rate of a 40-ft container has more than doubled from $1,899 on 26 February 2026 to $4,166 as of 25 June 2026.

Freight rates are likely to stay high until the end of the peak shipping season, with industry executives and analysts attributing the sustained demand to recovering trade flows and tight vessel capacity.

data.headline: 41 migrant workers from Jharkhand stranded in Tamil Nadu after ammonia leak at Tiruvallur firm

bullets: The Jharkhand government has been unresponsive to repeated requests from Tiruvallur district officials to facilitate the return of 41 migrant workers stranded in Tamil Nadu after an ammonia leak at a seafood firm.

Despite the June 21 ammonia leak claiming 16 lives, the 41 migrant workers who were evacuated from the Periyapalayam firm remain without assistance, with no clear plan in place to repatriate them to their home State of Jharkhand.
Tiruvallur district officials have made repeated requests to the Jharkhand government to facilitate the return of the stranded migrant workers, but so far, there has been no response.

data.headline: Kerala University row over Standing Counsel appointment

bullets: The Vice-Chancellor of Kerala University has replaced advocate Thomas Abraham as the university's Standing Counsel before the Kerala High Court with advocate Girija Gopal.

Kerala University has formally informed the High Court of the change in Standing Counsel, invoking Section 10(13) of the Kerala University Act, 1974, and has directed Mr. Abraham to hand over all case files to the newly appointed counsel within the earliest possible timeframe.

The controversy arises from Mr. Abraham's objection that the Vice-Chancellor does not have the authority to appoint or replace the Standing Counsel, citing the Kerala University First Statutes, 1977, which grants this power to the university Syndicate.

data.headline: Restrictive regulations will slow Indian startup formation by 20%, VC flows by 25%: Report

bullets: India's restrictive digital regulations may slow startup formation by 20% and VC flows by 25% between 2025 and 2035.
The report estimates a loss of approximately ₹91,500 crore in venture investments annually and a reduction of 245,000 startup jobs in India.
A shift from India's current enabling environment to a more restrictive digital regulatory environment is expected to lead to 2,130 fewer startups being created annually.

data.headline: Medical bail only in case of ‘grave necessity’, Supreme Court tells Asaram’s side

bullets: The Supreme Court has ruled that it will only consider granting medical bail to self-styled godman Asaram Bapu if there is a grave necessity and his life is in danger.
This decision implies that the court will not grant medical bail solely based on Asaram's usual health issues, with the liberty to make an urgent plea only if his condition deteriorates.

The Supreme Court has issued a notice to the State of Rajasthan, indicating that the court will consider Asaram's medical bail application on a case-by-case basis, taking into account the severity of his condition.

data.headline: M.R. Vijayabhaskar’s resignation displays fragile nature of truce between AIADMK rebels and party chief Palaniswami

bullets: M.R. Vijayabhaskar's resignation as MLA in Tamil Nadu has highlighted the fragile nature of the truce between AIADMK rebels and the party's general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami.
The resignation marks another setback for the AIADMK, following a pattern of defectors returning to the party fold only to later rejoin the rebels.
The policy implications of the resignation are likely to be felt within the AIADMK, potentially leading to a re-evaluation of the party's leadership dynamics and internal power struggles.

data.headline: The women behind India’s economy—and the price of invisible work

bullets: The Supreme Court in India has placed a notional value of ₹30,000 per month on unpaid domestic services provided by homemakers, creating a new head of compensation titled 'loss of domestic care'.
This valuation is expected to apply to approximately 370 million homemakers in India, although the notional compensation will not be included in the country's GDP calculations.

The Supreme Court's judgment aims to raise awareness about the significant economic value of unpaid domestic services, which are crucial for the functioning of households and the overall economy, and seeks to inform policymaking decisions accordingly.

data.headline: Bodies of teenaged inter-caste lovers found in Mayiladuthurai district; violence erupts

bullets: The Tamil Nadu Police has launched a probe into the deaths of a 19-year-old Scheduled Caste youth and a 17-year-old Most Backward Classes girl found in a shed in Mayiladuthurai district, amid suspicion of foul play and caste killing.

The investigation has resulted in the arrest of four individuals, including the girl's father, under the SC/ST Prevention of Atrocities Act, in connection with a complaint filed by the youth alleging assault.

Police have posted pickets in the village and shifted the bodies to Tiruvarur Government Medical College Hospital for autopsy, while villagers continue to be on edge following the discovery of the bodies.

data.headline: PDP says party ‘leaders prevented from protesting against outsourcing of govt. jobs in J&K’

bullets: The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) accused the administration of Jammu and Kashmir of placing its leaders under house arrest to prevent them from protesting against the outsourcing of 25,000 government jobs.

The outsourcing of 25,000 government jobs is a significant shift in the employment landscape of Jammu and Kashmir, affecting thousands of individuals who would have otherwise been employed by the government.

The PDP leadership has expressed concerns about the outsourcing of government jobs and the alleged crackdown on its leaders, with President Mehbooba Mufti calling for peaceful protests and denouncing the National Conference's alleged duplicity in enforcing government policies.

data.headline: SP’s Chief Whip in U.P. Assembly resigns, says followed direction of party leadership

bullets: The Samajwadi Party's Chief Whip in the Uttar Pradesh Assembly, Kamal Akhtar, resigned from his post on June 30, 2026, following a directive from party president Akhilesh Yadav.

This move is expected to result in the appointment of a new Chief Whip, potentially from the Other Backward Classes (OBCs) or Scheduled Caste (SC) community, in a bid to reshape the party's structure.

Kamal Akhtar, an MLA from the Kanth Assembly constituency, stated that he has always adhered to the party's leadership and will continue to do so, handing over responsibility as per the party's dynamics.

data.headline: Indus Waters Treaty remains ‘valid, binding and operative’: Pakistan Deputy PM

bullets: Pakistan rejects India's decision to revoke the Indus Waters Treaty, stating it remains a valid, binding, and operative agreement.
The treaty has been in effect since 1960, governing the distribution and use of the Indus River and its tributaries between India and Pakistan.

Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar claimed that any attempt to deprive Pakistan of its rightfully allocated waters under the treaty would have profound consequences for regional peace and security.

data.headline: After Manesar clashes, Gurugram police set up Labour Liaison Teams in all police stations

bullets: The Gurugram police have established Labour Liaison and Industrial Co-ordination Teams in all police stations to strengthen law and order in industrial areas and respond to labour unrest.

The police stations will have one or two teams each, consisting of four to five personnel with excellent public dealing skills, to co-ordinate with industry management, labour unions, and the Labour Department.

The teams will maintain regular liaison with industrial establishments, conduct visits to sensitive areas, promptly report disputes, and focus on the safety of women employees, with a goal to improve labour relations.

data.headline: Coal India targeting to spend ₹1,900 crore on R&D until FY2030 - The Hindu

bullets: Coal India has set a goal to invest ₹1,900 crore in research and development by fiscal year 2030, aligning with the government's mandate of allocating at least one percent of the entity's profit before tax for R&D.
Currently, Coal India oversees 19 R&D projects worth ₹225 crore and is actively engaged in 13 pilot-scale research and prototype development projects at its three Centers of Excellence.

The company's R&D efforts are further augmented by international collaborations, including agreements with Ergo Exergy, Ericsson, and CSIRO, aimed at developing innovative technologies such as underground coal gasification and 5G implementation.

data.headline: Despite war, net remittances from West Asia to India rose 70% in April 2026

bullets: The Reserve Bank of India reported a significant increase in net remittances from West Asia to India, with a 70% rise in April 2026 compared to the same period in the previous year.
The total remittance inflow from West Asia reached $1.35 billion in April 2026, marking a substantial recovery despite the ongoing regional conflict.

The Reserve Bank attributes this growth to improved economic conditions in West Asian countries and increased engagement of Indian workers in the region's burgeoning industries, with further analysis expected in upcoming policy reports.

data.headline: Economy holds firm, but risks remain from monsoon and geopolitics, says govt's economic review

bullets: The Indian government's economic review for June 2026 has identified uneven monsoon rainfall, emerging El Niño conditions, and geopolitical uncertainties as key risks to the country's economic outlook.

The economy remains resilient in the initial months of FY27, with high-frequency indicators such as e-way bill generation, PMI readings, electricity consumption, and automobile sales continuing to signal strength in domestic demand, albeit with some easing in momentum.

The finance ministry's monthly economic review is prepared by the department of economic affairs (DEA) and will be closely monitored to assess the impact of these risks on India's economic growth and stability.

data.headline: India's fiscal deficit at 9.6% of FY27 target in May

bullets: India's fiscal deficit reached 9.6% of the FY27 target at the end of May, narrowing to ₹1.62 trillion mainly due to a record ₹2.87 trillion dividend from the Reserve Bank of India.

The government has budgeted a fiscal deficit of 4.3% of GDP, or about ₹16.96 trillion, for FY27, relying on stronger tax collections and non-tax receipts in the coming months to keep the deficit within the target.

The Controller General of Accounts released the latest accounts on Tuesday, cautioning against reading too much into the first couple of months' data as direct tax collections and RBI dividends can fluctuate significantly.

data.headline: Morgan Stanley cuts oil price forecast again as Strait of Hormuz flows recover, warns of glut

bullets: Morgan Stanley has downgraded its oil forecasts for the second time in two weeks, citing the quicker-than-expected normalization of Strait of Hormuz traffic and strong US supplies combined with weak Chinese demand.
Brent prices are expected to average $75 per barrel for the next two quarters, a $15 and $5 decrease from previous forecasts, while Dated Brent is predicted to drop to $70 by the end of 2027.
The bank's analysts have downgraded their outlooks for all four quarters of the next financial year, attributing the changes to the "twin solvers" of high US oil exports and low Chinese imports.

data.headline: The human cost of India’s new welfare architecture, explained in charts

bullets: India is transitioning from a rights-based welfare system to a new model that prioritizes centralized cash transfers and tangible goods over public services.
The shift is expected to strain state finances by 15-20% in the next few years, exacerbating existing fiscal constraints.
The implementation of this new welfarism model will be rolled out through digital platforms, with a focus on technology-driven transfers to beneficiaries by 2028.

data.headline: Enumeration Forms in English for GHMC, in Telugu for the rest; dummy forms printed in Urdu for assistance: Telangana CEO office

bullets: The Telangana Chief Electoral Officer's office has begun distributing Enumeration Forms, printed in English for GHMC areas and in Telugu for the rest, as part of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) taken up in the State.
Nearly 60% of the total 3.38 crore electors in the state have received the Enumeration Forms, which will be distributed till July 24.
The forms are being distributed by Booth Level Officers (BLOs) starting from June 25, with dummy forms also printed in Urdu for assistance of the general public.

data.headline: Price of commercial LPG, 5-kg FTL and domestic ATF reduced as conflict pressures ease

bullets: Oil-marketing companies reduced the prices of commercial LPG cylinders by an average of ₹180 per cylinder and domestic ATF by ₹5 per litre on July 1, 2026.
The price cuts followed four prior tranches of hikes that increased the price of commercial LPG to ₹1,345 per cylinder since March 7, resulting in a ₹180 per cylinder decrease.
The price reductions come as a sign of easing supply situation due to a probable conclusion of the over hundred-day-long conflict in West Asia.

data.headline: LPG price hike: Government says rates in India among world's lowest despite 46% jump in global benchmark

bullets: The Indian government has increased the domestic LPG price by ₹29 per 14.2-kg cylinder.

The hike brings the price of a 14.2-kg LPG cylinder in Delhi to ₹942 from ₹913, and beneficiaries of the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana will pay an effective ₹642 per cylinder after receiving a subsidy of ₹300 per refill.

The government attributes the price increase to a surge in international prices triggered by disruptions in West Asia, stating that India's LPG prices remain among the lowest globally despite this jump.

data.headline: Kerala Assembly: CM says feasibility study on to set up airstrips in Idukki, Wayanad, Kasaragod

bullets: The Kerala government is conducting a techno-economic feasibility study to set up airstrips in Idukki, Wayanad, and Kasaragod districts for the operation of small aircraft and helicopters.

The state has allocated the project management consultant to Kerala Rail Development Corporation Limited and selected a joint venture consisting of RITES and KIIFCON through a tendering process, reportedly committing to a significant investment.

Construction work for five helipads in Wayanad district has commenced, aiming to expedite rescue operations during natural calamities, with the overall project expected to enhance Kerala's aviation connectivity and emergency transport capabilities.

data.headline: Brain health checkup centre inaugurated in Guntur

bullets: The Andhra Pradesh government has inaugurated a Comprehensive Wellness Clinic in Guntur featuring a Brain Health check-up programme for early detection and risk assessment.
The clinic will cater to the healthcare needs of the local community with a focus on preventive measures against brain diseases which affect one in three people worldwide.
The Lalitha PVS Institute of Medical Sciences, which operates the clinic, has begun its operations with over 40 specialties and a 600-bed capacity.

data.headline: Kerala will not allow communalisation of education, no compromise on university autonomy: Roji M. John

bullets: The Kerala state government has reaffirmed its commitment to preventing the communalization of education and safeguarding university autonomy.
The state's Higher Education department will conduct a comprehensive review of the Four-Year Undergraduate Programme to address practical difficulties faced by students and colleges.
Necessary reforms will be introduced within the framework of the existing academic structure, with a focus on upholding the autonomy and integrity of universities.

data.headline: Make learning and innovation lifelong pursuits, President Murmu tells Andhra graduates

bullets: The President of India, Droupadi Murmu, emphasized the importance of making learning and innovation lifelong pursuits for young graduates in an increasingly knowledge-driven world.
At least 100 students received their degrees at the Central University of Andhra Pradesh's first convocation, with the university also offering 44 courses in various disciplines.
The President's address was part of the university's first convocation, which was attended by students, faculty members, and other dignitaries at Janthaluru village in Anantapur, Andhra Pradesh.

data.headline: TMC leader Mahua Moitra alleges BJP workers hurled eggs at her in Bengal's Nadia district

bullets: The TMC leader Mahua Moitra alleged that BJP workers hurled eggs and raised slogans against her during a protest in West Bengal's Nadia district.
At least one video of the incident was shared on social media by Moitra, but its authenticity could not be independently verified.
Moitra's attendance at the TMC meeting in Palashi was disrupted by the protest, which was eventually dispersed by police and central security personnel.

data.headline: India, Japan eye LNG stockpiling partnership amid global supply uncertainty as Sanae Takaichi arrives today: Report

bullets: India and Japan are set to sign a liquefied natural gas (LNG) supply deal aimed at addressing global supply chain disruptions caused by the US-Iran conflict.

The proposed deal is expected to facilitate a joint task force for LNG stockpiling between the two countries, with the establishment of the task force to be mentioned in the joint statement issued at the end of the summit.

The signing of the LNG supply deal is scheduled to take place during the annual summit between Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, who arrived in New Delhi on Wednesday.

data.headline: Migrant workers robbed at knifepoint near Electronics City; cash, phones looted

bullets: The Bengaluru police received a complaint from a group of four migrant workers who were allegedly robbed at knifepoint by unidentified men near Electronics City.
The incident resulted in the theft of ₹10,000 in cash, four mobile phones, and the victims' SIM cards.
The police are currently investigating the incident, with the victims alleging that the accused threatened them with a knife, a wooden club, and an iron rod, and assaulted two of the victims.

data.headline: Ladakh civil society groups to hold informal talks with visiting MHA team, say ‘spadework for formal talks’

bullets: Civil society groups in Ladakh will hold informal talks with a visiting team from the Ministry of Home Affairs to discuss the region's demand for statehood and Sixth Schedule status.
The informal talks are expected to lay groundwork for formal negotiations, with the Ladakh leadership aiming to share their views and gauge the Centre's stance on the demands.

The talks will take place in Leh this week, marking the first step towards formal discussions between the Ladakh leadership and the Centre following the Centre's alleged backtracking on a previous agreement made in May 2026.

data.headline: Mob throws eggs and stones at Mahua Moitra; Bengal BJP president calls for restraint

bullets: A mob threw stones and eggs at Trinamool Congress leader Mahua Moitra in West Bengal's Nadia district, with Moitra accusing the BJP of orchestrating the attack.
At least one incident of egg-throwing was reported, and the Calcutta High Court has ordered the West Bengal government to frame guidelines for transporting accused individuals in police custody.
The incident occurred a day after the high court's order, and BJP president Samik Bhattacharya has shifted the blame onto internal divisions within the Trinamool Congress.

data.headline: Why managing fiscal is a tightrope for State governments

bullets: The US state governments are required to balance their annual budgets, leaving them vulnerable to economic downturns and limiting their ability to respond to unexpected expenses.
A total of $2.2 trillion in state government outlays were projected for fiscal year 2023, with a significant portion allocated towards education, healthcare, and infrastructure.

To address this fiscal constraint, the state governments have implemented various measures such as the 2014 US Supreme Court ruling in McCleary v. Washington, which required the state to improve its public education funding, and the development of long-term fiscal plans to ensure sustainable financial management.

data.headline: Monsoon tracker LIVE: Heavy showers flood parts of Mumbai, slow road traffic and trains

bullets: The Indian Meteorological Department has forecasted below normal monsoon rainfall for July, with a 40% deficit.
Several areas in Mumbai have logged more than 200 mm of rainfall over the last 24 hours, causing waterlogging in prime areas.
Heavy showers in Mumbai and Bhalesa in Jammu and Kashmir have caused inconvenience to commuters and slowed vehicular traffic, with the situation showing little sign of easing.

data.headline: Allegations of child abuse: Police summon creche staff at Capgemini in Bengaluru for questioning

bullets: Police in Bengaluru have issued a summons to five staff members of a creche operating inside the Capgemini office for questioning regarding allegations of physical abuse and cruelty towards children.
The allegations, which were reported and led to the registration of an FIR on June 29, involve caregivers at the Little Buds Day Care centre who cared for children of Capgemini employees.

The questioning process, which will determine the exact role of the staff, is expected to be based on video clips of the alleged abuse that were sent to the Forensic Science Laboratory for further verification.

data.headline: Madras High Court refuses to quash case against Ponmudy for 2025 derogatory speech

bullets: The Madras High Court refused to quash a private complaint against former Tamil Nadu Minister K. Ponmudy for derogatory remarks made against certain religious groups and women.
The case was filed under various provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, with the III Metropolitan Magistrate's court at George Town in Chennai taking cognisance of the complaint early this year.
A criminal revision petition filed by Ponmudy against the complaint was dismissed by Justice G.K. Ilanthiraiyan on July 2, 2026, allowing the case to proceed against the former minister.

data.headline: GST collections rise 14% to  ₹1.95 trillion in June, as tax revenue from imports soars

bullets: The Centre and states collectively collected ₹1.95 trillion in gross GST revenue in June, marking a 13.9% year-on-year increase.
The growth was driven by a 34.6% year-on-year surge in GST revenue from imports to ₹60,038 crore, while domestic GST collections increased 6.5% to ₹1.35 trillion.
GST refunds rose 29.1% during the month to ₹32,436 crore, with net GST mop-up standing at ₹1.62 trillion, up 11.2% from a year earlier, reflecting faster processing of claims.

data.headline: Can Bar Associations refuse to represent an accused? What does the law say?

bullets: The Supreme Court of India has consistently ruled that it is unlawful and unconstitutional for Bar Associations to collectively decide not to represent a particular accused individual, as this denies their right to fair trial and legal representation.

This stance is supported by a 2010 Supreme Court judgment in A.S. Mohammed Rafi v. State of Tamil Nadu, where the court deemed such resolutions by Bar bodies as "wholly illegal, against all traditions and professional ethics".

Under the Indian legal framework, every accused individual has the right to fair trial and legal representation, and Bar Associations are obligated to uphold this fundamental right by providing representation to those who require it.

data.headline: Naidu, Pawan, Chouhan launch VB-G Ram G scheme in Tirupati district

bullets: The Viksit Bharat Guarantee for Rozgar Ajeevika Mission Grameen (VB-G Ram G) scheme was launched on July 2, 2026, by Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu, Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan, and Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan in Tirupati district.

The scheme aims to provide employment and welfare benefits to farmers, with the Centre offering to procure 2.16 lakh tonnes of Totapuri mangoes, and the total potential expenditure is estimated to be around Rs 51,000 crore, six times the current expenditure of Rs 7,600 crore.

Implementation of the VB-G Ram G scheme will focus on rural employment, with the Centre planning to cover a significant number of farmers and rural communities, and the scheme is expected to be rolled out across various states in the country.

data.headline: The guides Hyderabad stopped looking for

bullets: The Hyderabad city government has allowed digital tools to disrupt the traditional profession of tourist guides, who are now often relegated to part-time work.
Over 70 percent of tourists to Hyderabad's heritage sites now rely on digital tools and guides, leading to a significant decline in the number of full-time guides employed in the industry.

The city's heritage structures, including Golconda Fort and Qutb Shahi Tombs, are still popular tourist destinations, but the role of traditional guides has become an afterthought, replaced by digital information and self-guided tours.

data.headline: T.N. govt. sanctions ₹300 crore as first instalment for Pongal 2027 free dhoti, saree scheme

bullets: The Tamil Nadu government has sanctioned ₹300 crore as the first instalment for its Pongal 2027 free dhoti and saree scheme, which will benefit 4,522,511 ration cardholders.
The estimated total cost of the scheme is ₹642.88 crore, with ₹606.94 crore allocated in the 2026-27 budget estimates.
The government has approved the distribution of new varieties of dhotis and sarees for Pongal 2027, with a total of 2,27,83,417 sarees and 2,25,14,094 dhotis required for the scheme.

data.headline: India's richest cities: urban affairs ministry is on a quest to assess economic output of cities for first time

bullets: The Indian government is developing a standardized methodology to estimate the economic output of cities through the City Economic Product initiative. This initiative aims to quantify urban economic contributions, which account for nearly 70% of India's economic output. The National Institute of Urban Affairs is leading the development of the City Economic Product methodology, with work starting to calculate the economic output of Indian cities.
Additional context pending.
Additional context pending.

data.headline: Centre amends Drugs Rules, 1945 to ensure uniform regulation of advance cell and gene therapies

bullets: The Central government has amended the Drugs Rules, 1945 to ensure uniform regulation of advanced cell and gene therapies through the Centrally Licence Approving Authority framework.

The revised framework expands the scope of joint regulatory supervision under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act to include stem cell-derived products, gene therapeutic products, and xenografts, alongside existing categories like vaccines and r-DNA based medicines.

The Centre's move is expected to strengthen regulatory oversight of emerging medical technologies, with the amendment aimed at covering additional categories of critical drugs and biological products by the Centrally Licence Approving Authority.

data.headline: Hurdles persist for persons with rare diseases seeking disability certification

bullets: The Indian state of Andhra Pradesh faces challenges in providing disability certification to individuals with rare diseases due to limited awareness among disability certifying authorities.
As of 2018, the lack of sustainable drug access and limited healthcare options for rare disease patients in India remains a persistent issue, affecting thousands of people nationwide.

The Andhra Pradesh government's NTR Pension Bharosa scheme provides a pension amount of between ₹6,000 and ₹15,000 to individuals with more than 40% disabilities, but many rare disease patients continue to face difficulties in obtaining the required disability percentage.

data.headline: Free and rules-based Indo-Pacific a shared priority for India and Japan: PM Modi

bullets: India and Japan have identified a "free and rules-based Indo-Pacific" as a shared priority for regional development and security.
India and Japan plan to invest in joint development of technologies for maritime security and regional peace, with the countries having some of the world's largest economies.
The announcement was made by Prime Minister Narendra Modi during his meeting with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi in New Delhi in July 2026.

data.headline: BJP urges State govt. to hand over to CBI misappropriation of funds case

bullets: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has called on the State government to transfer a case involving the misappropriation of multi-crore funds in Matoshri Hemareddy Mallamma Souharda Sahakara Sangha to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) for a thorough investigation.
The misappropriated funds amount to over ₹7 crore, prompting the police to hand the case over to the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) for further investigation.

BJP leader Ameen Reddy Patil Yalagi has requested the State government to reassign the case to the CBI, citing concerns over potential involvement of influential individuals and the need for a more comprehensive investigation.

data.headline: Petrol, diesel prices to fall only after cheaper crude oil reaches Indian refiners: Hardeep Puri

bullets: The Indian government has announced that petrol and diesel prices will be reduced when cheaper crude oil reaches the country's refineries.
The government estimates that a reduction of around Rs 8-10 per litre in petrol and diesel prices is expected once cheaper crude oil becomes available to Indian refiners.

The implementation of the price reduction is contingent on the receipt of cheaper crude oil and will be carried out by the Oil Marketing Companies, with no specific timeline announced for the reduction in prices.

data.headline: Labour Ministry makes EPF contributions beyond ₹1,800 voluntary

bullets: The Labour Ministry has made EPF contributions beyond ₹1,800 voluntary, allowing employees to contribute up to ₹35,000 per year to their Employees' Provident Fund accounts.
This policy change is expected to benefit around 6 crore employees who are currently enrolled in the EPF scheme, with an estimated ₹1,300 crore in additional contributions anticipated annually.
The Ministry will implement this change through an amendment to the EPF Scheme, 1952, and the necessary amendments are expected to be notified in the coming months.

data.headline: The ‘Hi, hello’ monsoon: In rural India, an anxious, high-stakes wait for the skies to swell

bullets: The Indian government has faced criticism for its handling of the crop purchase portal, which resulted in a loss of over ₹70,000 for a farmer like Raja Chourey in Madhya Pradesh.
The country is facing a large rainfall deficit, which could impact annual incomes of farmers like Chourey and reduce harvests worth millions of rupees.

The delayed and scanty monsoon rains are threatening to upend the plans of farmers, particularly those growing premium Basmati rice, and may force them to choose between waiting for the rain or packing their produce for the factory floor.

data.headline: Manufacturing PMI slows to 54.2 in June on softer demand

bullets: The June HSBC India Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) fell to 54.2, marking the second-slowest expansion since mid-2022.

The slowdown in the Indian manufacturing sector is evident in the PMI reading, which remained above the 50-mark but showed the weakest pace of growth in new orders and output in four years since 2022.

The easing of inflationary pressures and input costs are expected to moderate the impact of the slowdown, with manufacturers citing subdued client appetite and intense market competition as key factors in the decline in demand.

data.headline: GHMC sets up 16 SIR help desks

bullets: The Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation has established 16 help desks in various Assembly constituencies to provide information and address grievances related to the Special Intensive Revision being carried out by the Election Commission of India.
These help desks will be staffed by officials who will assist voters in filling enumeration forms and provide information on the Dos and Don'ts of the SIR process.
The 16 help desks are set to operate in ERO offices throughout Hyderabad district, with an additional desk to be located at the GHMC headquarters on Tank Bund, starting in July 2026.

data.headline: Two Kashmir Shia clerics ‘disallowed’ to travel to Iran for Ali Khamenei’s final rites

bullets: The Indian government's Bureau of Immigration prevented two Kashmir Shia clerics, Aga Syed Hassan Al-Mosavi Al-Safavi and Masroor Abbas Ansari, from traveling to Iran to attend the final rites of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.
The exact reason for the denial of travel permission is unclear, with no written explanation or order provided to the clerics.
The incident occurred a day after the Iranian International Relations Department extended invitations to the clerics and PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti to attend the funeral ceremony.

data.headline: Fleet shortage forces SpiceJet withdrawal from Chennai | Explained

bullets: SpiceJet has suspended its flight operations from Chennai due to a fleet shortage, with services expected to resume in October as the airline rebuilds its fleet.
The airline has scheduled 44% fewer flights in July compared with April, reducing its daily operational capacity in response to operational and financial challenges.
SpiceJet's fleet has shrunk to around 12-13 aircraft from more than 30 a few months ago, forcing the temporary suspension of services to several destinations.

data.headline: Govt expects record  ₹80,000 cr dividend haul from non-financial state firms in FY27

bullets: The Indian government anticipates collecting a record ₹80,000 crore in dividend receipts from non-financial state firms in FY27.
This represents an increase from the budget estimate of ₹75,000 crore and surpasses the FY26 collection of ₹78,438.07 crore.

The expected dividend haul is driven by healthy earnings from profitable state-owned enterprises in key sectors such as oil and gas, coal, and infrastructure, with a focus on maintaining consistent payouts while balancing capital expenditure requirements.

data.headline: Indian Railways freight volumes climb 4% in June, passenger traffic up 2.3%

bullets: Indian Railways registered growth in both freight and passenger traffic in June, with freight volumes increasing by 4% and passenger traffic rising by 2.3% compared to the same month last year.

The national transporter carried 142.21 million tonnes of freight and 638.1 million passengers in June, generating additional revenue of approximately ₹430 crore through healthy growth in freight earnings, a 3% increase over the same month in 2025.

Indian Railways plans to continue supporting economic growth, strengthening logistics, and providing convenient travel options across the country, with sustained efforts to improve operational performance and augment passenger services.

data.headline: 5kg LPG cylinder demand from immigrant labourers plummets up to 80% amid price surge

bullets: The demand for portable 5kg LPG cylinders, primarily used by migrant workers and students, has plummeted by up to 80% following a price surge due to the West Asia war. The price of these cylinders in Delhi has increased from ₹323 in March to ₹805.50 in June, a rise of approximately 150%. The fall in demand is attributed to the price hike and coincides with a trend of workers returning to urban areas after an exodus during a previous cooking gas squeeze.
Additional context pending.
Additional context pending.

data.headline: Legislative debates must focus on solutions, not criticism: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla

bullets: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla emphasized that legislative debates in Indian Houses must focus on finding practical solutions to public problems rather than mere criticism.

The orientation programme for newly-elected members of the 18th West Bengal Legislative Assembly will be held over two days, organized by the Lok Sabha Secretariat, Parliamentary Research and Training Institute for Democracies, and the West Bengal Legislative Assembly.

The programme aims to equip MLAs with essential knowledge and skills to enrich democratic discourse, guided by public welfare and facts, research, and reasoned arguments, and is scheduled to take place in Kolkata on a specified date.

data.headline: T.N. govt. to expand Thayumanavar scheme to benefit more elderly citizens, persons with disabilities

bullets: The Tamil Nadu government plans to expand the Chief Minister's Thayumanavar Scheme to deliver essential commodities to more elderly citizens and persons with disabilities at their doorsteps.
The expansion is expected to benefit approximately 4 lakh additional individuals by reducing the eligibility age from 70 to 60 and issuing 50,000 new ration cards.
The Tamil Nadu government is set to formally launch the distribution of new smart ration cards to applicants during the Chief Minister's proposed visit to Perambur in the next few weeks.

data.headline: Progress slow on Comprehensive Dam Safety Evaluation in Kerala as deadline closes in

bullets: The Kerala State Electricity Board and Water Resources department have been slow in completing the Comprehensive Dam Safety Evaluation despite the deadline of December 31, 2026.

Only 12 dams out of a total of 60 have undergone the comprehensive safety evaluation, with the Kerala State Electricity Board completing the exercise on eight dams and the Water Resources department on four.

The Kerala State Electricity Board has asked its Chief Engineer (Civil-Dam Safety) to submit a detailed action plan within 15 days for completing the Comprehensive Dam Safety Evaluation on all its dams by November 2026.

data.headline: Shashi Tharoor recalls past security concerns amid Adani’s proposed MSC stake transfer in Vizhinjam port

bullets: The Indian government is considering a proposal to sell a 49% stake in the Adani Vizhinjam Port Private Limited to the MSC Group, a Swiss-based shipping major, amidst concerns over national security.

The proposed deal is worth ₹13,220 crore, representing a significant investment in the Vizhinjam port project, which has previously struggled to secure bidders due to concerns over the involvement of Chinese companies.

The stake transfer requires the concurrence of both the central and Kerala governments, and Congress MP Shashi Tharoor has emphasized the importance of national security considerations in the decision-making process.

data.headline: FMCG majors stay upbeat despite flagging inflation, El Niño risks

bullets: Indian fast-moving consumer goods companies Dabur and Godrej Consumer Products expect to achieve double-digit and high-teens revenue growth respectively despite elevated input costs and global inflationary pressures.
The forecasted revenue growth is expected to be driven by strong volume gains despite a volatile market and below-normal monsoon rainfall that could hurt farm output and rural consumption.
The companies' resilient performance is attributed to consumer sentiment remaining upbeat despite geopolitical tensions and the return of El Niño which poses risks to demand and supply chains.

data.headline: India’s services sector grows at slowest pace in 17 months in June as demand softens: HSBC India Services PMI

bullets: India's services sector expanded at its slowest pace in 17 months in June, with the HSBC India Services PMI falling to 57.4, its lowest reading since December 2024.

The sector's growth rate was significantly impacted, with new order growth slowing to its weakest pace in over two-and-a-half years, resulting in a decline in employment and weakening business confidence.

The weak demand for services was largely driven by domestic factors, although the sector's export orders remained resilient, rising at the fastest pace in three months and helping to cushion the slowdown.

data.headline: RBI says VDAs, including cryptocurrency poses threat to emerging economies like India, opposes its legalisation

bullets: The Reserve Bank of India has informed a Parliamentary panel that virtual digital assets, including cryptocurrencies, pose a threat to emerging economies like India and should remain prohibited.
The RBI cited risks such as terror financing and regulatory challenges, but also mentioned its ongoing pilot initiatives for sovereign digital currency.
Implementation of the RBI's stance on prohibiting virtual digital assets may impact India's financial innovation, as the country seeks to balance innovation with monetary and financial stability.

data.headline: SIT likely to re-audit Ram Temple Trust accounts for last five years

bullets: The Special Investigation Team is likely to re-audit the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust's accounts for the past five years following preliminary investigation hints at large-scale anomalies and irregularities.
The repeat audit is expected to scrutinize the trust's accounts over a five-year period, covering construction-related expenditure and donations valued in jewelry, gold, and silver.
The re-audit is set to be conducted by the SIT team in accordance with government sources, with the investigation ongoing since July 3, 2026.

data.headline: South Zone Women’s Canoeing and Kayaking League to begin in Vizag today

bullets: The South Zone Women's Canoeing and Kayaking League will commence on Saturday and Sunday at the Gambeeramgedda Reservoir in Visakhapatnam under the Khelo India initiative of the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.

The championship will feature competitions in kayak and canoe sprint events across four categories, including sub-junior, junior, senior, and women's categories, with distances ranging from 200 to 1,000 meters.

The ASMITA South Zone Women's Canoeing and Kayaking League is being organised in association with the Sports Authority of Andhra Pradesh and the Canoeing and Kayaking Association of Andhra Pradesh, with competitions scheduled to take place from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. on both days.

data.headline: Pushing for transparency, social activist demands Ram Temple Trust to place documents in public domain

bullets: The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust is urged to release its trust documents, annual reports, and financial statements into public domain for transparency and accountability.
The Trust's financial statements and audit reports for the last five years are likely to be re-audited by the SIT.
A former IPS officer, Amitabh Thakur, first requested the Trust to release the documents in February 2024 and sent a follow-up representation in June 2025.

data.headline: Cabinet sub-committee will decide on cloud seeding: Karnataka Medical Education Minister Sharan Prakash Patil

bullets: A Cabinet sub-committee will decide on cloud seeding in Karnataka to address the state's rain shortfall.
The district's 41% of crop sowing was reported so far, with farmers having until July 15 to cover unsown areas.

Implementation of cloud seeding will depend on the Cabinet sub-committee's decision, while priority will be given to ensuring drinking water supply using the Tungabhadra dam's available water instead of irrigating crops.

data.headline: India, New Zealand ink “historic” free trade agreement, to be implemented later this year

bullets: The governments of India and New Zealand have reached a "historic" free trade agreement, which will reduce or eliminate tariffs on a significant portion of traded goods between the two countries.
The agreement is expected to increase bilateral trade by 25% over the next five years, with India's exports to New Zealand projected to rise by 35% and New Zealand's exports to India by 20%.

The agreement will be implemented later this year, pending ratification by both countries' parliaments, and is expected to come into effect by the end of 2023, marking a significant milestone in the countries' economic relationship.

data.headline: 'Middle class is India's engine of growth': Nirmala Sitharaman on how reforms drive consumption

bullets: India's Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has identified the country's expanding middle class as the primary driver of its economic growth, citing the class's rising consumption and financial inclusion as key contributors to the economy.
The middle class currently represents around 31% of India's population and has been growing steadily at a 6.3% annual rate since the country's economic liberalisation in 1995.

The Finance Minister plans to sustain this growth through continued reforms and welfare initiatives, as announced during her speech at the Les Rencontres Économiques d'Aix-en-Provence 2026 conference in France.

data.headline: How El Niño could damage India’s economy | Explained

bullets: India's economy is vulnerable to damage due to a poor monsoon season, which can negatively impact agricultural output, rural income, and food prices.
A 40% deficit in the first month of the monsoon and a predicted "below-normal" rainfall in July pose significant challenges for various sectors, including agriculture and water resources.

The India Meteorological Department has warned of potential difficulties for ecosystem sustainability, hydropower generation, and drinking water availability, underscoring the need for preparedness and mitigation strategies.

data.headline: MHA designates 23 Pakistan-based individuals as ‘terrorists’ under UAPA

bullets: The Union Home Ministry has designated 23 Pakistan-based individuals as 'terrorists' under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) for their alleged involvement in various terror activities.

These designations cover individuals associated with Jaish-e-Mohammed, Lashkar-e-Taiba, Jamaat-ud-Dawa, and The Resistance Front, and are linked to terror attacks in India including the Sunjwan and Nagrota attacks.
The NIA will be empowered to block the finances, impose embargo on arms sales, and seize assets of the designated individuals as a result of the new listing.

data.headline: Absenteeism crackdown sparks calls for systemic reforms in T.N. public health sector

bullets: The Tamil Nadu Health Department initiated disciplinary action against 1,420 government doctors for unauthorised absenteeism and breach of service bond obligations.

The disciplinary action is reportedly in response to a shortage of 8,000 doctors in the public health sector in Tamil Nadu, with the State requiring an additional 25,000 personnel to meet its healthcare needs.

To address the systemic issues plaguing the public health workforce, government doctors have called for pay disparities, manpower shortages, extended duty hours, and workplace safety to be addressed through comprehensive reforms.

data.headline: No need for India to take a leaf out of Pakistan’s Iran mediation book, says envoy

bullets: India does not see value in mediating the Iran crisis due to a crowded field of mediators.
India has no current plans for Iran crisis mediation and has contributed in the past but sees no additional benefit.
The statement was made by Ambassador to China Vikram Doraiswami at the 14th World Peace Forum on July 4, 2026, in Beijing.

data.headline: Fifty Bangladeshi nationals from Attur detention camp sent to West Bengal by train for deportation

bullets: Fifty Bangladeshi nationals were deported and sent to West Bengal by train to facilitate their repatriation, comprising 44 men and six women previously lodged at the Attur detention camp in Salem district.

The deportation process involved a 40-member armed police team escorting the individuals on a specially designated coach on the Howrah Express, with the Tamil Nadu police set to formally hand over the nationals to the Border Security Force upon arrival.

The deportation was carried out following official orders, with the group being transported by road from the detention camp to Tiruchirappalli on July 3, amid tight security, before boarding the train on the same day.

data.headline: 2020 Delhi riots case: Court rejects fresh bail pleas of Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam

bullets: A Delhi court has rejected bail pleas filed by activists Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in connection with the 2020 Delhi riots case.
The Delhi court rejected two bail applications, which were filed after a Supreme Court bench raised objections to a coordinating bench's order denying them bail.
The bail pleas were rejected by Additional Sessions Judge Sameer Bajpai on July 4, 2026, in the larger conspiracy case related to the 2020 North East Delhi riots.

data.headline: Centre’s intervention to stabilise Andhra mango sector | Explained

bullets: The Centre has approved a two-pronged strategy to stabilise Andhra Pradesh's Totapuri mango sector, which generates an estimated annual turnover of over ₹4,000 crore.

The government will constitute a high-level expert panel and implement the Price Deficiency Payment (PDP) under the Market Intervention Scheme (MIS) to address the structural issues and price crashes in the industry.
The Price Deficiency Payment scheme is expected to provide relief to thousands of mango growers in Andhra Pradesh who are facing one of the sharpest price crashes in recent years.

data.headline: What is the copyright dispute between Saregama and Ilaiyaraaja? | Explained

bullets: The Delhi High Court ruled in favor of music label Saregama India Ltd. in its copyright dispute with composer Ilaiyaraaja, restraining him from broadcasting 134 films' songs until further orders.
The court held that Ilaiyaraaja enjoys copyright over his musical compositions but not over the sound recordings in the films, which are owned by the producer Saregama.

The copyright dispute between Saregama and Ilaiyaraaja dates back to 1976 and involves two copyright infringement suits filed by Saregama against the composer and a connected case with Black Madras Films.

data.headline: DMK MLA Anitha Radhakrishnan gets bail in case over remarks against T.N. CM Vijay
