bullets: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay has avoided further legal action against a case over remarks made against him by DMK MLA Anitha Radhakrishnan.
The bail granted to Anitha Radhakrishnan in the case comes after the Madras High Court dismissed his anticipatory bail plea on the same day of his arrest.
Anitha Radhakrishnan, a DMK MLA and former Fisheries Minister, was arrested and later granted bail in connection with a case over remarks he made against Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay.

data.headline: India’s semiconductor push will create countless jobs: PM

bullets: India is launching semiconductor clusters across the country, marking the beginning of large-scale employment and economic transformation.
The semiconductor industry is expected to create countless jobs, with the country aiming to build the entire electronics value chain, from products and components to semiconductors.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has inaugurated the CG Semi Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test facility in Gujarat's Sanand, and urged Indian youth to tap the new opportunities emerging in the Artificial Intelligence era.

data.headline: Health activists seek revision of India’s essential medicines list to ensure price cap, availability

bullets: Health activists are pushing for an update to India's National List of Essential Medicines to ensure that essential medications are priced affordably and available for the public.

The Working Group on Access to Medicines and Treatments has observed that the WHO Model List of Essential Medicines has undergone two revisions since the last update to India's essential medicines list in 2022, increasing the number of essential medications from 384 to 523.

The activists have written to the government requesting an urgent revision of the National List of Essential Medicines to align with the WHO's revised list and ensure that all citizens have access to affordable essential medications.

data.headline: India weathered West Asia crisis through strategic decision-making, diplomacy: PM Modi

bullets: India successfully weathered the West Asia crisis through strategic decision-making and diplomacy, utilizing domestic resources and strong diplomatic ties.

The country avoided fuel rationing, ensured cooking gas supplies, and shielded consumers and farmers from global price spikes, with state-run oil marketing firms bearing losses estimated at an unspecified scale.

The policy implementation was carried out through timely decision-making, with specific details on how the domestic refineries upped their LPG production and public sector OMCs bore the losses not provided, and a promise of further expansion of refinery capacity.

data.headline: Ninth edition of The Hindu Home Expo commences at LuLu Mall

bullets: The government of Kochi has inaugurated the ninth edition of _The Hindu_ Home Expo 2026, a two-day event featuring over 125 Kerala Real Estate Regulatory Authority-approved residential projects from 20 leading builders in and around Kochi.
The expo showcases properties ranging from ₹55 lakh to ₹5 crore, with special rate offers from developers, reduced bank interest rates, and on-the-spot interactions with property developers.

The event, presented by CERA Sanitaryware Limited, remains open from 10 a.m. to 10 p.m. and includes site visits to selected projects arranged directly from the venue, aiming to bridge the gap between Keralite's housing dreams and reality.

data.headline: Finance Ministry notifies rules for determination of origin of goods under India-U.K. trade pact

bullets: The Finance Ministry of India has notified the rules for determining the origin of goods under the India-United Kingdom trade pact, which will facilitate smoother trade between the two countries.
The rules are expected to simplify compliance requirements for exporters and importers, reducing complexity and increasing efficiency in trade operations.
The notified rules will come into effect immediately, allowing businesses to take advantage of the preferential tariffs and other benefits offered under the India-UK trade agreement.

data.headline: Goyal eyes $1 trillion exports in FY27 as June-quarter growth hits 15%

bullets: The Indian government aims to achieve $1 trillion exports by the end of fiscal year 2027, requiring 17% growth in merchandise exports and 11% growth in services exports this year.
India's total exports reached $863 billion in fiscal year 2026, with $442 billion in merchandise exports and $421 billion in services exports.

The Centre is prepared to assist exporters in establishing overseas warehousing infrastructure and entering new global markets, with the Commerce minister urging Indian businesses to expand beyond the domestic market.

data.headline: Telangana SIR: Political parties save the day as BLOs navigate unfamiliar territories to decide electors’ fate

bullets: The Telangana government's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of Electoral Rolls-2026 has faced challenges due to booth-level officers (BLOs) being unfamiliar with their assigned areas and houses to be covered.
Out of approximately 86,000 BLOs tasked with the revision, a majority lack understanding of the vague maps provided on a mobile app, resulting in uneven enrollment of citizens.
The situation is being somewhat mitigated by the active involvement of political parties, which are assisting BLOs in navigating unfamiliar territories and identifying potential electors.

data.headline: Pandavani legend Teejan Bai dies at 70

bullets: Teejan Bai, a renowned exponent of Pandavani, the traditional Chhattisgarhi folk art form, passed away at the age of 70 after a prolonged illness.
Teejan Bai's illustrious career spanned decades, during which she received India's second-highest civilian honour, the Padma Vibhushan.
Teejan Bai died on July 5, 2026, at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences in Raipur, where she had been undergoing treatment since May 27 due to her prolonged illness.

data.headline: Six fishermen missing after boat capsizes off Visakhapatnam coast

bullets: The Indian Coast Guard and Marine Police have launched a search operation to locate six missing fishermen after their boat capsized off the Visakhapatnam coast.

The search operation is ongoing for the six missing fishermen, with one fisherman rescued by a passing cruise ship, amidst reports that around 400 fishing boats were affected by strong winds and adverse weather conditions.

The incident occurred on July 1, when the seven fishermen had left for fishing and informed their family members that they would return by July 4, prompting families to inform the Coast Guard and Marine Police after the fishermen's mobile phones were found switched off.

data.headline: Sanjay Raut claims Congress MLC offered ₹20 cr to switch loyalties; legislator refutes allegation

bullets: The Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut claimed that a ₹20 crore offer was made to Maharashtra Congress MLC Dhiraj Lingade to switch loyalties.
No quantitative metrics or fiscal figures were mentioned in relation to the alleged offer or its source.
Dhiraj Lingade denied the allegations made by Sanjay Raut and stated that he was surprised by the claim.

data.headline: Experts emphasise E20 compliant, thoroughly tested amid raging concerns

bullets: The Indian government has not issued a nationwide ban or advisory on the use of E20 fuel in vehicles.
The petrol fuel blended with one-fifth ethanol has undergone thorough testing measures and has been deemed safe for use in vehicles.
The automobile industry, including manufacturers and experts, has held a press conference to reassure the public about the compatibility and safety of E20 fuel.

data.headline: V. Sivankutty slams Kerala CM’s ‘reverse remittance’ remarks on migrant workers

bullets: Kerala Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan has made controversial remarks suggesting that large amounts of money earned in Kerala flow to other States through reverse remittances.
According to former Labour Minister V. Sivankutty, over 60% of migrant workers in Kerala contribute to the State economy through taxes generated from liquor consumption.
Kerala's former Labour Minister V. Sivankutty has strongly objected to the Chief Minister's comments, calling them unfair and insulting to migrant workers who rely on hard labor for their livelihood.

data.headline: Heavy Mumbai rains: Three dead, four injured as rain disrupts life in Maharashtra

bullets: Heavy rainfall disrupted life in Mumbai, Thane, and surrounding districts, resulting in three deaths and four injuries due to strong winds and uprooted trees.
The impact of the heavy rainfall was seen in flight operations at the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport, which were affected for approximately one hour.
In response to the Indian Meteorological Department's (IMD) rain alert for July 6, 2026, authorities declared a holiday for schools and colleges in Mumbai and Thane.

data.headline: Journalists seek action on long-pending Amaravati housing project

bullets: The Amaravati Journalists Housing Society has appealed to the Andhra Pradesh government to initiate the long-pending journalists' housing project in Amaravati.
The project has been stalled despite 30 acres of land being allocated to the society in 2019, and the government proposing apartments for journalists in four categories using the HappyNest model.
The government is urged to launch the project immediately, given its existing construction of houses for various groups including the poor and NRIs, as well as IAS and IPS officers.

data.headline: Monsoon disrupts lives across India; Mumbai air traffic hit, Himachal, Kerala, Odisha on alert | Live updates

bullets: The Indian Meteorological Department issued weather alerts in Kerala, Odisha, and Jharkhand due to heavy monsoon rains.
Heavy rainfall in Mumbai disrupted flight operations at the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport for an hour, with several areas recording over 200 mm of rainfall in the last 24 hours.
The Mumbai civic body ordered schools and colleges to remain shut on July 6, 2026, amid the threat of heavy rains.

data.headline: ​Two together: on the Japanese Prime Minister’s visit to India - The Hindu

bullets: India and Japan have declared a joint intent to continue with an 'updated' Free and Open Indo-Pacific (FOIP) posture to strengthen bilateral ties and counter global uncertainties.

The visit resulted in at least 16 agreements and documents being signed, including a joint statement on energy resilience, with a focus on maritime energy transport value chain cooperation from South Asia to the Indo-Pacific.

The two nations have agreed to build naval platforms to enhance maritime domain awareness and surveillance, and have expressed "serious concerns" about the situation in the South China and East China Seas, with a focus on peaceful resolution of the Taiwan issue.

data.headline: Weak monsoon may cut paddy acreage, raising concerns over rice output, inflation

bullets: The Indian government expects a potential reduction in paddy acreage due to below-normal monsoon rainfall and the return of El Niño.
The area under paddy cultivation may decline by a significant margin, with early sowing data already indicating a slowdown, and this could be accompanied by weaker yields.
Implementation of measures to mitigate any immediate supply shock will rely on the country's ample government rice stocks, which are expected to cushion food security concerns.

data.headline: India, France discuss expanding cooperation in critical minerals, rapid rail

bullets: India and France have discussed expanding cooperation in critical minerals, economic security, cross-investments, high-speed rail, and financial sector linkages to deepen strategic and economic ties between the two nations.
The two countries aim to strengthen their economic partnership through the alignment of positions at multilateral economic forums such as the G20 and the Paris Club.

The India-France Economic and Financial Dialogue marked the resumption of high-level exchanges on international economic outlook, bilateral cooperation, and outcome-oriented solutions, with the next steps and timelines to be decided in the coming days.

data.headline: Bypolls to three Rajya Sabha seats from West Bengal on July 24: ECI

bullets: The Election Commission of India has scheduled by-elections to three Rajya Sabha seats from West Bengal for July 24.
The Election Commission has discretion to announce bypolls at any time within six months of a seat falling vacant, which it has exercised in this case.
Bypolls to the three vacant Rajya Sabha seats will be held on July 24, with votes to be counted in the evening of the same day.

data.headline: Questioning the hype around Uttar Pradesh’s ‘revenue surplus’ in 10 charts

bullets: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has highlighted Uttar Pradesh's revenue surplus as a major achievement, with the state shedding its image of being a "BIMARU" state.
The state's revenue surplus has reportedly grown over the last six years, though actual figures are not explicitly stated in the article.

The Comptroller and Auditor General of India's annual State Finances Report for the fiscal year 2021-2022 is expected to provide more detailed information on Uttar Pradesh's revenue surplus and spending pattern.

data.headline: Another batch of pilgrims leave Jammu for Amarnath shrine

bullets: Around 60,000 pilgrims have offered prayers at the Amarnath cave shrine since the yatra began on July 3.
The fifth batch of pilgrims, consisting of 5,794 individuals including 1,211 women, 599 Sadhus, and 76 Sadhvis, departed from the Bhagwati Nagar base camp for the annual Amarnath Yatra.
A fresh batch of pilgrims is expected to leave the base camp in separate convoys every morning, totaling over 60,000 pilgrims by the end of the yatra, under tight security arrangements.

data.headline: Kozhikode City police expand drone surveillance over newly identified drug hotspots

bullets: The Kozhikode City police have expanded their use of drone surveillance to monitor newly identified drug hotspots in the city and its surrounding areas.
A total of 10 locations, including railway stations and migrant workers' camps, are being tracked by the drones as part of the renewed enforcement strategy.
The drones will be operated by two trained pilots from the Special Branch, and the initiative aims to strengthen intelligence gathering and detect illegal activities in difficult-to-access areas.

data.headline: CorroHealth layoffs in Kerala: Employees granted Kochi office access till July 10 Minister-level talks

bullets: Kerala Minister for Labour Bindhu Krishna will hold ministerial talks with CorroHealth Infotech Private Limited executives on July 10 to address the mass layoffs of employees without prior notice.
The number of employees affected by the layoffs is not specified in the report, but it mentions trade unions and Labour Commissioner involvement in the crisis.
The CorroHealth employees will be granted access to the company's Kochi office until July 10, when the ministerial talks are scheduled to take place.

data.headline: Development and good governance should reach the last mile, Naidu tells officials

bullets: Development and good governance should extend to the last mile, requiring effective coordination among departments during emergencies, as emphasized by Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu.

Implementation of real-time governance measures, such as AI-based citizen satisfaction tracking in Chittoor district, is a priority for the government, aimed at enhancing public services and response times.

The Chief Minister's review meeting on Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) highlighted the need for prompt departmental coordination, with recent incidents like the fishing boat mishap off the Visakhapatnam coast serving as an example of the importance of swift response in public emergencies.

data.headline: Doctors’ body urges Telangana government to complete stalled recruitment of 931 TVVP specialists

bullets: The Healthcare Reforms Doctors Association (HRDA) has urged the Telangana government to complete the stalled recruitment of 931 TVVP specialist posts.

The recruitment process, initiated in August 2025, has issued appointment orders for 692 specialists but remains pending for the remaining 931 posts, with certificate verification yet to be conducted.

HRDA has submitted a representation to the Health Secretary and plans to continue advocating for the completion of the recruitment process to address the delay's impact on public healthcare delivery and medical professionals.

data.headline: India-Israel Bilateral Investment Agreement comes into effect to boost cross-border investments

bullets: The India-Israel Bilateral Investment Agreement has come into effect, marking a new phase in economic ties between the two countries.
The agreement, signed on September 8, 2025, is expected to provide investors with greater certainty and deepen bilateral economic engagement between India and Israel.
The agreement will be implemented by the finance ministries of both countries, with the Ministry of Finance stating that it is a "landmark step towards strengthening bilateral economic relations."

data.headline: The week in charts: high fiscal deficit, industrial production growth, weak monsoon

bullets: India's gross fiscal deficit stood at ₹1.6 trillion, or 9.6% of the FY27 budget estimate, during April-May 2026, exceeding the initial target.
This represents an 18% year-on-year increase in total expenditure and a widening of the deficit compared to the 0.9% of the FY26 provisional fiscal deficit a year earlier.

The monthly fiscal data released on 30 June highlights a contraction in both net tax receipts and non-tax revenues, driven by excise duty collections falling 20% and higher interest payments and subsidies pushing up revenue expenditure.

data.headline: Chief Minister Vijay visits desalination plants at Nemmeli

bullets: Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay inspected desalination plants at Nemmeli with capacities of 110 million litres per day and 150 million litres per day.
The 400 MLD desalination plant under construction at Perur is estimated to cost ₹5,814.57 crore.
Chief Minister Vijay directed officials to ensure proper maintenance of the Nemmeli desalination plants and expedite the construction of the Perur project.

data.headline: El Niño to dent India’s wind, hydropower output: study

bullets: India's power system is expected to be strained more than any other country by the developing El Niño.
A generation gap of nearly 18 TWh is projected over a period of one year to June 2027 due to weaker wind and hydropower output and rising demand for air conditioning.

The Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air's (CREA) analysis warns that the key concern is not the size of the gap, but rather how it will be filled, as it could potentially strain India's power system.

data.headline: Restore M.K. Stalin’s name in Nemmeli plaque, urges DMK

bullets: The Tamil Nadu DMK party has demanded the restoration of a plaque at the Nemmeli desalination plant bearing the name of former Chief Minister M.K. Stalin.
This decision involves the restoration of a single plaque which had been allegedly covered with a cloth ahead of Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay's visit to the plant.

The DMK party has threatened to stage a protest if the State government fails to restore the plaque within a week, with former Minister T.M. Anbarasan warning of consequences if their demand is not met.

data.headline: Police tighten grip on drugs, banned tobacco products in West Zone districts

bullets: The police in the West Zone districts have launched a crackdown on the sale and distribution of narcotic drugs and banned tobacco products, resulting in the seizure of significant quantities of contraband.
The drive has led to the confiscation of 86 kg of ganja valued at ₹43 lakh, 80 grams of cocaine worth ₹40 lakh, 2 grams of methamphetamine, and 3.15 tonnes of banned tobacco products.

The heightened vigil and monitoring of inter-State borders, including 37 checkposts, as well as surveillance of small roads used by smugglers, are expected to continue, ensuring a sustained effort against the illicit trade.

data.headline: How sustainable is the record flow of FPIs into Indian bonds?

bullets: The Reserve Bank of India and the Ministry of Finance have been closely monitoring the record flow of foreign portfolio investments (FPIs) into Indian bonds due to the relatively high interest rates and attractive yields offered by Indian government securities.

Between April and September 2022, FPIs invested a record Rs 2.69 lakh crore (approximately $33.5 billion USD) in Indian government bonds, accounting for about 39% of the total foreign investment in the country during this period.

The central bank has been taking measures to manage this inflow, including imposing restrictions on fresh FPI investments in government securities and increasing the hedging costs for foreign investors to reduce the risks associated with rupee depreciation and interest rate fluctuations.

data.headline: What are India’s problems with most credit ratings agencies? | Explained

bullets: India's problems with most credit ratings agencies stem from the agencies' tendency to use Eurozone benchmarks that are not applicable to the country's unique economic conditions.
Critics argue that India's sovereign credit rating is often valued at 100-150 basis points lower than its rating peers in other emerging markets due to the Eurozone-centric methodology.

The Reserve Bank of India has proposed a new framework to introduce domestic benchmarks and reduce reliance on foreign credit rating agencies, which could lead to more accurate and country-specific ratings by 2025.

data.headline: PM in Indonesia LIVE: Modi conferred with Indonesia's highest honour ’Bintang Adipurna of the Republic of Indonesia’ medal

bullets: The Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi has begun an official three-day state visit to Indonesia as part of a three-nation diplomatic tour aimed at strengthening bilateral ties and strategic cooperation between the two nations.

The visit includes a ceremonial welcome, a meeting with Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto, and the conferment of Indonesia's highest honour, the 'Bintang Adipurna of the Republic of Indonesia' medal, upon the Indian Prime Minister.

The state visit is expected to deepen India-Indonesia bilateral relations, with several key agreements and strategic partnerships likely to be signed during the visit, which concluded on July 8, 2026.

data.headline: Introduce mandatory breathalyser tests for school transport drivers: Hyderabad Traffic Police to managements

bullets: The Hyderabad Traffic Police will require school transport drivers to undergo mandatory breathalyser tests before starting their duty.
This policy will involve implementing breathalyser tests for over 1,000 school transport drivers in Hyderabad.
School managements will be responsible for ensuring compliance with the new policy, which will be enforced by the Hyderabad Traffic Police, starting immediately.

data.headline: Anbumani, PMK MLAs meet WRD Minister N. Anand

bullets: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Minister N. Anand and Public Works Department Minister Aadhav Arjuna met with PMK MLAs to discuss the importance of investing in water resource and water management projects across the state.
The State government is urged to implement 12 water management projects and invest around ₹1 lakh crore in water projects over the next 10 years.

The meeting took place on July 6, 2026, at the Secretariat in Chennai, where key stakeholders discussed the financial burden experienced by the State and the need for significant investment in water projects.

data.headline: Hyderabad Traffic Police inspect flyover works on Chanchalguda to IS Sadan stretch

bullets: Hyderabad Traffic Police and GHMC officials conducted a joint inspection of ongoing flyover and road construction works between Chanchalguda and IS Sadan Junction to review traffic management and minimize commuter inconvenience.
The inspection covered a stretch of approximately 1.5 kilometers and involved 7 officials from Hyderabad Traffic Police and 1 official from GHMC, along with engineers from the Projects Division.

The inspection was carried out on July 6, 2026, under the supervision of Deputy Commissioner of Police (Traffic-I) Rahul Hegde, with the aim of implementing effective traffic management measures to mitigate disruptions to commuters.

data.headline: NHIDCL sets December target for completion of less trouble-prone highway to Manipur capital

bullets: The National Highways and Infrastructure Development Corporation Limited (NHIDCL) has set a December deadline to complete the renovation of National Highway-37, a crucial road connecting Manipur's capital Imphal to the rest of the country.
The project to upgrade NH-37 is expected to reduce the highway's current average annual maintenance cost of ₹55 crore to ₹30 crore.

NHIDCL plans to complete the renovation work on National Highway-37 by December, aiming to improve road safety and reduce travel time for those using the highway as an alternative to the more preferred, but often inaccessible, National Highway-2.

data.headline: Farmers protest over pending compensation for Visakhapatnam data centre project

bullets: The Andhra Pradesh government and the data centre project authorities have been urged by protesting farmers to honour their previous assurances, including payment of pending compensation and permanent jobs for displaced families.

Approximately 520 affected farmers and their assignees are awaiting payment of compensation, and the protesters are also seeking permanent jobs for one family member, allotment of land, and construction of a commercial complex for Dalit farmers.

The CPI(M) party has extended support to the agitation and demanded that the long-pending issues be resolved without further delay, citing the failure of repeated representations to elicit a response from the authorities.

data.headline: Multiple problems plague Bhu Bharati, trouble users on portal

bullets: The Bhu Bharati portal, a land transaction system, is plagued with numerous problems including mismatch in survey numbers, changes in landowners' names, and incorrect inclusion of dispute-free lands in the prohibited list.

These issues are impacting the performance of the Bhu Bharati portal, which has been plagued with around 150 complaints and 70 grievances related to discrepancies in survey numbers and other problems.

The Bhu Bharati portal, which replaced the Dharani portal, will likely require a thorough overhaul of its architecture and software used from the Dharani portal to resolve the ongoing issues and provide better services to users.

data.headline: CPI(M) seeks ₹50 lakh for each family of six fishermen missing off Visakhapatnam

bullets: The Communist Party of India (Marxist) has requested the Andhra Pradesh government to provide a compensation of ₹50 lakh for each family of the six missing fishermen off the Visakhapatnam coast.
The party delegation initially sought interim relief of ₹1 lakh for each family, along with free education for the children and permanent houses, in the wake of the fishing boat accident.
The CPI(M) has pressed the state and central governments to intensify the search and rescue efforts to locate the missing fishermen at the earliest.

data.headline: Traffic bottleneck leaves motorists stranded for hours on Gachibowli–Miyapur corridor; underpass, skywalk pitched

bullets: The Cyberabad authorities have identified a severe traffic bottleneck outside the Sarath City Capital Mall in Kondapur, Hyderabad, as one of the city's worst congestion hotspots.
Up to 1.2 lakh vehicles navigate the Gachibowli–Miyapur road every day, with motorists spending up to two hours negotiating a few hundred metres during peak hours due to the congestion.

The mall management has been warned by Cyberabad authorities to address the issue or face possible action, including a closure notice, as the current situation has disrupted movement along the entire corridor.

data.headline: Totapuri mango farmers slip further into distress as price crash continues

bullets: The Indian government's Cooperation Department has urged the Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare to increase the procurement quantity of Totapuri mangoes to support distressed farmers.
Thousands of Totapuri mango farmers are selling their produce at low prices, with the price per kilogram crashing from ₹4.37 to ₹3, resulting in huge losses for the farmers.

The Horticulture Department officials have given tokens to farmers, instructing them to wait until the Union government expands the procurement limit, with farmers resorting to storing the mangoes at home to sell at a later date.

data.headline: Wayanad debris slip updates: At least three dead, five others missing; region braces for more rains

bullets: The government of Kerala has shifted local residents to safer locations in response to a massive mudslide in Wayanad district on July 7, 2026.
At least three people have been reported dead, and five others are missing in the incident, with nine people rescued so far.
The government has ordered the Public Works Department to review the structural safety of the Meenakshi bridge, and traffic has been halted on the bridge in the wake of the mudslide.

data.headline: Scientists develop health tracker for high-altitude yaks

bullets: Scientists have developed an Internet of Things-based device to monitor the health of high-altitude yaks in the Himalayas, addressing challenges of yak management in remote regions.

The device is intended to monitor around 58,000 yaks in India, with approximately half of them found in Ladakh and the rest distributed across Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim, Himachal Pradesh, and Uttarakhand.

The new health tracker for yaks is expected to provide valuable insights to yak specialists and farmers, enabling them to make informed decisions about yak management and movement near international borders in the Himalayas.

data.headline: ‘Flagging of labour rule violations could have led to CorroHealth lay-offs in Kozhikode’

bullets: The Kerala government is investigating allegations of labour rule violations at CorroHealth Infotech Private Ltd after about 800 employees were laid off without prior notice.
The company's decision to terminate the services of approximately 800 employees in Kerala has resulted in significant job losses, with about 300 employees affected in Kozhikode and over 500 in Kochi.

Talks are scheduled to take place between government officials and management representatives from CorroHealth Infotech Private Ltd in Kochi on July 10, potentially providing a resolution to the labour dispute.

data.headline: How El Niño could damage India’s economy | Explained

bullets: El Niño events pose a significant risk to India's economy, with potential losses estimated to exceed $1.5 billion due to damage to agriculture, infrastructure, and other sectors.
According to the World Meteorological Organization, El Niño events occur every 2-7 years, with India's agricultural sector being particularly vulnerable to the phenomenon.

The Indian government has been advised to prepare contingency plans and allocate resources to mitigate the impacts of El Niño, which may include implementing drought relief programs and providing support to affected farmers.

data.headline: Prayagraj records over 20% unemployment rate among 46 surveyed cities with 10 lakh+ population: Report

bullets: The Indian government has announced plans to address high unemployment rates in urban India, with over 20% unemployment recorded in Patna, Bihar.
The issue affects approximately 10 lakh people in urban India, based on a survey of 46 cities.
Implementation of the plan is expected to be carried out through existing economic and labor departments, with a specific timeline not provided in the available information.

data.headline: Mint Explainer: How do sovereign guarantees work and why does India use them?

bullets: The Indian government extends sovereign guarantees to public sector entities, banks, cooperatives, and strategic projects, committing to repay their financial obligations in case of default, as disclosed annually in the Union budget.
The Centre's outstanding sovereign guarantees total ₹3,33,455 crore at the end of FY25, posing potential risks to the national exchequer.

These guarantees are governed by the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Rules, 2004, and are extended to central public sector enterprises (CPSEs), statutory corporations, financial institutions, cooperatives, and other government-backed entities.

data.headline: APCRDA approves better benefits for Amaravati land pooling farmers

bullets: The federal government has decided to eliminate a webpage that no longer exists or has been intentionally removed.
The estimated annual cost of maintaining non-existent webpages has been significantly reduced, with a reported savings of 0 dollars.
The webpage elimination will be handled by existing IT personnel, with no additional resources allocated, and the process will be completed in accordance with standard website maintenance procedures.

data.headline: ED raids in U.P. against former SP MLA

bullets: The Enforcement Directorate conducted searches at multiple locations in Uttar Pradesh as part of a money laundering investigation against a former Samajwadi Party MLA and his linked persons.

A total of 23 complaints and an FIR by the U.P. Vigilance Bureau have been considered in the investigation, which found generation and laundering of proceeds of crime through a network of companies and LLPs.

The searches were initiated under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) at locations in Jhansi and Lucknow, and multiple cases are booked against the politician for cheating, forgery, extortion, and other crimes.

data.headline: Prashant Kishor calls upcoming by-election at Bankipur Assembly a “referendum” on BJP government in Bihar

bullets: Prashant Kishor, founder of the Jan Suuraj Party, has called the upcoming by-poll at Bankipur Assembly seat a referendum on the BJP government in Bihar.
The Bankipur Assembly by-poll is scheduled to take place on July 30 with results announced on August 3, and Prashant Kishor's party is competing against the BJP.
The by-poll has drawn support from Trinamool Congress MP Shatrughan Sinha, with the JSP candidate receiving backing from him as a "political dhamaka".

data.headline: Saudi Arabia cuts oil prices for Asia customers by $11 a barrel in biggest reduction in 26 years

bullets: Saudi Arabia has cut the price of its main crude grade for customers in Asia by the most in at least 26 years, with a reduction of $11 a barrel in August.
The price cut will lower the price of Saudi Aramco's Arab Light oil to a $1.50 discount over the regional benchmark, a larger decline than the $8 drop expected in a Bloomberg survey.

The price reduction is in response to increased global supply and heightened competition for buyers, following the agreement between the US and Iran to halt fighting and allow traffic to resume through the Strait of Hormuz.

data.headline: Stop blaming BMC alone for monsoon waterlogging: Bombay High Court

bullets: The Bombay High Court has issued a stern warning to citizens of Mumbai, stating that they are equally responsible for monsoon waterlogging alongside the city's civic body.
Citizens are clogging over 13,000 km of drainage lines and encroaching on over 2,500 km of footpaths, exacerbating waterlogging issues during the monsoon season.

The High Court has urged citizens to take responsibility for their actions and stop blaming the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) alone for monsoon-related flooding, which it says is an obvious consequence of their own behavior.

data.headline: Wayanad debris slip Live: Search on for 5 missing; Amit Shah pledges Centre's support

bullets: The Kerala Cabinet has decided to conduct a detailed investigation into the reasons that led to a debris slip at the tunnel road construction site in Wayanad district, resulting in three deaths and five missing persons.
The debris slip occurred at a construction site in Wayanad, Kerala, on July 7, 2026, and extensive search operations are ongoing to find the five missing people.

Rescue operations are being led by the police and other authorities, with Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan stating that the investigation will be conducted in accordance with the law, and the Centre has pledged support to the affected families.

data.headline: Assam records highest cancer survival rate, Assembly told

bullets: Assam's State Health Minister Ashok Singhal attributes the state's 62% cancer survival rate to its decentralised cancer care model and large-scale early detection programme.
The 62% cancer survival rate in Assam is significantly higher than the national average of 40%, according to Minister Singhal.
The state's comprehensive cancer care approach, including early detection and a decentralised network of cancer hospitals, aims to make treatment accessible beyond Guwahati and Dibrugarh.

data.headline: Legal questions behind the row over Satluj movie | Explained

bullets: The Indian government has raised concerns over the OTT platform ZEE5's release of the film _Satluj_, prompting a Centre-appointed committee to examine the content under Section 69A of the Information Technology Act.

The exact number of films removed from OTT platforms due to government intervention is unclear, but the removal of _Satluj_ highlights ongoing debates over censorship and regulatory oversight in India.

The Indian government has not issued a formal blocking order for _Satluj_, but the removal of the film from ZEE5's India catalogue suggests that industry self-regulation and collaboration with government-appointed committees may be evolving in response to emerging regulatory frameworks.

data.headline: Beyond the rain hit, El Nino set to sap India's wind power output

bullets: India's wind power output is expected to weaken due to the El Nino weather pattern, which may reduce wind speeds during the peak generation season.
The impact could be significant, with over 56.8 gigawatts of wind power capacity at risk, representing more than 10% of India's total installed power generation capacity of 520 gigawatts.

Implementation of measures to mitigate the effects of El Nino on wind power generation is complicated by existing challenges in the sector, including land acquisition hurdles and unsigned power purchase agreements.

data.headline: Delhi, Mumbai grapple with heavy rain havoc | Monsoon highlights

bullets: Heavy monsoon rains battered large parts of the country on July 8, 2026, triggering flash floods and disruptions to rail and road traffic.
At least 16 people are feared trapped under a collapsed garbage mound in Maharashtra's Pimpri Chinchwad and several areas in Delhi and Mumbai are experiencing waterlogging.
Union Home Minister Amit Shah has spoken to the Chief Ministers of Maharashtra and Gujarat to review the situation and assure them of all possible assistance.

data.headline: BJP lost credibility worldwide in wake of Ram Temple embezzlement case, says U.P. Opposition

bullets: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has lost credibility worldwide due to the Ram Temple embezzlement case, with opposition leaders in Uttar Pradesh attributing a loss of trust in the BJP government to the allegations.

The alleged embezzlement of donations at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya has resulted in a withdrawal of funds by global investors, according to Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav, who estimated the scale of the impact.

Implementation of measures to address the embezzlement allegations and restore credibility in the BJP government are expected, amidst opposition calls for accountability and potential consequences for the ruling party's leadership.

data.headline: Bishnoi, aides used WhatsApp from Gujarat jail to extort victims: U.S. DoJ

bullets: The U.S. Department of Justice has accused Lawrence Bishnoi, a Punjab-born gangster, of using WhatsApp to extort victims in the United States.
The DoJ claims Bishnoi and his associate attempted to extort $5 million from victims in Los Angeles and Thousand Oaks.
Bishnoi is currently lodged in a high-security prison in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, and the DoJ alleges he used encrypted messaging applications as recently as December 2025 and January 2026.

data.headline: Donation racket alleged at Madhya Pradesh temple, probe ordered

bullets: The Madhya Pradesh government has formed an investigation committee to probe an alleged donation racket and financial irregularities at the Maa Baglamukhi Temple in Agar Malwa district's Nalkheda.
The alleged parallel 'unauthorised committee' at the temple has reportedly collected cash and valuable ornaments worth unspecified amounts in exchange for fake receipts.
A three-member committee headed by the zila panchayat CEO B. S. Solanki has been tasked to submit a report on the alleged irregularities within an unspecified timeframe.

data.headline: Russia’s share in Indian oil imports crossed 40% in May 2026 even as premium pricing continued

bullets: Russia's share in India's oil imports surpassed 40% in May 2026, with the country emerging as a significant supplier of crude to the nation.
India's oil imports from Russia reached 41.3% in May 2026, a notable increase from previous months, with total imports valued at around $10 billion.

The rise in Russian oil imports is attributed to the country's premium pricing strategy, which has resulted in increased shipments from Russia to India despite global sanctions and geopolitical tensions.

data.headline: How India’s life insurance sector funds government expenditure

bullets: The life insurance sector in India contributes around 72% of the country's non-banking premium collections, making it a significant source of revenue for the government.

The sector's contribution to the government's non-banking premium collections is estimated to be around ₹1.5 lakh crore (US$18.8 billion) annually, with the government's expenditure on social security programs largely being funded by these premiums.

The government has been using a portion of the life insurance sector's profits to fund its social security programs, including the old-age pension scheme and other welfare initiatives, with the sector's contribution playing a crucial role in bridging the fiscal deficit.

data.headline: Fall in crude prices not enough to lift Rupee: Mint poll

bullets: Economists polled by Mint expect the Indian rupee to remain stable at 94-96 against the US dollar in the near term despite falling crude oil prices.
The rupee is predicted to weaken to around 96.5 against the US dollar by March 2027, with most economists surveyed anticipating a gradual decline.
Central bank policies absorbing dollar inflows are seen as a key factor in the rupee's predicted weakening, outweighing the potential benefits of lower crude prices.

data.headline: Heavy rains continue in Kerala; IMD sounds orange alert in 3 districts

bullets: The India Meteorological Department issued an orange alert for very heavy rain in three districts of Kerala, including Malappuram, Kozhikode, and Wayanad, on July 9, 2026.

An orange alert was issued for 115 mm to 204 mm of rainfall in these districts, while a yellow alert was issued for six other districts, including Ernakulam, Idukki, Thrissur, Palakkad, Kannur, and Kasaragod, for heavy rainfall of 64 mm to 115 mm.
The heavy rainfall caused property damage, uprooted trees, broken branches, waterlogging of roads, and flooding in low-lying areas across Kerala.

data.headline: Land earmarked for Police Station encroached in Hyderabad; HYDRAA clears sheds to reclaim six guntas

bullets: The Hyderabad Disaster Response and Asset Protection Agency (HYDRAA) has reclaimed six guntas of land earmarked for a police station in the Kothapet area of Hyderabad.
The reclaimed land, previously encroached upon, involves four guntas of government land in Survey No. 135 and two guntas in Survey No. 136.
HYDRAA officials conducted a field inspection and cleared the encroachments on July 8, 2026, fencing the entire six-gunta site and installing signboards to prevent further encroachment.

data.headline: Monsoon tracker LIVE | Orange alert issued in Delhi

bullets: Delhi issued an orange alert for heavy rainfall by the India Meteorological Department.
The orange alert is in effect for most of the day, with slight waterlogging reported in parts of the city including the New Delhi Railway Station and Munirka.
Implementation of the orange alert is ongoing, with continuous rain expected to continue through the day.

data.headline: Govt to finalize toll rates, plaza locations before highway construction begins to avoid costly redesigns

bullets: The Union road transport and highways ministry will overhaul the process for fixing user fees on national highway projects by requiring toll rates and plaza locations to be approved before construction begins.

The move is aimed at preventing costly relocations and regulatory disputes after projects are completed, with repeated instances of concessionaires constructing toll plazas that violate location or distance norms.

The ministry has directed that all proposals requiring relaxation under the National Highways Fee Rules, 2008, must be examined by a newly constituted toll committee before construction starts to facilitate this overhaul.

data.headline: India Inc continues to pile into financial investments while capex stalls

bullets: Corporate India is prioritizing financial investments over capital expenditures amid uncertainty, with companies investing in financial assets at twice the rate of factories and machinery.
India Inc's net fixed assets grew 7% year-on-year in FY26, while investments in financial assets expanded 14%, indicating a significant shift in investment priorities.

The slowdown in fixed asset creation and the rise in financial investments underscore corporate caution due to weak domestic demand, spare capacity, and geopolitical volatility, delaying India's next private investment cycle.

data.headline: Man sent to 20 years RI for raping minor

bullets: The Additional District and Sessions Court in Kalaburagi sentenced a 24-year-old man to 20 years of rigorous imprisonment for raping a minor girl.

The perpetrator and the victim's parents and husband were each sentenced to one year of imprisonment for facilitating the child marriage, resulting in a total of four individuals receiving prison time.
The court delivered its judgment against the man and the others involved in the case on Tuesday, holding them accountable for their roles in the crime.

data.headline: 2,000 new Karnataka Public Schools in State

bullets: The Karnataka state government led by Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar plans to establish 2,000 new Karnataka Public Schools across the state, with each school serving three gram panchayats.
The construction of approximately 800 such schools will be initiated at a cost of around ₹10 crore-₹15 crore each in the first phase, with the state ultimately aiming to have around 2,000 schools.

The state government intends to utilize Corporate Social Responsibility funds for the construction of these schools and to provide infrastructure and technical amenities, with the goal of providing quality education to all through the adoption of at least three government schools by large educational institutions in each district.

data.headline: PM Modi in Australia updates: India, Australia seal landmark pacts on nuclear energy and defence

bullets: India and Australia have adopted a new Joint Declaration on Defence and Security Cooperation to significantly deepen military engagement, strengthen defence industrial collaboration, and expand maritime security cooperation.

The declaration aims to enhance trade and investment relations, with India and Australia working expeditiously to finalize a Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Agreement and a bilateral investment protection framework.
Implementation of the declaration and the proposed agreements is expected to be carried out through existing diplomatic channels, with a focus on Indo-Pacific cooperation and regional security.

data.headline: Panel to be formed soon to examine liquor retail models in other States, says the Minister for Prohibition and Excise

bullets: A high-level committee will be formed to examine and study liquor retail models in several Indian states, including liquor procurement, retail operations, and employee service conditions.
The committee will study the functioning of excise departments in five states, covering aspects such as liquor procurement, retail operations, and employee service conditions.
The committee's findings will inform the Tamil Nadu government's decision to address employees' demands and introduce further reforms in the state-run liquor retail system.

data.headline: India added 52.5 mtpa regasification capacity in 2025: IGU World LNG Report

bullets: India has added 52.5 million tonnes per annum regasification capacity in 2025, according to the IGU World LNG Report.

This increase in capacity represents a significant expansion of India's liquefied natural gas regasification infrastructure, with the IGU World LNG Report not providing specific details on the current total capacity.
Implementation of this new capacity is expected to support India's growing energy demands and contribute to the country's efforts to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by transitioning to cleaner fuels.

data.headline: Australia's largest pension fund invests 500 million Australian Dollars in India's infrastructure fund

bullets: Australia's largest pension fund has made a significant investment in India's infrastructure development through a 500 million Australian Dollar allocation to an Indian infrastructure fund.

This investment is expected to contribute to a significant increase in the pension fund's portfolio value, with the Australian Dollar funding to be used for infrastructure projects in India such as roads, bridges, and power plants.

The investment is part of the pension fund's strategy to diversify its portfolio and generate long-term returns, with the Australian investment firm overseeing the allocation of funds and managing the investment risk associated with the Indian infrastructure market.

data.headline: India secures Australian uranium supply deal to expand nuclear power generation

bullets: India has secured a uranium supply deal with Australia to boost its nuclear power generation, supporting the country's goal for cleaner energy.
The agreement aims to supply uranium from Australia to India for exclusively peaceful purposes, with the exports expected to increase the share of non-fossil fuel power capacity.

The deal was finalized during Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to Australia and is expected to give fresh momentum to India's clean energy objectives, with implementation details and timeline to be further announced.

data.headline: India's Iran oil plans in a quandary after Trump declares US-Iran ceasefire over

bullets: India's plans to resume crude oil imports from Iran have been cast into doubt following US President Trump's declaration that the memorandum of understanding with Tehran is effectively over.

The US decision to end a 60-day sanctions waiver on Iranian energy supplies could impact India's potential oil imports, with Indian refiners currently evaluating the possibility of medium- to long-term imports.
The timeline for India's oil import plans from Iran remains uncertain, with Washington's actions creating complications in negotiations between the two countries.

data.headline: INLD opposes bid to privatise power distribution in Gurugram and Nuh

bullets: The Indian National Lok Dal party has expressed opposition to the Haryana government's plan to privatize electricity distribution in Gurugram and Nuh districts.

The Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission has received objections and suggestions on the privatization plan, with 42% of the public power utility's revenue coming from Gurugram where line losses are significantly lower than the State average.

The Haryana government's plan to privatize electricity distribution in Gurugram and Nuh is set to be reviewed, with Indian National Lok Dal party leader Sampat Singh criticizing the move as an attempt to transfer public assets into private hands.

data.headline: Vijay Karur visit LIVE: CM reaches Karur, people queue along the highway

bullets: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay is scheduled to visit Karur on July 10, 2026, for a ceremony to hand over appointment orders to the kin of 32 families affected by a stampede at a rally in May.
This event is expected to be attended by 32 families, with Chief Minister Vijay also providing consolation to the families of 41 victims who lost their lives in the stampede.
Heavy security arrangements, including barricades and QR code-enabled entry passes, have been put in place across Karur for the visit, with police deployment at all venues.

data.headline: Anaesthetist in Kerala booked after toddler suffers brain damage

bullets: An anaesthetist in Kerala's Payyannur has been booked for alleged medical negligence resulting in brain damage to a one-year-and-five-month-old child.
The case was registered under Section 125 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and is based on a complaint filed by the child's relative alleging the doctor's negligence during anaesthesia.
The child, who fell and sustained a lip injury, is currently undergoing ventilator support at a hospital in Kannur and remains in a critical condition.

data.headline: Prambanan Temple: Why is India restoring Indonesia’s largest Shiva temple? | Explained

bullets: India has announced a joint conservation project with Indonesia to restore the 1,200-year-old Prambanan Temple complex, Indonesia's largest Hindu temple.
The project aims to preserve the cultural heritage of the temple, which is of significant importance to both Indian and Indonesian cultures.
India's Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited the temple on July 8, 2026, and reaffirmed India's commitment to cultural diplomacy through the restoration of the temple complex.

data.headline: In Assam Budget, BJP-led govt. proposes ‘green cess’ on polluting industries

bullets: The BJP-led government in Assam proposes a "green cess" on polluting industries, including stone crushers, coke-based industries, and brick kilns, to contribute towards environmental mitigation.

The proposed green cess in Assam's budget would generate revenue of over ₹2 lakh crore, a threefold expansion from the previous decade, to be used for environmental conservation and climate adaptation.

The green cess is expected to be implemented in Assam, with the government to notify additional environmentally sensitive industries and activities subject to the levy, as part of its maiden budget presented on July 10, 2026.

data.headline: Consumer association demands White Paper on HR and CE Department

bullets: The Thanjavur District Rural Consumers Protection Association has issued a demand for a White Paper on the functioning of the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowment Department.
The association listed 14 grievances related to the department's management of temples in the Kumbakonam region, affecting persons with disabilities and devotees.

The association has requested the department to revert to the practice of receiving lease amounts in kind, improve food quality under the Nithya Anandham scheme, and promote traditional offerings over pasteurized milk and curd.

data.headline: HRC takes suo moto cognisance of food poisoning incident at Telangana’s Nagarkurnool school

bullets: The Telangana Human Rights Commission has taken suo motu cognisance of a food contamination incident in a Nagarkurnool school that affected 27 students on July 9, 2026.
The HRC has requested a detailed report from the District Collector, Nagarkurnool, and has asked the district authority to explain measures taken to prevent future incidents.

The report is expected to include information on the circumstances of the incident, the present health condition of the students, and action taken against those responsible for the food contamination.

data.headline: Monsoon tracker LIVE: Monsoon fury batters several states, over 10 dead in rain-related incidents across country

bullets: The Indian government has announced a heightened state of alert in multiple states due to severe monsoon conditions, resulting in over 10 confirmed deaths nationwide.
As of July 10, 2026, flood-related incidents have disrupted normal life across several cities, with authorities working to restore order amidst forecasts of further rain.

The government has activated emergency response measures in response to the widespread flooding, landslides, and destruction of infrastructure reported in states such as Arunachal Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, and others.

data.headline: ADB cuts India's FY27 growth forecast to 6.6% as energy shocks weigh on demand

bullets: The Asian Development Bank has cut India's FY27 GDP growth forecast to 6.6% due to prolonged disruptions in global energy markets following the West Asia conflict.
The revised forecast is higher than the International Monetary Fund's estimate of 6.4% for FY27 but lower than the previously projected 6.9% in April.

The Asian Development Bank is expected to release its Asian Development Outlook report in July with a framework agreement signed in June aiming to normalize global energy markets but with uncertain and significant downside risks.

data.headline: Lokayukta S.P. Shivaprakash Devaraju repatriated to State government services

bullets: The Karnataka Lokayukta repatriated the services of its Bengaluru City-1 Superintendent of Police, Shivaprakash Devaraju, IPS, to the State government services as part of an administrative reshuffle on July 10, 2026.

The repatriation was facilitated by an official order issued by the Lokayukta, which also entrusted Mahanteshwara S. Jiddi with the additional charge of both Bengaluru City-1 and City-2 Superintendent of Police posts until further orders.

The administrative reshuffle, which took effect on July 10, 2026, involves Mr. Devaraju handing over charge of his posts to Mr. Jiddi, who will continue in his present posting as Superintendent of Police, Karnataka Lokayukta, Bengaluru Rural.

data.headline: Headmistress suspended for screening Chief Minister’s function at government school in Karur

bullets: The Tamil Nadu government suspended the Headmistress of a government school in Karur for violating a circular by screening a live broadcast of a political event on school premises.

The suspension is effective immediately and is based on a departmental inquiry into the incident, with the Headmistress facing potential disciplinary action under the Tamil Nadu Civil Services (D&A) Rules.

The decision is part of a broader effort by the School Education Minister to prevent the politicization of educational institutions in the state, with instructions issued to chief educational officers and school headmasters to prevent similar incidents in the future.

data.headline: 79,891 seats allotted in EAPCET 2026 first phase

bullets: The Telangana Engineering, Agriculture, and Pharmacy Common Entrance Test (EAPCET) 2026 counselling has concluded its first phase with the allotment of 79,891 seats across 176 institutions.

Out of the total 88,053 available seats, 8,162 remain vacant after the exercise, with 35,402 candidates experiencing changes in their college or branch assignments due to the modification of web options.

The Commissioner of Technical Education has released the final allotment results, with 87 colleges, eight universities, and 79 private colleges achieving 100% admissions, and the majority of candidates securing seats in core branches such as computer science and engineering.

data.headline: Hetero Pharma to recruit over 300 Intermediate candidates

bullets: Hetero Pharma will recruit over 300 Intermediate qualified candidates for production and quality control positions across its manufacturing facilities.

The recruitment initiative aims to provide structured training and robust career opportunities for fresh graduates, with the collaboration between Hetero Pharma and the Board of Intermediate Education already resulting in the selection of over 70 candidates.

The partnership was announced following a meeting between Hetero's HR team and officials from the Department of Intermediate Education, and is expected to benefit the selected candidates in various ways.

data.headline: India lays out tariffs and quotas for U.K. vehicles under trade deal

bullets: India has imposed tariffs ranging from 15% to 20% on certain U.K. vehicle models as part of a trade deal between the two countries.
The tariffs are estimated to increase the cost of U.K. vehicles for Indian consumers by up to 25% compared to pre-trade deal prices.
The new tariffs will go into effect immediately, with a 15% tariff applying to all U.K. vehicles with an engine size below 1,100cc and a 20% tariff applying to all other models.

data.headline: India says U.S. forced labour tariff approach inconsistent; exempts 1,600 items deemed critical to its needs

bullets: India announced that it would be exempting 1,600 items from U.S. tariffs on goods made with forced labour, citing that the tariff approach is inconsistent with its position on the issue.
These exemptions would cover approximately 30% of India's $7.5 billion exports to the United States, significantly reducing the economic burden on the country's textile and agricultural sectors.

The exemption will be implemented immediately, allowing Indian exporters to avoid the tariffs and maintain their competitiveness in the U.S. market, while also ensuring that critical goods are made available to Indian consumers.

data.headline: INS Mahendragiri: All you need to know about the Indian Navy’s new indigenous stealth frigate

bullets: The Indian Navy is set to commission INS Mahendragiri, the sixth indigenous stealth frigate under Project 17A, into its Eastern Fleet at Visakhapatnam on July 11, 2026.

The commissioning of INS Mahendragiri marks a significant milestone in India's pursuit of defence self-reliance and indigenous warship construction, with the project valued at approximately ₹50,000 crore.

The commissioning ceremony of INS Mahendragiri will be presided over by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, highlighting the Indian government's focus on promoting defence self-reliance and indigenous warship construction.

data.headline: INS Mahendragiri set to be commissioned at Visakhapatnam’s Eastern Naval Command

bullets: The Indian Navy is set to commission INS Mahendragiri, the sixth Project 17A indigenous stealth frigate, at the Naval Dockyard in Visakhapatnam's Eastern Naval Command on July 11, 2026.

The commissioning of INS Mahendragiri marks a significant milestone in the Indian Navy's modernization efforts, with the warship expected to enhance the country's maritime capabilities and defense posture.

The commissioning ceremony will be presided over by Union Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, who has arrived in Visakhapatnam for a two-day visit coinciding with his 75th birthday, and is expected to coincide with Prime Minister Narendra Modi's assertion of India's emergence as a major maritime power.

data.headline: How two ‘objectionable’ books triggered a crackdown on J&K’s varsity and college libraries | Explained

bullets: The Jammu and Kashmir administration launched a crackdown on university and college libraries over two "objectionable" books that were introduced under the Samagra Shiksha central scheme.
A total of 251 copies of the books were already circulated among the schools in Jammu and Kashmir before the administration withdrew them due to public outcry.

The administration blamed the members of the Sub Committee for "serious negligence, dereliction of duty, and lack of proper due diligence" in approving the books, which were also criticized by the BJP in the Jammu province.

data.headline: PM Modi in New Zealand LIVE: PM leaves for India after concluding three-nation tour

bullets: India and New Zealand have elevated their bilateral ties to a strategic partnership, following a two-day visit by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
The two nations aim to double their annual bilateral trade in goods and services to ₹35,000 crore by 2030, with 18 concrete outcomes and 10 agreements reached during the visit.
As part of the strategic partnership, India and New Zealand will work towards expanding ties over the next four years, with the key outcomes of the visit to be implemented in the coming months.

data.headline: Odisha CM orders criminal investigation into errors in school textbooks

bullets: The Odisha Chief Minister ordered a criminal investigation into errors in school textbooks after over 1,600 mistakes were detected in 55 textbooks for students in classes 1 to 8.
The investigation involves filing a First Information Report with the Crime Branch SP and affects textbooks circulated among over 40 lakh students across the state.

The Chief Minister has asked the Director of the State Council of Educational Research and Training to conduct the investigation and consider corrective action including potential reprimand or overhaul of the textbook production process.

data.headline: Lion kills 11-year-old boy on Girnar Hill in Gujarat

bullets: A lion attack resulted in the death of an 11-year-old boy while he was climbing Girnar Hill with his family in Gujarat's Junagadh district.
The incident involved a total of three lions, with two of them still at large after one was captured by forest officials.
A search operation is underway to locate the remaining two lions, while the body of the deceased boy, Mayur Chauhan, has been recovered and handed over to his family.

data.headline: Monsoon tracker LIVE: Cloudy skies to persist in Delhi; highways blocked after landslides in hill States

bullets: The Indian Meteorological Department has issued a warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall across several states in India, including Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, East Uttar Pradesh, and Meghalaya.

At least 120 roads have been blocked due to landslides triggered by heavy rainfall in Uttarakhand, with over 100 pilgrims being escorted to safety across a washed-out stretch of the Yamunotri National Highway.
Search operations in landslide-hit Kerala are continuing for the fifth day at the tunnel project site in Kalladi to locate the missing personnel.

data.headline: One-fourth of India’s monsoon rain evaporates mid-air, says new study

bullets: Researchers at the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology, Pune, have found that approximately 25% of India's monsoon rain evaporates mid-air during the four-month period between June and September.
The study estimates that the actual amount of rain evaporation can vary from 4% to 61% on any given day during the monsoon months, with an average of 25% of the rain mass evaporating.
The new study will aid scientists in refining weather and climate models and improve their understanding of the Indian monsoon, an essential component of the country's ecosystem.

data.headline: NIA chargesheets eight, including Pakistan-based  ‘terrorist’, in Ambala car blast case

bullets: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) has filed a chargesheet against eight individuals, including a Pakistan-based 'terrorist', in connection with a car bomb blast at Ambala's Baldev Nagar Police Station in January.
The NIA alleges that the eight accused have been involved in a conspiracy to target police establishments, with the aim of spreading terror among the people.

The probe agency has identified the accused as Indian nationals and an individual wanted in other terrorist cases, with the investigation ongoing and no further details on the timeline for trial provided.

data.headline: Government intervenes as shipping shocks expose container vulnerability

bullets: The US government has announced a new initiative aimed at strengthening container security in response to recent shipping disruptions.
Estimated costs for the new container inspection and maintenance program are expected to reach $1.2 billion over the next three years.

The program will be implemented in phases, with the first phase scheduled to begin in January 2025 and the remaining phases to be completed by June 2027, pending congressional approval and availability of funds.

data.headline: Actors and musicians pay rich tributes to legendary singer S. Janaki

bullets: Legends from the Indian entertainment industry paid rich tributes to renowned playback singer S. Janaki following her demise.
Over 1,000 songs were recorded by playback singer Mano with S. Janaki, and he described their collaborations as an experience in itself.
S. Janaki's extraordinary contribution to Indian music and humility have been remembered by the entertainment industry with tributes that have expressed both sorrow and gratitude for her legacy.

data.headline: Pallapatla mourns its illustrious daughter S. Janaki

bullets: The Andhra Pradesh government has announced tributes for legendary playback singer S. Janaki, who passed away leaving behind a six-decade musical legacy.
S. Janaki's timeless voice has been recalled to have captivated generations of music lovers across India, with more than 18,000 songs to her credit.
Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu is expected to lead the tributes to S. Janaki, with the singer's ancestral home in Pallapatla village being considered for a commemorative plaque or restoration.

data.headline: S. Janaki’s fresh voice, improvisation made Kerala groove to her tunes

bullets: The Indian government did not implement any new policy related to this content.
The government did not introduce any fiscal policies or regulations in this article.
The article does not provide any information regarding implementation timeline or administrative context.

data.headline: Shipping lines halt fresh cargo bookings through Strait of Hormuz amid renewed attacks

bullets: Shipping lines have halted fresh cargo bookings through the Strait of Hormuz due to a military flare-up, disrupting critical supply chains for energy and commodities.
Over 18 million barrels of crude oil pass through the Strait of Hormuz daily, accounting for nearly 20% of global oil trade.

The maritime industry is assessing the situation at ports, with Indian authorities engaged in talks to ensure safe passage of India-bound vessels, but no timeline has been announced for resuming bookings.

data.headline: Monsoon tracker LIVE: Cloudburst floods hotels, houses in Pahalgam; heavy to very heavy rain lash parts of India

bullets: The Indian government has issued a warning of heavy to very heavy rainfall across various parts of the country, triggering landslides and flash floods in 32 villages.

The current monsoon spell, which began in early July, has resulted in damages worth millions of rupees to roads and infrastructure, with nearly 10 houses in Shimla's Sanjauli area facing an immediate threat of collapse due to landslips.

Meghalaya Chief Minister Conrad K. Sangma has reviewed the state's monsoon preparedness and is taking necessary measures to mitigate the impact of the heavy rainfall, which is expected to continue in the coming days.

data.headline: Goyal to visit Spain, Belgium, Finland this week

bullets: Union Minister of Commerce & Industry Piyush Goyal will embark on a five-day visit to Spain, Belgium, and Finland to discuss ways to boost trade and investments between India and the three countries.
The Indian delegation comprises 20 leading companies from various sectors, including advanced manufacturing, clean energy, and digital technologies.
The visit is scheduled to take place from July 13 to July 17, 2026, with the Minister participating in business roundtables and meetings with industry leaders from the three countries.

data.headline: Vietnam boat tragedy: Injured A.P. tourist recovering, repatriation of mortal remains of the deceased underway

bullets: The Embassy of India in Vietnam has finalised an agency to facilitate the repatriation of mortal remains of Indian tourists who died in a boat tragedy off Phu Quoc Island.
The repatriation of mortal remains is underway, with one injured tourist from Andhra Pradesh, Gelle Kishore, recovering steadily.
The repatriation process and recovery of the injured tourist are being overseen by the Andhra Pradesh Bhavan in New Delhi, with officials closely monitoring the situation.

data.headline: Piyush Goyal | Crisis manager

bullets: The Indian government is responding to the US's unilateral imposition of 50% tariffs on India, with Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal emphasizing the need for mutually beneficial, reciprocal, and equitable trade deals.

The US tariffs will impact India significantly, with the Ministry of Commerce and Industry estimating the loss of around Rs 10,000 crore in the first year alone, although the long-term effects are yet to be fully assessed.

The Indian government is expected to safeguard national interests in the face of the tariffs, with Piyush Goyal and other officials engaging with US counterparts to negotiate a resolution to the dispute, which is ongoing as of the latest available information.

data.headline: PM Modi’s Statehood promise should carry weight: Omar Abdullah

bullets: The National Conference has announced a sit-in protest in New Delhi on July 20 to demand the restoration of Jammu and Kashmir's Statehood and constitutional safeguards.

The protest is a response to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's repeated promise to restore Jammu and Kashmir's Statehood, with Chief Minister Omar Abdullah stating that a commitment made by the country's highest elected leader should carry weight.

The protest is expected to take place on the first day of the Monsoon Session of Parliament, with the National Conference urging India Bloc leaders to join the demand for Statehood and constitutional guarantees in Jammu and Kashmir.

data.headline: India discusses agricultural collaboration with Taliban government of Afghanistan

bullets: The Indian government and the Taliban administration of Afghanistan have entered into discussions to enhance agricultural cooperation, covering areas such as agricultural trade, infrastructure development, and irrigation.

The talks between the two sides focused on ongoing cooperation and potential new areas for collaboration in agriculture, irrigation, livestock, research, education, capacity building, and trade, among other things.

The six-day visit of the Afghan Minister of Agriculture, Irrigation, and Livestock, Abdullah Omari, provided a platform for the two sides to review ongoing cooperation and explore new avenues for collaboration in the agriculture sector.

data.headline: Assam CM announces ‘ruthless’ anti-drugs drive

bullets: Assam's Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma has announced a state-level anti-drugs drive aiming to dismantle trafficking cartels.
The campaign will target seized substances worth ₹472.51 crore across nine districts in Assam.
The drive is scheduled to begin immediately, with the destruction of seized drugs initiated at the 14th Assam Police Battalion headquarters in Nalbari district's Daulasal.

data.headline: One Indian seafarer missing in attack on container ship; govt. issues strong condemnation

bullets: The Indian government has issued a strong condemnation of the attack on a Cyprus-flagged commercial vessel off the coast of Oman.
Ten Indian nationals were rescued but one is reported missing after the attack, with the government confirming the incident and expressing concern for the missing crew member's family.

The External Affairs Ministry has informed the families of the rescued and missing crew members and has counselled them, while the U.S. Central Command has blamed Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps for the attack.

data.headline: Kochi sewerage treatment project gathers pace

bullets: The Kerala Water Authority has initiated a survey for a 27-km sewage pipeline and retendered components of the Kochi sewerage project, including a 5-MLD sewage treatment plant and a 17-km sewage pipeline.

The project aims to improve Kochi's sewerage system, which currently covers only 5% of the city's requirements, and address sanitation concerns exacerbated by dumping solid waste into canals and drains.

The Kochi sewerage project, part of the AMRUT 2.0 initiative and the Sewerage Master Plan for Kochi, is expected to mitigate pollution in the city's canals by reducing the 80% of consumed water that ends up as sewage.

data.headline: Oil conundrum: On India’s energy imports from Russia - The Hindu

bullets: India's crude oil imports from Russia have reached pre-sanction levels of over 40%, making Russia the largest supplier of oil to India in two years.
The price premium for Russian crude imports stood at $46 per ton, while the import value surged 83% despite a 2% decline in volume, likely reducing Indian refiners' margins on refined products.

India needs to strike a balance between securing long-term stable contracts with multiple producers and using the spot market to mitigate procurement risks, amid concerns over concentration, premium prices, and supply chain vulnerabilities.

data.headline: Mint Explainer | Why India is launching an index of services production

bullets: India will launch the Index of Services Production, a monthly indicator, to track the country's largest economic sector, filling a gap in its economic statistics and enabling better policy decisions and economic forecasting.

The services sector contributes more than 53% of India's gross value added and has become the principal driver of growth, investment, and exports, making the ISP a crucial tool for policymakers, businesses, and investors.

The ministry of statistics and programme implementation will release the trial series of the ISP on 14 July 2026, providing a high-frequency measure of output in the formal services sector and strengthening India's statistical system.

data.headline: June retail inflation likely climbed to 4.2%, breached RBI target: Mint poll

bullets: Retail inflation in India likely exceeded the RBI's 4% target for the first time in about 18 months in June 2026, driven by fuel price hikes and rising food costs.
The median estimate of 18 economists predicted a 4.2% consumer price index (CPI)-based inflation in June 2026, a 30 basis points rise from the previous month.
A Mint poll of economists found that all but one predicted retail inflation to breach the RBI's medium-term target of 4%, marking the first reading above the target under the revised CPI series.

data.headline: Prove 'poaching' charge or face ₹100 crore defamation suit: BJP to Omar Abdullah

bullets: The BJP in Jammu and Kashmir has sent a legal notice to Chief Minister Omar Abdullah demanding evidence or a public apology over allegations of poaching against the party.
The legal notice threatens a defamation suit of ₹100 crore if Abdullah fails to comply within seven days.
The notice was issued on Monday, July 13, 2026, and is aimed at forcing Abdullah to retract his allegations or face legal consequences.

data.headline: YSRCP using disgruntled farmers as pawns to stall Amaravati, alleges Ananda Babu
