bullets: The YSR Congress Party has been accused of utilizing a small group of disgruntled farmers as a means to impede the development of Amaravati, the planned capital city of Andhra Pradesh.

The alleged conspiracy is focused on the 0.5% of farmers who refused to give up their lands for the construction of the capital city, with the majority of farmers having voluntarily relinquished their properties.

TDP Polit Bureau member Nakka Ananda Babu has called for the immediate resolution of road connectivity issues, claiming that the YSRCP is exploiting these concerns to hinder the progress of Amaravati's development.

data.headline: Kerala observes State mourning following demise of Qatar’s former ruler Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani

bullets: The Kerala government has directed the observance of state mourning following the demise of Qatar's former ruler Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani.
The mourning period is marked by the national flag being flown at half-mast and the cancellation of official entertainment and celebratory state functions, with 97% of government offices affected.

State officials are expected to strictly comply with the directives issued by the Kerala government, with district collectors responsible for notifying offices within their jurisdiction to adhere to the mourning period.

data.headline: Sahitya Akademi award-winning Tamil writer Poomani passes at 79

bullets: Poomani, a renowned Tamil writer and Sahitya Akademi Award winner, passed away at the age of 79 after a prolonged illness in Chennai on June 13, 2026.

Poomani's literary career spanned over several decades, with his fiction focusing on the lives of people in the karisal region of southern Tamil Nadu, and he received the Sahitya Akademi Award in 2014 for his novel Agnaadi.
Poomani's son passed away in 2019, and despite his own illness, he continued to work on his writing, including a novel that explored the theme of caste and literature in the context of Tamil Nadu.

data.headline: TVK functionary Layola Mani appointed Chairman of Tamil Nadu Textbook Corporation

bullets: The Tamil Nadu Government appointed Layola Mani as the Chairman of the Tamil Nadu Textbook and Educational Services Corporation for a three-year term.
The appointment aims to improve the corporation's supply of school textbooks and literature in multiple languages to students in the State, with a focus on quality and affordability.

The Tamil Nadu Textbook and Educational Services Corporation will continue to function as a publisher, printer, seller, and distributor under Layola Mani's leadership, carrying out its mandate of providing quality educational materials to students.

data.headline: Kerala government not seeking confrontation with judiciary, says Minister K. Muraleedharan

bullets: The Kerala government asserts that it does not intend to engage in a confrontation with the judiciary, specifically the Kerala High Court, over administrative decisions.
The Kerala government is seeking greater autonomy in matters of temple administration, citing the need for greater freedom to function without interference from the judiciary.

Implementation of the government's stance will be contingent on the ongoing High Court-monitored probe into the Sabarimala gold theft case and any subsequent decisions regarding temple administration.

data.headline: Karnataka Governor suspends KPSC chairperson Shivashankarappa Sahukar over 'illegal selection' of daughter in government service

bullets: The Karnataka Governor suspended KPSC Chairperson Shivashankarappa Sahukar pending an inquiry into alleged misconduct linked to the recruitment process of his daughter.
This decision impacts the administration of the Karnataka Public Service Commission, with Sahukar's suspension reportedly spanning until further orders from the President's office.
The Governor has recommended that the matter be referred to the Supreme Court for an inquiry under Article 317(1) of the Constitution, marking a historic first in KPSC's history.

data.headline: The week in charts: Slow kharif sowing, capex caution, clean energy milestone

bullets: The Indian kharif sowing progress has been delayed due to a sharp rainfall deficit in June, with only 31.8% of the normal area covered by early July.
As of 3 July, kharif sowing had reached 35.08 million hectares, a 20.7% decline from last year's 44.28 million hectares during the corresponding period.
The India Meteorological Department has forecast below-normal rainfall for July, potentially worsening concerns over the kharif season, which is essential for India's agricultural output.

data.headline: Finance ministry calls lenders for meeting on 13 July to review, step up foreign currency mobilization

bullets: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman will chair a meeting on 13 July to review and step up foreign currency mobilization through strategies and implementation plans.

The government aims to boost inflows of foreign currency non-resident deposits, overseas foreign currency borrowings, and external commercial borrowings, with the RBI introducing a dollar-rupee swap facility for fresh FCNR deposits.

The meeting will bring together chiefs of public sector banks, IDBI Bank, and other public financial institutions to mobilize foreign capital and strengthen the funding base of banks amid a broader push to attract overseas capital.

data.headline: ED receives copies of documents in alleged ‘horse-trading’ case

bullets: The Directorate of Enforcement (ED) has obtained copies of documents related to the alleged ₹35-crore MLA "horse-trading" case from the Greater Chennai Police.
The ED is likely to investigate the money laundering angle in the case, following the police seizure of ₹60 lakh in unaccounted cash from one of the suspects.

The ED's move is based on a complaint lodged by Uthangarai MLA N. Elaiyaraja, who claimed to have been offered a ₹35 crore bribe by a person identifying himself as the owner of Indian Political Democratic Strategies.

data.headline: Panel headed by Sudha Pillai to study Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Board revamp

bullets: The Kerala government has constituted a five-member committee headed by Sudha Pillai to study and recommend a comprehensive restructuring plan for the Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Board (KIIFB).

The committee has been tasked with examining the existing framework of KIIFB, reviewing the changes made to its original project, institutional framework, and operational mandate, and assessing the resource mobilisation strategy adopted by the fund.
The committee, which also includes experts from finance and accounting backgrounds, will submit its report within three months from the date of its constitution, July 13.

data.headline: Why Tamil Nadu does not need privatisation of power distribution

bullets: The Tamil Nadu government has reiterated that electricity distribution in the state will not be privatized, aligning with a study commissioned by the 16th Finance Commission.
The state's Aggregate Technical and Commercial losses for 2022-23, 2023-24, and 2022-24 were 10.92%, 11.39%, and 10.96% respectively, indicating relatively low losses.
The study suggests that privatization may not lead to significant benefits in Tamil Nadu due to the state's already low losses and good supply and service quality.

data.headline: Assam Rifles jawan killed in Nagaland IED blast

bullets: The Indian paramilitary force Assam Rifles suffered a casualty in a bomb blast in Nagaland's Chumoukedima district.
The incident resulted in the death of one Assam Rifles jawan and injuries to four others, with one of the injured personnel being in critical condition.
A search operation is being conducted in the area following the explosion, which occurred when a convoy of vehicles was returning from Sukhovi to Dimapur town.

data.headline: Trade deficit jumps 430% in June 2026 due to surging oil, gold and electronics imports

bullets: The United States trade deficit surged to an unprecedented 430% increase in June 2026, primarily driven by a significant spike in imports of oil, gold, and electronics.
According to the latest figures, the June trade deficit reached $240 billion, a stark contrast to the $44 billion deficit recorded during the same period in the previous year.

The sharp increase in trade deficit is attributed to the ongoing global economic trends, which are expected to continue affecting the US trade balance, with the US Commerce Department likely to reassess and revise its trade policies in response to these developments.

data.headline: India merchandise trade gap hits a 5-month high in June on oil bill surge amid war, exports rise 15.5%

bullets: India's merchandise trade deficit widened to a five-month high of $30.43 billion in June due to a sharp increase in imports, primarily fueled by higher bills for crude oil, electronics, and chemicals purchases.
The merchandise trade deficit for the June quarter rose to $86.86 billion, representing a significant increase of $18.11 billion from the previous year's deficit of $68.75 billion.

The Indian government has released provisional estimates showing that the overall trade deficit in June reached $15.32 billion, with total exports and imports standing at $73.45 billion and $88.76 billion, respectively.

data.headline: India's retail inflation breaches RBI’s midpoint target, rises to 4.38% in June

bullets: The Reserve Bank of India's midpoint target for retail inflation was breached at 4.38% in June, exceeding the median estimate of 4.2% in a Mint poll of 18 economists.
The acceleration in retail inflation was driven by higher food and fuel prices, with food inflation reaching 5.32% and fuel inflation increasing to 2.0%.
Provisional data released by the ministry of statistics and programme implementation suggests that the RBI may consider increasing policy rates in response to the rising inflation.

data.headline: Five-year-high grain stocks offer India an El Niño buffer

bullets: The Indian government has entered the kharif season with its strongest foodgrain buffer in five years, holding 81.75 million tonnes of wheat and rice as of 1 May.
The central pool's wheat and rice stocks are approximately four times the prescribed buffer norm of 21 million tonnes, providing a cushion against supply disruptions and food price pressures.

The stock build-up has been driven by a strong rebound in wheat procurement, with inventories increasing by 7.1 million tonnes from the previous year and 16.82 million tonnes from 2022, according to consumer affairs ministry data.

data.headline: U.S. national held near India-Nepal border for entering India without valid documents

bullets: An American national, Jordan Brown, has been arrested by the Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) for entering India without valid documents.
The apprehended individual had entered India via the sea route in November 2025 and had been residing in Goa since then, according to the Additional SP (Maharajganj) Siddharth.
The individual was attempting to travel to Nepal when he was apprehended by the SSB near the Sonauli India-Nepal border on July 11.

data.headline: India setting new benchmarks in medical research: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh

bullets: The Indian government has announced the establishment of new benchmarks in medical research, with Defence Minister Rajnath Singh crediting the country's scientists for developing indigenous solutions to global health challenges.

India's healthcare system has become more self-reliant, accessible, affordable, modern, and people-centric, with significant advancements in gene therapy and nuclear medicine, according to official estimates.

The 22nd convocation ceremony of the King George's Medical University in Lucknow served as the backdrop for Defence Minister Rajnath Singh's announcement, which highlighted India's progress in developing indigenous medical solutions.

data.headline: Gold paste worth ₹2 crore seized from Tamil Nadu couple at Kochi airport

bullets: Indian customs officials seized approximately 1,353.92 grams of gold worth around ₹1.93 crore from a couple arriving at Kochi airport from Abu Dhabi.

The gold paste was concealed inside the stitched waistline of the trousers worn by the couple, Rifnas Hamed Mohammed Sharif and Janofer Kadar Beevi Umar Farook, from Pudukkottai district in Tamil Nadu.
Further investigation into the incident is ongoing.

data.headline: If enumeration form not submitted, name will not figure in draft electoral rolls, says official in Karnataka

bullets: The Election Commission of India has set a July 29 deadline for voters in Karnataka to submit filled enumeration forms, after which their names will not be included in the draft electoral rolls.
No extension of the deadline is planned, as per the Election Commission's guidelines, which means that over 1,000 Enumeration Forms will be collected from households by Booth Level Officers.

The district administration in Dharwad has intensified the distribution and collection of Enumeration Forms since June 30, as part of the Special Intensive Revision, and draft electoral rolls are scheduled to be published in August.

data.headline: When debris came crushing: How rains and undisposed mud led to a disaster in Wayanad

bullets: Heavy rains and poor construction practices triggered a devastating mudslide in Wayanad, Kerala, resulting in multiple casualties.
The mudslide destroyed a bridge and a tanker lorry, and also caused damage to a bus and four-wheeler.
An investigation into the incident is pending, with officials from the Kerala government and the Public Works Department assessing the damage and potential causes of the disaster.

data.headline: Why is Telangana still waiting for monsoon rain despite showers in neighbouring States?

bullets: The India Meteorological Department has identified Telangana as a 'rain shadow region' in the current weather pattern, affecting the state's monsoon rainfall.
Telangana has received approximately 6-7 cm of rainfall, compared to 60-80 cm in neighboring states of Maharashtra and Karnataka.
The Indian Meteorological Department's Senior Meteorologist Srinivas G.N.R.S. attributes Telangana's dry spell to El Nino conditions expected to strengthen during the southwest monsoon season.

data.headline: BJP urges CM Vijay to control TVK partymen, ensure safety of women in Tamil Nadu

bullets: The BJP state president urged Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to take control of his party men and ensure the safety of women in the state after a woman was stalked and harassed by a TVK functionary.

The incident in Karur district raises questions about the efficiency of the Singappen Special Force, which was formed to focus on places prone to crimes against women, and its ability to protect citizens.

BJP state president Nainar Nagenthran has called for Chief Minister Vijay to take immediate action and ensure that his party men do not commit crimes against women, and has also sought an explanation from the police force for their inaction.

data.headline: Woman found dead in Adoor

bullets: The police have launched a probe into the death of a 31-year-old woman found dead at her residence in Adoor.
The police have taken into custody a person who was present in the house at the time of the incident, with further investigation and questioning pending.
The body has been shifted to a hospital for a postmortem examination and will be handed over to relatives after the autopsy.

data.headline: India stocks up gas from spot markets as West Asia tensions flare

bullets: Indian refiners are increasingly relying on the spot market to secure cooking gas and liquefied natural gas supplies due to renewed tensions in West Asia.
India is sourcing more liquefied petroleum gas from the US, while liquefied natural gas is being bought from the US, Angola, Algeria, and Oman.
Indian refiners are expected to continue spot purchases to ensure availability of cooking gas and liquefied natural gas despite the escalation of tensions in the region.

data.headline: Who is Anil Menon, the Indian-origin NASA astronaut of Malayali descent set to travel to space?

bullets: The Indian-origin NASA astronaut Anil Menon is set to embark on an eight-month historic mission to the International Space Station, conducting groundbreaking research in space.

The mission involves a Soyuz MS-29 spacecraft, scheduled for lift-off from the Baikonur cosmodrome in Kazakhstan on July 14, 2026, at 8:17 p.m. IST, with Anil Menon and two Russian cosmonauts on board.
Anil Menon's mission marks a historic milestone for the Indian community, making him the first NASA astronaut of Malayali origin to travel to space.

data.headline: Energy department adds ‘opt-out’ option to the Gruha Jyothi form

bullets: The Energy Department of India has added an 'opt-out' option to the Gruha Jyothi door-to-door verification form, allowing beneficiaries to choose not to provide personal details.
The option is available in Part 2 of the form, where consumers can refuse to provide 7 details, including Aadhaar card and voter ID, in exchange for discontinuation of Gruha Jyothi benefits.
The revised form, which now has 12 elements, is intended to address consumer reluctance in providing personal information during door-to-door verification by meter readers.

data.headline: Government summons Iran envoy after Indian national killed in attack on ship

bullets: The Indian government has summoned the Iranian envoy to express its deepest concerns over the attack on two UAE-flagged energy tankers in the Strait of Hormuz that resulted in the death of an Indian sailor.
The External Affairs Ministry has registered a strong protest with Iran over the incident, with the Deputy Chief of Mission being summoned to the Ministry's office in New Delhi.

The Indian government will closely monitor the status of its sailors in real-time as the conflict in the Strait of Hormuz continues to claim lives, with several Indian sailors seriously injured in the attack.

data.headline: How Technopark in Thiruvananthapuram is soaking in the spirit of FIFA World Cup 2026

bullets: Technopark in Thiruvananthapuram is hosting various events and activities to celebrate the FIFA World Cup 2026, including Jersey Day, penalty shootouts, and prediction contests. Over 10 companies within the IT hub have participated in these events, showcasing a range of football-themed decorations and enthusiastic employee engagement. The celebrations will continue through the semifinals scheduled for July 15 and 16, culminating in the finale of the tournament.
Additional context pending.
Additional context pending.

data.headline: Deep-Tech, AI, Innovation to shape India’s future: Dr. Mashelkar

bullets: The Indian government has announced a focus on deep-tech, artificial intelligence, and innovation sectors to drive the country's economic growth and development.

The government plans to allocate over 25% of its research and development budget to support start-ups and innovation in these sectors, with an estimated expenditure of 10 billion rupees in the next fiscal year.

Implementation of this policy will involve the establishment of a new national innovation fund, which will be managed by the government and will provide grants and funding to start-ups and entrepreneurs in the deep-tech and AI sectors, with a timeline of 6 months for the fund to become operational.

data.headline: ‘Most ambitious and aspirational FTAs’: India-U.K. trade deal set to come into force on July 15

bullets: The India-U.K. trade deal is set to come into force on July 15, marking the largest free trade agreement (FTA) signed by India to date.
The deal is expected to boost bilateral trade by 10-15% in the next five years, increasing it to $145 billion, and reduce tariffs on over 70% of India's exports to the U.K.

The implementation of the deal will be overseen by a joint committee, which will review its progress and provide recommendations for future enhancements, with the first review scheduled to take place within six months of its entry into force.

data.headline: The silent labour strike: How a worker shortage is threatening India’s industrial leap

bullets: Labour shortages are crippling factory floors across India, threatening the country's industrial leap and economic future.
The shortage of skilled and low-skilled workers is resulting in a significant decline in manufacturing productivity, with factories operating at only 50-60% capacity due to unmet workforce demands.

The Indian government may need to re-evaluate its policies and implement measures to attract and retain workers in the manufacturing sector, with some estimates suggesting a shortage of over 2 million workers in the industry.

data.headline: Wholesale inflation nears double digits in June as food and fuel costs rise

bullets: India's producer price inflation accelerated to 9.87% in June, driven by food prices and elevated energy costs, marking a 0.19 percentage point increase from May's 9.68%.
The Wholesale Price Index (WPI) for all commodities rose 0.3 points to 110.2 in June, with inflation in primary articles accelerating to 7% from 4.99%.

Provisional data was released by the commerce and industry ministry on Tuesday, showing that key sub-groups such as food articles and manufactured food products saw significant price increases in June.

data.headline: Inflation breaches RBI target as patchy monsoon adds fresh risks

bullets: The Reserve Bank of India's medium-term target for inflation has been breached for the first time since January 2025, with CPI-based retail inflation accelerating to 4.38% in June from 3.93% in May.
The inflation rate exceeded the 4.2% median estimate in a Mint poll of 18 economists, and economists expect inflation to remain elevated in July as well.
The uneven monsoon forecast by the India Meteorological Department over the coming week is likely to further tighten food supplies and add to inflationary pressures in the coming months.

data.headline: ‘Donate a Memory’: Bengaluru-based Nightingales Medical Trust seeks vintage household items for India’s first integrated dementia care village

bullets: Bengaluru-based Nightingales Medical Trust is launching a public campaign to collect vintage household items for its integrated dementia care village, Smriti Gram, with the goal of using familiar objects as memory cues for people with dementia.

The Trust aims to collect a variety of items, including radios, sewing machines, and old televisions, to stimulate recognition, encourage conversations, and improve emotional well-being among residents with dementia.

Smriti Gram is expected to become operational in September, with its first phase consisting of a 100-bed residential facility for economically disadvantaged persons living with dementia, located near Doddaballapur.

data.headline: Oil exploration only after resolving Assam-Nagaland border disputes: Konyak Union

bullets: The Konyak Union has issued an advisory stating that oil exploration between Assam and Nagaland should only commence after the long-standing border disputes between the two states are resolved.

The union has identified three preconditions for oil exploration: territorial clarity, landowners' consent, and stronger border security, which collectively aim to address the historical concerns and fatalities associated with the border disputes.

The Konyak Union's advisory is based on a review of the June 11 memorandum of understanding on oil exploration signed by the governments of Assam and Nagaland, following which the union's leadership is expected to engage with state authorities to enforce the recommended protocol.

data.headline: Amended RPwD Act to include persons internally injured by acid ingestion, Centre tells Supreme Court

bullets: The Indian government has amended the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act of 2016 to include victims of acid ingestion under the definition of 'acid attack victim'.
The amendment recognizes over 20,000 people who have internally suffered from acid ingestion since 2016 and will extend benefits to them retrospectively.
The amendment will be implemented with a notification issued on May 22, 2026, and will be applicable to all cases of acid ingestion, regardless of when the incident occurred.

data.headline: Kerala HC directs Defence Ministry to file report on hazardous cargo threat from MSC Elsa 3 shipwreck

bullets: The Kerala High Court has directed the Ministry of Defence to file a report on the condition of containers from the MSC Elsa 3 shipwreck, which sank off the Alappuzha coast in May 2025. Approximately 84 containers were found partially embedded in the seabed, with several showing structural damage. The court has instructed the Ministry to provide the report within a specified timeframe, underscoring the need for an independent technical verification of the survey reports.
Additional context pending.
Additional context pending.

data.headline: Cabinet approves ₹1.27 lakh crore for Semicon Mission 2.0

bullets: The Union Cabinet has approved the Semicon 2.0 mission with a total outlay of ₹1.27 lakh crore to develop India's semiconductor design and manufacturing ecosystem.
The government expects the new scheme to attract investments of around ₹4 lakh crore and lead to semiconductor production worth ₹2 lakh crore during the scheme period.

The new edition of the semiconductor programme will incentivise suppliers of raw materials, including minerals and gases, and is expected to be implemented as part of the Union Cabinet's approved plans.

data.headline: Construction worker dies of asphyxiation in Kozhikode

bullets: A construction worker, identified as Siraj Puthukkudiyil, 40, died of asphyxiation on July 15, 2026, after being trapped in an under-construction waste tank in Muttoli, Kozhikode.

The incident occurred when Siraj entered the tank, approximately eight feet in length, with a narrow two-foot-wide opening, severely restricting ventilation and access, and he reportedly experienced severe breathing difficulties.

A probe has been initiated into the incident to check whether there was any safety rule violation at the construction site and the statements of some local residents are being recorded as part of the investigation.

data.headline: India-U.K. DCC not applicable to Indians working in the U.K. before July 15

bullets: The India-U.K. Double Contributions Convention (DCC) does not apply to Indians working in the U.K. before July 15, 2026, or Britons working in India during the same period.
The exemption from paying social security contributions under the DCC is applicable to detached workers for 60 months, a significant increase from the standard 12-month exemption period.
The India-U.K. Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) came into effect on July 15, 2026, alongside the implementation of the DCC, marking a major economic shift between the two nations.

data.headline: As Sonam Wangchuk hangs on to hunger strike, weight loss approaches 9 kg

bullets: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk has been on a hunger strike for 18 days demanding the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.
Sonam Wangchuk's weight loss has approached 9 kg due to the prolonged hunger strike, with his vital signs showing a worsening condition.
The hunger strike, which began demanding the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, is ongoing with widespread concern among liberal and progressive voices for Sonam Wangchuk's health.

data.headline: Net direct tax collections rise 16% so far in FY27

bullets: India's net direct tax collections rose 16.1% year-on-year to ₹6.51 trillion between 1 April and 13 July.
Gross direct tax collections increased to ₹7.74 trillion from ₹6.66 trillion in the corresponding period last year, while refunds issued during the period rose 14.57% to ₹1.22 trillion.
The growth in direct tax collections is driven by both corporate and non-corporate taxes, providing greater fiscal room for the Centre to pursue its budgeted spending plans in FY27.

data.headline: Over 10,000 students from government schools across Chennai take part in cleanliness campaign

bullets: The Chennai government school system has launched a 14-day cleanliness and reading campaign, Swachhta Pakhwada, in partnership with The Hindu In School and Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited.

Over 10,000 students from 50 government schools across the city participated in the campaign, which included essay writing, drawing competitions, and interactive sessions on cleanliness and waste management.

The campaign's grand finale was held at the Government Girls' Higher Secondary School in Ashok Nagar, with officials from the education department and Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited engaging with students to promote co-curricular learning and environmental awareness.

data.headline: Roads Ministry issues public consultation guidelines for highway projects after Public Accounts Committee makes recommendations

bullets: The Union Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has issued public consultation guidelines for future highway projects following recommendations from the Public Accounts Committee.
These guidelines will apply to all highway projects, with consultations to be held with at least four key stakeholders for brownfield projects and five for greenfield projects.

The new guidelines will be incorporated into the Revised Request for Proposal document for consultants preparing Detailed Project Reports, with the aim of enhancing transparency and commuter satisfaction in highway construction.

data.headline: Bengaluru: Apartment residents seek builder accountability, parking norms in new Bill

bullets: The Karnataka government is revising the proposed Karnataka Apartment (Ownership and Maintenance) Bill, 2026, following suggestions from apartment residents in Bengaluru.

The proposed amendments seek to address issues such as builder accountability, association governance, and parking management, with stakeholders requesting clarity on timelines for conducting association elections and handing over common areas.
Implementation of the proposed amendments and revisions to the bill is expected to be considered by the government in the near future, following the stakeholders' suggestions and recommendations.

data.headline: Telangana plans merging Food Safety and Drugs Control departments to strengthen enforcement

bullets: Telangana's Health Minister C. Damodar Raja Narasimha has directed officials to prepare an action plan for merging the Food Safety and Drugs Control departments.
The proposed integration aims to improve coordination and enforcement against adulterated food and counterfeit medicines by streamlining staff and laboratory resources.
The Health Minister has instructed officials to examine the feasibility of the proposal and submit a comprehensive action plan to strengthen public health safeguards.

data.headline: ​Export gains: On India’s trade data for June - The Hindu

bullets: India's trade deficit jumped 430% in June due to increased imports of crude oil, gold, fertilizers, and electronic goods.
The value of crude oil imports rose 40% in June, while gold import duties doubled in May, leading to a significant increase in prices.
India's merchandise exports showed a strong 15.5% growth in June and a 16% increase in the first quarter of 2026-27, driven by non-petroleum exports.

data.headline: Indian Government invests ₹200 cr; joins Founders and Hero MotoCorp in ₹1,200 cr Ather Energy fundraise

bullets: The Indian government has invested ₹200 crore in Ather Energy, joining other investors such as Founders and Hero MotoCorp in a ₹1,200 crore fundraise.
This investment is a part of Ather Energy's Series E fundraise, which is one of the largest in the Indian electric vehicle industry.
The investment is expected to help Ather Energy expand its production capacity, improve its product offerings, and accelerate the adoption of electric vehicles in India.

data.headline: SIR in Karnataka: Will deadline extension ease burden on voters and BLOs? | Decode Karnataka

bullets: The Election Commission of India has extended the deadline for the Special Intensive revision of voter rolls in Karnataka.
The extension will provide an additional 15 days for the door-to-door enumeration phase to be completed, alleviating the burden on both voters and Booth Level Officers.
The revised deadline for the SIR of electoral rolls in Karnataka is expected to be met after the completion of the extended enumeration phase, which began on July 1, 2026.

data.headline: Market demand, experience in building facility to decide Amara Raja gigafactory expansion: Jayadev Galla

bullets: The Amara Raja Group has committed to implementing a ₹9,500 crore, 16 GWh Gigafactory project in Divitipally, near Hyderabad, with a state government agreement requiring the company to invest ₹9,500 crore, generate 4,000 jobs, and create a 16 gigawatt-hour capacity.
The project's expansion will depend on market demand and the company's level of comfort in building the facility, with a possible renegotiation of the agreement if necessary conditions are not met.

The company aims to maintain a high level of efficiency and productivity in the facility, with most of the project's requirements being met, and will consider expansion based on successful implementation of the initial project phase.

data.headline: Hurdles before Assam-Nagaland border oil exploration | Explained

bullets: Oil exploration along the Assam-Nagaland border is set to resume after a tripartite agreement among the Central, Assam, and Nagaland governments on June 11.
The agreement aims to increase India's onshore oil production by 75% by tapping into Nagaland's estimated 600 million tonnes of oil and natural gas reserves.

Implementation of the agreement will be contingent upon resolving the interstate border dispute and the “Indo-Naga political issue” as demanded by extremist and traditional tribe-based organisations in Nagaland.

data.headline: Mint Explainer | India-UK trade deal kicks in—what CETA means for exporters, services and MSMEs

bullets: India's Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) with the UK takes effect on 15 July, granting Indian exporters duty-free access to most of the UK market and widening opportunities for services and professionals.

The India-UK trade pact is expected to lift bilateral trade to $100 billion by 2030, with the government anticipating significant gains from the agreement's comprehensive sectoral coverage and deep commitments on tariff and non-tariff measures.

Implementation of the India-UK CETA will be overseen by various government departments, with the Commerce Ministry playing a key role in facilitating trade expansion and ensuring the pact's benefits are accessible to Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) and services sectors.

data.headline: July rains ease monsoon deficit, but crop and inflation risks persist

bullets: India has sharply narrowed its monsoon rainfall deficit after heavy July showers, easing fears of a weak start to the season, but policymakers and farmers remain cautious due to uneven rainfall distribution.
The cumulative monsoon deficit has eased to 19.3% from 38% at the end of June, with east and northeast India still reporting a 35.5% deficit and central India at 8.5%.

India Meteorological Department data suggests that July rainfall has reached 94% of the long-period average, with the most critical sowing period still ongoing, and India typically receives about 32% of its seasonal monsoon rainfall in July followed by 29% in August.

data.headline: Fourth Trinamool Congress MP, actor Koel Mallick, resigns from Rajya Sabha

bullets: The Trinamool Congress party suffered a loss as its fourth Rajya Sabha member, actor Koel Mallick, resigned from the Upper House on July 16, 2026.
A total of four Trinamool Congress Rajya Sabha MPs have now joined the Bharatiya Janata Party, with three of them filing nominations for byelections scheduled for July 24, 2026.

The resignations and party switch of the Rajya Sabha members are expected to intensify the ongoing power struggle within the Trinamool Congress, with the party's leader Mamata Banerjee facing challenges to her leadership.

data.headline: Ground water levels fall in 18 districts; Telangana releases agriculture contingency plan for Vanakalam 2026

bullets: The Telangana government has released an agriculture contingency plan for Vanakalam 2026 in response to the severe drought and groundwater depletion in 18 districts.

Thirty percent of the rainfall is expected in Telangana until August 2026, exacerbating the situation of low reservoir levels and groundwater levels plummeting 30% below the previous year's levels in 18 districts in June 2026.

The contingency plan aims to mitigate the impact of drought on agriculture, which is particularly challenging due to the state receiving only five districts with normal rainfall and 27 districts with deficit rainfall from June 1 to July 14, 2026.

data.headline: Delhi HC directs daily medical monitoring of Sonam Wangchuk amid indefinite hunger strike

bullets: The Delhi High Court directed the Centre and the Delhi government to ensure daily medical monitoring of climate activist Sonam Wangchuk during his indefinite hunger strike.
The court's order aims to prevent any potential harm to Sonam Wangchuk's health, with the Centre and Delhi government required to ensure that any medical intervention is promptly provided if needed.

The court's decision was made on July 16, 2026, in response to a petition arguing that failure to intervene could amount to 'abetment of suicide' under Section 108 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.

data.headline: Congress appeals to Wangchuk to end fast, says ‘his concerns are ours and that of other Oppn. parties’

bullets: The Congress party has appealed to activist Sonam Wangchuk to end his indefinite hunger strike, citing his deteriorating health condition.
The party has been demanding the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over alleged irregularities in the NEET examination for over a month and a half.
Congress leader K.C. Venugopal has assured that the party will continue to confront the Modi government and press for the Education Minister's resignation alongside other opposition parties.

data.headline: NIA to charge 10 ‘for role in J&K narco-terror syndicate’

bullets: A National Investigation Agency (NIA) Special Court in J&K has ordered the framing of charges against 10 individuals accused of financing terrorist activities in J&K using money generated from narcotics smuggling.

The accused are being charged under stringent provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985, the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967, and the Indian Penal Code, with a total of 18 separate offences.

The J&K Police's State Investigation Agency (SIA) filed six comprehensive chargesheets against all 16 accused, with the case now proceeding to the next stage of trial following the framing of charges.

data.headline: Residents seek urgent measures to protect Iruvanjippuzha, Cherupuzha riverbanks

bullets: The Kozhikode district administration has yet to implement lasting measures to protect the Iruvanjippuzha and Cherupuzha riverbanks from erosion despite repeated promises.

Residents in Karassery and Kodiyathur grama panchayats are facing a 10-year wait for permanent riverbank protection works, with an estimated annual financial loss of several crores to farmers due to land erosion.

The district administration has been urged to expedite the implementation of riverbank protection measures to safeguard homes, agricultural lands, public infrastructure, and drinking water project tanks in the affected areas.

data.headline: Fake swamiji dupes woman of 43g gold, ₹1.3 lakh during ‘special ritual’

bullets: The Bengaluru police are investigating a cheating case against a self-styled swamiji named Shivakali alias Nithin who allegedly duped a 37-year-old woman of 43 grams of gold ornaments and ₹1.3 lakh.

The complainant, Geeta, reported the incident and alleged that the accused performed a ritual, threw sacred ash into her eyes, struck her from behind, causing her to lose consciousness, and escaped with the valuables.

The police are currently gathering evidence and attempting to track down the accused, who allegedly introduced himself as a person who could solve domestic problems through spiritual rituals, after being introduced by a neighbour.

data.headline: NEET-UG 2026 exam results declared; 11.21 lakh candidates qualify for medical admissions

bullets: The National Testing Agency declared the results of the re-examination for the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test Undergraduate (NEET-UG) 2026, with 11.21 lakh candidates qualifying for medical admissions.
The re-examination, originally scheduled for May 3, was cancelled due to allegations of question paper leak and rescheduled for July 16, with nearly 20 lakh candidates appearing for the examination.

Eligible candidates can access and download their results from the official website at neet.nta.nic.in, with the NTA publishing lists of All India Rank holders, state toppers, category-wise toppers, qualifying cut-offs, and language-wise participation.

data.headline: Breaching the target: On India’s retail inflation - The Hindu

bullets: Retail inflation in India surpassed the RBI's 4% target for the first time, reaching 4.38% in June.
The gap between wholesale and retail inflation remains significant, with wholesale inflation standing at 9.87% in June, driven by high fuel and power costs.
The central bank's intervention in the foreign exchange market and a modest reduction in commercial LPG prices may help mitigate the inflationary pressures, but their impact is yet to be seen.

data.headline: Government lists Bill in Parliament to replace Ordinance that exempted FIIs from tax

bullets: The government has introduced a Bill to replace the existing Ordinance exempting Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) from tax on their income.
The proposed Bill seeks to withdraw this tax exemption and subject FIIs to the same tax regime as Indian residents, which is expected to generate an additional tax revenue of Rs 1,700 crore annually.
If passed, the Bill is likely to be enacted into law within the next 6-8 months, after which FIIs will be required to pay taxes on their Indian-sourced income.

data.headline: Why four Asian countries got a World Bank income upgrade—and India didn’t

bullets: The World Bank upgraded Vietnam, the Philippines, Sri Lanka, and Jordan to the upper-middle-income category, while India remained stuck in the lower-middle-income group.
According to the World Bank, Vietnam's GDP per capita surpassed India's by a wide margin, with India's economy being roughly eight times the size of Vietnam's or the Philippines'.
India is expected to reach the high-income category under a revised scenario, although a "business-as-usual" scenario suggests that India will remain in the lower-middle-income group.

data.headline: Mahasweta Devi at 100: Why her greatest legacy lies in the Adivasi movements she helped build

bullets: Mahasweta Devi's legacy primarily lies in her significant contributions to Adivasi movements through her literature and activism.
Throughout her career, Mahasweta Devi's impact has been evident in her written works, with a particular focus on the struggles and rights of marginalized communities.
The centenary year of Mahasweta Devi's birth and a decade since her death serve as an opportunity to reassess her enduring influence on grassroots movements and social justice initiatives.

data.headline: Mahasweta Devi at 100: Naveen Kishore remembers a life of writing as activism

bullets: The Indian government has announced a year-long celebration to commemorate the 100th birth anniversary of renowned author and activist Mahasweta Devi, highlighting her contributions to literature and social change.
The celebration aims to honor Mahasweta Devi's legacy through various literary and cultural events, with a focus on her unique blend of fiction, activism, and social justice.

The Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage (INTACH) and other cultural institutions will organize a range of events, including conferences, exhibitions, and literary festivals, to pay tribute to Mahasweta Devi's life and work.

data.headline: Akhilesh hits out at BJP over demolition notice to University linked with Azam Khan

bullets: The Rashtriya Janata Dal and the Samajwadi Party have condemned the Bharatiya Janata Party for issuing a demolition notice to the Mohammad Ali Jauhar University, citing alleged unauthorized construction.

The Rampur Development Authority has served a demolition notice to 38 out of 40 buildings at the university, prompting opposition from the Congress, which has called for the court to take suo motu cognizance of the matter.

Akhilesh Yadav, president of the Samajwadi Party, has accused the BJP of seeing communalism even in education and has questioned why the party has not taken action against its allies with illegal buildings.

data.headline: Provident Fund interest credited to all 34 crore accounts on July 15

bullets: The Indian government has approved an 8.25% interest rate for Provident Fund accounts for the financial year 2025-26.
The interest totaling over ₹1.44 lakh crore has been credited to all 34 crore Provident Fund accounts simultaneously on July 15.
The interest credited is a result of the implementation of the Centralised IT Enabled Services (CITES) project for updating the Employees Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) database.

data.headline: India's development did not come to standstill despite oil supply crisis: PM Modi

bullets: India's development continued uninterrupted despite the oil supply crisis, with nearly 99% of the Indian Railways network being electrified under Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government.
The electrification of the Indian Railways network, which was primarily reliant on diesel in 2014, has reduced the country's vulnerability to oil supply disruptions.
The hydrogen train launched by Prime Minister Modi in Haryana marks a significant step towards green mobility, a key aspect of the country's transition away from fossil fuels.

data.headline: Parliamentary panel on bill to remove PM, CMs defers adoption of report

bullets: The Joint Committee on the 130th Amendment Bill has decided to defer the adoption of its draft report containing five recommendations.
The committee's decision came after members realized that more discussions and consultations with stakeholders were essential, delaying the progress of the bill.
Implementation of the bill remains uncertain, as the parliamentary panel has put on hold the adoption of its draft report, requiring further voting and stakeholder consultations.

data.headline: HYDRAA fences 3.63 acres land in Hyderabad’s Banjara Hills, reclaims park sites in Hayathnagar and Boduppal

bullets: Hyderabad Disaster Response and Asset Protection Agency (HYDRAA) fenced 3.63 acres of government land worth over ₹600 crore in Banjara Hills and reclaimed 1,800 square yards of encroached park land in Ranga Reddy and Medchal-Malkajgiri districts to prevent fresh encroachments.
The land protection operations by HYDRAA resulted in the securing of government land valued at over ₹600 crore, and the agency fenced all the reclaimed properties to prevent further encroachments.

HYDRAA carried out the land protection operations across Hyderabad on July 16, 2026, securing government land and reclaiming encroached park land in Ranga Reddy and Medchal-Malkajgiri districts following complaints from residents and local committees through its Prajavani platform.

data.headline: Sonam Wangchuk loses over 9 kg, weakens significantly on 19th day of hunger strike: CJP

bullets: Sonam Wangchuk, an Indian activist, has lost over 9 kg of weight and weakened significantly after 19 days of his hunger strike, prompting constant medical supervision.

The medical assessment on the 19th day of his fast revealed a weight decline to 56.90 kg, with vital signs including a blood pressure of 101/65 mmHg, pulse of 72 beats per minute, oxygen saturation of 98%, and random blood sugar of 89 mg/dL.

The Delhi High Court has directed daily medical monitoring of Sonam Wangchuk during his indefinite hunger strike, amid demands for the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over alleged examination irregularities and NEET paper leak.

data.headline: Cabinet approves  ₹1.27 trillion for Semiconductor Mission 2.0: Here's what's new

bullets: The Indian Union Cabinet has approved ₹1.27 lakh crore for the second edition of the India Semiconductor Mission to incentivize raw material suppliers in the chip manufacturing sector.

The implementation of the ₹1.27 trillion Semiconductor Mission 2.0 aims to make India self-reliant in producing indigenous chips by the end of the program, with a focus on design, development, and production.

The new scheme is expected to attract investment from other chip segments to meet chip requirements for artificial intelligence devices, timing in with the global chip shortage and the need for increased production capacity.

data.headline: Mandatory training for staff to make hospitals patient-friendly

bullets: The Kerala Health Minister has made soft skills training mandatory for hospital employees, excluding doctors, to improve patient-friendliness and communication in public hospitals.
The training program will cover over 1600 employees across various hospital types, with a focus on improving interactions with patients and the public.
The education and training initiative is expected to commence shortly, with the Principal Secretary (Health) overseeing the implementation and follow-through of the policy decision.

data.headline: Jantar Mantar protest LIVE: Opposition support grows as Wangchuk’s hunger strike enters day 20

bullets: The Delhi High Court has agreed to hear a public interest litigation against the alleged "intrusive" monitoring of Sonam Wangchuk's health during his indefinite hunger strike.
The PIL aims to address concerns over Wangchuk's health and safety amid warnings from doctors that his prolonged fast has reached a critical stage.

The court will hear the case on Monday, July 20, 2026, as opposition support for Wangchuk's cause continues to grow, with notable figures such as Congress MP Pawan Khera visiting him at Jantar Mantar.

data.headline: Govt. to launch bullet rail project with Indian train; Japan to provide next-gen Shinkansen series after 4 years

bullets: The Indian government has announced plans to launch a bullet rail project in collaboration with Japan, utilizing the country's next-generation Shinkansen series.
The project is expected to span over four years, during which Japan will provide the E10 series Shinkansen trains to India.
The construction work for the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail project is reportedly progressing well, with the first section scheduled to be opened in 2027.

data.headline: HC grants interim bail to Sub-Registrar Justin Manikandan Subramanian in the Palani math fraudulent land registration case

bullets: The Madras High Court granted interim bail to Sub-Registrar Justin Manikandan Subramanian in the Palani math fraudulent land registration case until August 4.
The court imposed conditions on the bail, requiring the petitioner to report daily to the CB-CID from July 27 to August 3, except Sundays, and cooperate in the investigation.

The bail was granted to balance the interests of the investigation and the liberty of the petitioner, considering that the substantial part of the registration process had already been completed by the then Sub-Registrar.

data.headline: A trade deal that tests India’s competitive confidence

bullets: The Indian government has agreed to a trade deal with the United States, potentially liberalizing tariffs on $31 billion worth of US goods and opening up the Indian market to American companies.
The deal aims to increase bilateral trade by 25% within two years, with the US currently accounting for just 2% of India's global trade.

The agreement is set to be ratified by the Indian Parliament and is expected to face opposition from domestic industries that fear they will be harmed by increased competition from cheaper American imports.

data.headline: Government working on FTA utilisation plan to maximise benefits for businesses

bullets: The government has initiated a Free Trade Agreement (FTA) utilization plan to increase benefits for local businesses by optimizing their trade activities with partner countries.
The plan aims to achieve a 20% increase in exports to FTA partner countries within the next two years and reduce trade barriers by 30% through strategic negotiations.

Implementation of the FTA utilization plan is expected to commence in the first quarter of the upcoming fiscal year, with regular progress assessments and reviews to ensure timely achievement of set targets.

data.headline: Factional equations, community balance shape Congress’ deputy mayor choice in Kochi

bullets: The post of deputy mayor in Kochi has remained vacant since May 13, 2026, following the resignation of Deepak Joy to take up his MLA position.

The opposition Left Democratic Front has criticized the delay in filling the deputy mayor position, which also chairs the finance standing committee of the Corporation, with the Congress party's leadership being divided into factions.

The Congress party's 'A' group is pushing for their candidate to fill the deputy mayor position for the remainder of the term, while the 'I' faction is supporting K.V.P. Krishnakumar, who has been chairing meetings in the absence of a deputy mayor.

data.headline: AAP slams Delhi Police for shifting Wangchuk to hospital, using force on protesters

bullets: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) has criticized Delhi Police for shifting activist Sonam Wangchuk to a hospital from Jantar Mantar, alleging use of force against protesters.
The AAP claimed that the police action was taken ahead of Wangchuk's proposed march to Parliament on July 20, with 21 days of indefinite hunger strike.
AAP MP Sanjay Singh has appealed to the youth to continue supporting Wangchuk's agitation, with options to subscribe to premium content on the topic.

data.headline: India eyes UAE ports to skirt Hormuz risks for energy cargoes

bullets: India has decided to reroute a significant portion of its oil and liquefied gas imports from the Strait of Hormuz through the United Arab Emirates' Fujairah and Khor Fakkan ports to mitigate risks associated with the ongoing war in West Asia.

Approximately 60% of India's crude oil imports, 54% of liquefied natural gas imports, and 90% of cooking gas or liquefied petroleum gas imports were previously sourced from West Asia and routed through the Strait of Hormuz.

Indian refiners are utilizing the UAE's Habshan-Fujairah strategic oil pipeline, a 406km bypass of the Strait of Hormuz, and relying on alternative ports in Fujairah and Khor Fakkan as a lifeline to ensure a steady supply of energy supplies from the region.

data.headline: Sonam Wangchuk hunger strike LIVE: Wangchuk refuses medical intervention at hospital; Dipke holds indefinite hunger strike at Jantar Mantar

bullets: Sonam Wangchuk, a climate activist, has been hospitalized after 21 days of a hunger strike, with his supporter Abhijeet Dipke announcing an indefinite hunger strike in solidarity.

The hunger strikes have sparked a high-profile protest with Abhijeet Dipke demonstrating at Jantar Mantar and Sonam Wangchuk at a hospital in New Delhi, with both events garnering significant media attention.

The protests, which aim to draw attention to environmental and social issues, are expected to continue with Abhijeet Dipke refusing medical intervention and Dipke's indefinite hunger strike entering its initial stages.

data.headline: U.S. lawmaker urges Congress to review arms sales to India

bullets: A US lawmaker has called for Congress to review India's eligibility for US arms sales due to alleged transnational repression.
The review is expected to impact the scale of US arms sales to India, which could range from billions of dollars to potentially no sales at all.
The US lawmaker has urged the Secretary of State to undertake the review under the Arms Export Control Act, with a possible timeline for implementation pending Congressional approval.

data.headline: Chennai hospital gets non-invasive ventilator, pulse oximeters

bullets: A Chennai hospital has received a donation of essential tools, including a non-invasive ventilator and pulse oximeters, to strengthen its Pediatric Intensive Care Unit.
The donation, valued under the text, is part of enGen Global's Corporate Social Responsibility program, aimed at enhancing healthcare capabilities in the region.

The tools, donated on July 18, 2026, will enable the hospital to provide more advanced and timely care to its young patients, particularly in respiratory support and continuous oxygen saturation monitoring.

data.headline: Will join NC protest if Article 370 restoration, lifting ban on Jamaat added to agenda: PDP

bullets: The Peoples Democratic Party has set conditions for joining the National Conference's Delhi protest, seeking the restoration of Jammu and Kashmir's statehood, release of political prisoners, and lifting the ban on Jamaat-e-Islami.
The conditions include the restoration of Article 370, a demand not initially included in the National Conference's protest agenda, and would require significant changes to the existing protest plan.
PDP president Mehbooba Mufti announced these conditions on July 18, 2026, ahead of the National Conference's protest scheduled for July 20, 2026.

data.headline: India’s first private orbital rocket Vikram-1 set for lift-off

bullets: India's first private orbital rocket, Vikram-1, is set to launch from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre on July 18, marking a historic moment for the country's space program.
The Vikram-1 rocket will cover 14 phases during its 15.46-minute flight sequence, including lift-off and orbit injection, marking a significant milestone in India's space exploration journey.

Developed by private space launch company Skyroot Aerospace, Vikram-1 is a seven-storey-tall, multi-stage orbital launch vehicle built with an all-carbon composite structure and powered by in-house developed propulsion systems.

data.headline: Maharaja’s College governing council members nominated

bullets: The Kerala State government has nominated members to the governing council of Maharaja's College in Ernakulam, including a former judge and educationist, to oversee the college's administration.
A total of 10 members, including the Principal and nominees from Mahatma Gandhi University, are expected to be part of the reconstituted governing council.

The Director of Collegiate Education has been given the authority to reconstitute the governing council with the newly nominated members, with an administrative assistant serving as the staff representative.

data.headline: Amit Shah inspects indigenous border security technology in West Bengal

bullets: Union Home Minister Amit Shah inspected indigenous border security technology in West Bengal to bolster border security and strengthen defense systems.

Amit Shah's visit aims to review the operational preparedness of border security technologies, including Intruder Warning Systems and Radio-based Fence Intrusion Detection Systems, installed along the borders.

As part of his three-day visit, the Union Home Minister will continue reviewing these security measures with the 18th Battalion of the BSF's North Bengal Frontier until the end of his visit on July 19, 2026.

data.headline: Those who endanger safety of daughters or traders belong only in jail or hell: Yogi Adityanath

bullets: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath inaugurated 57 development projects worth ₹574 crore in Bulandshahr.
These projects aim to bring positive change to the region, which was previously plagued by fear, terror, and insecurity, causing many families to stop sending their daughters to school.

The development projects are expected to improve the safety and security of daughters and traders, and the government aims to ensure that justice is served to the underprivileged and women are protected from insecurity.

data.headline: U.S. imposing 25% tariff on some Brazilian imports starting July 22, citing unfair trade practices

bullets: The United States has announced a new trade policy, imposing a 25% tariff on certain Brazilian imports, effective July 22.
The tariffs are expected to affect approximately $4 billion worth of Brazilian imports annually, impacting a range of industries including agriculture and manufacturing.

The U.S. Trade Representative's office has stated that the tariffs are a result of ongoing trade disputes and investigations into Brazil's unfair trade practices, including the use of export subsidies and other trade barriers.

data.headline: NTPC-NPCIL JV floats  ₹28,000 crore tender for nuclear power plant in Rajasthan

bullets: The Indian government has invited bids for a ₹28,000-crore contract to build the nuclear island of the proposed 4x700 MW Mahi Banswara project in Rajasthan.
The tender, the largest of its kind under India's indigenous pressurized heavy water reactor programme, aims to rapidly scale up the country's nuclear capacity by 4,280 MW.

The Nuclear Island EPC package, floated by Anushakti Vidhyut Nigam Ltd, a joint venture between NTPC and NPCIL, is to be completed under the government's plan to open up the nuclear power sector for private firms, starting with the Mahi Banswara project in Rajasthan.

data.headline: Domestic tourism powering travel boom, but foreign visitor spending flat, says apex tourism body

bullets: India's domestic tourism spending has outpaced international visitor spending since 2019, with a 37% rise to ₹17.7 trillion ($202.5 billion) compared to a flat ₹2.9 trillion ($32.9 billion) in international visitor spending.

International visitor spending in India is expected to increase by only 15.3% to ₹3.3 trillion ($37.9 billion) in 2026 compared to 2019 levels, while the rupee has devalued by approximately 26.92% against the US dollar from 2019 to July 2026.
The World Travel & Tourism Council calls for stronger collaboration between the government and private sector to boost inbound tourism and help India capture a fair share of international spend.

data.headline: Jammu and Kashmir rains LIVE: Amarnath Yatra suspended as J&K braces for heavy rain

bullets: The Amarnath Yatra has been temporarily suspended from both Pahalgam and Baltal routes in Jammu and Kashmir due to adverse weather conditions and forecast of widespread rainfall.
At least four people have died and several are missing following flash floods and landslides triggered by heavy rains in Poonch district of Jammu and Kashmir.

Jammu and Kashmir authorities have suspended the Amarnath pilgrimage on July 19, 2026, as the region braces for heavy rain and flash floods with multiple fatalities and missing persons reported in Poonch district.

data.headline: How will U.S. visa policy changes affect students, media professionals, and exchange visitors | Explained

bullets: The U.S. Department of Homeland Security has introduced amended immigration rules for F, J, and I category visa holders citing national security risks.

The new rules will limit the stay for PhD students to four years and introduce a fixed period of admission for non-immigrant students and exchange visitors, who will be allowed to stay for the length of their specific programs.

The new order is expected to impact the knowledge sector, with a four-year timeline for implementation and an immediate end to the "Duration of Status loophole" allowing foreign students, exchange visitors, and media representatives to remain in the U.S. indefinitely.

data.headline: Sonam Wangchuk calls July 20 Parliament march India's 'second freedom movement'

bullets: Activist Sonam Wangchuk called the proposed July 20 Parliament march India's second freedom movement, urging supporters to make the mobilisation a success.
The movement aims to achieve "freedom from injustice" linked to alleged paper leaks and "freedom from fear" related to Mr. Wangchuk's alleged illegal detention.
Sonam Wangchuk's handwritten note, shared from Safdarjung Hospital through his wife, was posted on his X account and called for a march to the Parliament on July 20.

data.headline: Delimitation not just an INDIA bloc issue, concerns our Constitutional framework’ says Congress’ K.C. Venugopal

bullets: The Indian National Congress opposes the proposed Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill on delimitation, citing concerns that it undermines federalism and democratic representation.

The Congress party has not specified a particular opposition to the amendment's fiscal implications, but has expressed concerns about the bill's impact on India's democratic and constitutional framework.
The party's general secretary, K.C. Venugopal, made these comments ahead of the Monsoon Session of Parliament in July 2026, as part of an interview with The Hindu newspaper.

data.headline: RBI governor Malhotra flags West Asia, weak monsoon as biggest risks to Indian economy

bullets: The Reserve Bank of India has identified geopolitical tensions in West Asia and uneven southwest monsoon rainfall as the biggest risks to India's economy.
The RBI expects India's economic growth to slow down to around 6.6% in the April-June quarter from 7.8% in the previous quarter, with full-year growth also forecast to be around 6.6%.

Reserve Bank of India governor Sanjay Malhotra defended the rupee's performance despite a stronger dollar, citing services exports, remittances, and foreign direct investment as external-sector buffers.

data.headline: The week in charts: Inflation heat, export shift, tracking services production

bullets: Retail inflation in India rose to 4.4% in June, exceeding the Reserve Bank of India's medium-term target of 4% for the first time since January 2025, driven by higher food and fuel prices.
Food inflation surged to 5.3% in June, with ginger recording a 50.4% rise and garlic experiencing a 17.9% increase in price, after facing deflation at the beginning of the year.
India's inflation is expected to remain elevated due to weather-related risks and renewed tensions in West Asia, with the statistics ministry to continue monitoring the situation.

data.headline: Jantar Mantar protest LIVE: Wangchuk will end fast if Parliament session focuses on education accountability, says Gitanjali Angmo

bullets: The Indian government has no plan to intervene in the ongoing protest by Sonam Wangchuk at Jantar Mantar, with Delhi Police stating that no permission was sought or granted for the protest march.

Thousands of protesters gathered at Jantar Mantar on July 19, 2026, with 20,000 people reportedly in attendance, as they demanded the resignation of the Union Education Minister over alleged examination irregularities and the NEET paper leak.
The Delhi Police have Section 144 in effect in the New Delhi district, and the Monsoon Session of Parliament is set to begin on Monday, July 20, 2026.

data.headline: At least 11 killed, 10 missing as heavy rain triggers flash floods in J&K

bullets: Heavy rain triggers flash floods in Jammu and Kashmir's Poonch and Rajouri districts, resulting in the deaths of 11 people and 10 missing individuals.
The initial assessment indicates that over 100 houses and approximately two dozen school structures were damaged in the floods.
The Jammu and Kashmir government, under the guidance of Chief Minister Omar Abdullah, convened an emergency review meeting to monitor vulnerable areas and implement disaster relief measures.

data.headline: Will end fast if education accountability issue raised in Parliament Monsoon Session: Wife Gitanjali conveys Wangchuk’s message

bullets: Activist Sonam Wangchuk will end his indefinite hunger strike if education accountability is committed to be raised in Parliament during the Monsoon Session.
Several leaders and parties will need to be approached to meet the conditions for ending the strike, with a total of 2 key demands being education accountability and prevention of NEET paper leak.

The proposed meeting between political leaders and Sonam Wangchuk is scheduled to take place at Safdarjung Hospital, with plans to commence on July 19, 2026, following the start of the Monsoon Session of Parliament.

data.headline: Maturing approach: On the India-U.K. Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement - The Hindu

bullets: The India-U.K. Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) reflects a more mature approach to free trade negotiations, balancing liberalisation with domestic sensitivities in an increasingly fragmented global trading system.

The pact offers zero-duty access on 99% of India's exports, covering almost the entire value of bilateral trade, but may place competitive pressure on already cost-disadvantaged MSMEs due to stringent U.K. standards.

Implementation of the CETA is expected to be challenging for Indian MSMEs due to their lack of documentation and compliance capacity, requiring India to strengthen regulatory administration and provide support to ensure the deal's benefits are maximised.

data.headline: India bans the import of goods made using forced labour, even as U.S. investigation is pending

bullets: India has prohibited the import of goods manufactured using forced labor, effective immediately, in order to combat human trafficking and protect workers' rights.
Over 800 types of goods, including cotton, rubber, and coal, worth approximately $40 billion, are at risk of being blocked from entering the Indian market due to suspected forced labor.

The new regulations will be enforced by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade, which will require importers to provide proof that goods were made without the use of forced labor, with compliance expected to be in place by the end of 2023.

data.headline: PLI success prompts Centre to explore next phase for food processing sector

bullets: The Centre is reviewing the success of the PLI scheme for the food processing sector to explore a new incentive framework by 31 March 2027.

Discussions with industry stakeholders and PLI beneficiaries have identified segments requiring additional policy support, including plant-based proteins, nutrition products, and technologies to reduce food wastage.
The government has begun consultations with industry to assess the performance of the PLI scheme, drawing lessons from its six-year implementation to inform the contours of a successor programme.

data.headline: ₹10 and  ₹20 notes may be the first polymer currency as RBI's printing arm invites global bids: Report

bullets: The Reserve Bank of India's currency printing arm has invited global bids for manufacturers to supply polymer substrate sheets for printing Indian banknotes.
Approximately 68,000 reams of biaxially oriented polypropylene-based substrate are required, split across two denominations, with each ream consisting of 500 sheets.

Interested companies have until August 18, 2026 to submit their bids, with the initial polymer notes, likely in ₹10 and ₹20 denominations, potentially being introduced following successful field trials.

data.headline: As BSF mulls 90-km Sundarbans fence, security clashes with ecology

bullets: The Border Security Force (BSF) is conducting a feasibility study for a 90-km fence along the Sundarbans mangrove forests in the Indo-Bangladesh border to deter infiltration.
The BSF plans to install physical fences in a region that spans 90 kilometers, posing significant logistical challenges due to its thick mangrove forests, creeks, and swamps.

The BSF will expedite work on the project in collaboration with other government departments, following a recent feasibility study and the sanctioning of construction funds for the massive undertaking.

data.headline: Monsoon session of Parliament LIVE: Lok Sabha adjourns briefly; new members take oath in Rajya Sabha

bullets: The Centre will initiate the Monsoon Session of Parliament on July 20, 2026, by proposing several bills, including the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026.

Four bills are scheduled to be introduced during the Monsoon Session: the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026; the Income Tax (Amendment) Bill, 2026; the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026; and the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026.
The Monsoon Session will convene amidst a CJP protest in Delhi, which is expected to take place at Jantar Mantar on July 20, 2026.

data.headline: 'Dr. Doom' Nouriel Roubini predicts 10% economic growth by 2050—but says AI will replace many jobs

bullets: Economist Nouriel Roubini predicts a future with 10% economic growth by 2050, driven by advancements in artificial intelligence.
Roubini projects that AI and robotics could replace a significant 2-3 decade share of the workforce, exacerbating the depletion of Social Security trust funds.
Governments will eventually need to rethink income distribution in the face of widespread AI adoption, potentially implementing universal basic income to mitigate the impact of job displacement.

data.headline: Tamil Nadu Today: Supreme Court rejects DMK’s plea against TVK leaders over Karur stampede

bullets: The Supreme Court rejected a plea by the DMK to restrain TVK leaders from making public statements linking the party with the Karur stampede.
The court dismissed the plea, stating that an injunction on the TVK leaders' remarks may amount to an infringement on their free speech rights.
The Supreme Court, through its July 7, 2026, ruling, advised the DMK to counter the TVK leaders' statements with "more speech" rather than seeking a judicial gag.

data.headline: Yellow alert for two districts on July 21

bullets: The India Meteorological Department has issued a yellow alert for Kasaragod and Kannur districts on Tuesday due to expected moderate heavy rain.
Approximately 4 days of moderate heavy rain are forecasted for north and central Kerala under the influence of an upper cyclonic circulation.

The IMD has upgraded the alert for Kannur and Kasaragod districts on Monday from yellow to orange, warning of intense heavy rainfall, and an upper air cyclonic circulation lies over the West Central Bay of Bengal and adjoining coastal Andhra Pradesh.

data.headline: Kozhikode DIET launches ‘IntelliTrait’ to mentor schoolchildren

bullets: The Kozhikode District Institute of Education and Training has launched a training programme titled 'IntelliTrait' to develop and promote entrepreneurial skills and job orientation among schoolchildren.
The programme will be implemented in 17 higher secondary schools and 17 high schools in the district in the first phase and is expected to reach a total of 34 schools across the district.

The project, expected to be implemented in two phases, utilizes an AI-assisted platform based on established theories of multiple intelligences, natures, and emotional intelligence to scientifically evaluate students' thought processes, learning methods, problem-solving skills, and emotional maturity.

data.headline: No new diarrhoea cases reported in Giripuram, officials confirm

bullets: Health authorities in Vijayawada reported no new diarrhoea cases in Giripuram on July 19-20, following a rise in cases from July 16-18.
The total number of reported diarrhoea cases in Giripuram between July 16-18 was 13, with four patients admitted to the hospital and one discharged.
Medical camps set up in response to the diarrhoea outbreak will be removed from July 21, as officials confirmed that the situation is under control despite misinformation circulating on social media.

data.headline: Best performing students urged to become role models at Shining Stars award event

bullets: The Andhra Pradesh State government has launched the Shining Stars Awards program to recognize and encourage students who excel in their examinations.
Over 500 students received awards and certificates at the inaugural event of the program, with the State government allocating a budget to support the initiative.

The program aims to provide a platform for students to showcase their talents and inspire others to achieve academic excellence, with the State government planning to expand the program to cover more students in the coming years.

data.headline: One hotel ordered to shut, two eateries fined in food safety inspection in Ernakulam

bullets: The Ernakulam district administration has ordered the closure of one hotel and fined two eateries a total of ₹6,000 for food safety violations during a joint inspection.

The food safety inspection covered eight establishments in the Kaloor and Kadavanthra areas of Ernakulam, with drinking water samples collected from six establishments without water quality test reports.

The surprise inspection drive will continue in the coming days, with officials from the District Health department, the Food Safety wing, the Kochi Corporation Health department, and the police conducting joint checks at hotels, street-side stalls, and roadside eateries.

data.headline: Accommodating dissent: On the TVK government’s actions - The Hindu

bullets: The TVK government in Tamil Nadu has been criticized for its handling of dissent, with at least 10 people arrested or facing police action for speaking out against the Chief Minister or his cabinet colleagues.
Over 10 individuals have been subject to police action in the first couple of months of the TVK government, with cases ranging from arrest to police searches and filing of charges.

The TVK government's actions have raised concerns about authoritarianism and the normalization of using police and criminal law to silence critics, potentially undermining democratic principles in Tamil Nadu.

data.headline: Govt eases battery PLI norms to attract more storage players; subsidies lowered

bullets: The government has eased battery production-linked incentive (PLI) norms to attract more storage players by shifting policy priorities and lowering subsidies per kilowatt-hour.

The new 10 GWh tender under the ₹18,100-crore PLI scheme for advanced chemistry cells (ACC) has easier entry requirements and focuses on battery efficiency, marking a significant shift from the 2021 version.
Bids for the new tender will be accepted until 13 October, with a pre-bid conference scheduled on 29 July and bids to be opened on 14 October.

data.headline: SIR: Voters above 85 years face double checks, say BLOs

bullets: Booth Level Officers in Karnataka have been instructed to double verify voters aged 85 years and above and place them under the "probable absent, shifted, dead/deleted or duplicate (ASDD)" category.
Multiple Booth Level Officers reported that around 20 lakh voters in Karnataka fall under this category, which is approximately 10% of the total voters in the state.

The instruction to flag voters above 85 for ASDD verification is reportedly being carried out as part of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in Karnataka, with Chief Electoral Officer V. Anbu Kumar denying any such instructions had been issued.

data.headline: Tunnel collapses in Sikkim’s Namchi; 8 workers killed, rescue ops under way
